Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2041210], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1290201], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2041220], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1290203], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [87], Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-00087]

Title: Pardons and Criminal Records
Definition: This category concerns issues around how a pardon (when a crime is officially forgiven and the offender is absolved of legal consequences) affects it has on one's criminal record.
Parent Terms: Criminal Records [CR-06-00-00-00], Pardon for a crime [CR-02-01-00-00]

Title: Juvenile Criminal Records
Definition: This category covers how records of criminal activity when a person was still a juvenile (not an adult) may be accessed, sealed, or kept confidential.
Parent Terms: Criminal Records [CR-06-00-00-00], Juvenile Justice [CR-10-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1490500], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1490504]

Title: Accessing a juvenile criminal record
Definition: This category covers how a person can access their own juvenile criminal record, or how others can access it.
Parent Terms: Juvenile Criminal Records [CR-06-03-00-00]

Title: Confidentiality of juvenile criminal records
Definition: This category covers the rules about whether juvenile criminal records are protected as confidential or not.
Parent Terms: Juvenile Criminal Records [CR-06-03-00-00]

Title: Expungement of juvenile criminal record
Definition: This category covers how a person can get their juvenile criminal record expunged, cleaned, or sealed.
Parent Terms: Juvenile Criminal Records [CR-06-03-00-00], Expungement or Sealing of Criminal Record [CR-06-01-00-00]

Title: Death Penalty
Definition: This category concerns the options, rights, and procedure of those facing the death penalty. It includes issues around understanding the local laws on death penalty, seeking clemency, problems with legal counsel representation, selection of juries, prosecutor's conduct, presentation of scientific evidence, showing competency or mental retardation, and other issues.
Parent Terms: Crime and Prisons [CR-00-00-00-00]

Title: Going to criminal court and being on trial
Definition: This category covers the specifics of the court process for those facing criminal charges. This includes how to defend oneself, how to get an attorney, how to deal with witnesses and evidence, and how to raise witnesses.
Parent Terms: Crime and Prisons [CR-00-00-00-00], Going to court and dealing with procedure [CO-07-00-00-00]

Title: Appealing criminal court's decision
Definition: This category covers how a criminal defendant may appeal the court's decision, and what the court procedure is for appeals.
Parent Terms: Going to criminal court and being on trial [CR-08-00-00-00], After being found guilty of a crime [CR-02-00-00-00], Appealing a court's judgment [CO-07-02-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2040300], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2040399]

Title: Courts of appeal
Definition: This category covers the court procedure of appealing a criminal court's decision, including which court of appeals or intermediate appellate court a defendant can take their appeal to.
Parent Terms: Appealing criminal court's decision [CR-08-01-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2040320], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2040330]

Title: Preservation of error in a criminal case to have appeal
Definition: This category covers the options of a defendant in a criminal court to preserve an error, by raising them during litigation and trial so they could later raise them for review in an appeal to an appellate court. It also covers what happens if this process has not been done correctly, and if the appellate court says the opportunity to appeal has been waived.
Parent Terms: Appealing criminal court's decision [CR-08-01-00-00]

Title: Collateral appeal to court after conviction
Definition: This category covers options for a defendant to make a 'collateral appeal' (rather than a direct appeal) after being convicted, to challenge their imprisonment or the guilty verdict. This could be through a petition for habeas corpus, a position for a new trial, a motion to void correct sentence, or claim ineffective assistance of counsel.
Parent Terms: Appealing criminal court's decision [CR-08-01-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2041800], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2041899]

Title: Appealing based on ineffective assistance of counsel
Definition: This category covers how a criminal defendant can appeal their verdict by claiming that their defense lawyer did not correctly and fully represent them at trial, by claiming ineffective assistance of counsel in an appeal. This could be through a collateral review process.
Parent Terms: Appealing criminal court's decision [CR-08-01-00-00], Having a lawyer in a criminal case [CR-04-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2041810], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2040900]

Title: Criminal trial process
Definition: This category covers how criminal trials proceed, some of the issues and technical/procedural key stages, and how a defendant can protect their rights or victims and their families may be able to participate.
Parent Terms: Going to criminal court and being on trial [CR-08-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2041600], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2041699]

Title: Criminal trial jury selection
Definition: This category covers how a jury can be selected in a criminal trial, and what challenges or issues may arise.
Parent Terms: Criminal trial process [CR-08-02-00-00]

Title: Jury instructions in a criminal trial
Definition: This category covers what instructions are given to jurors in a criminal jury trial, that lets them know what they should be paying attention to and how they should make their decision.
Parent Terms: Criminal trial process [CR-08-02-00-00]

Title: Lawyers' arguments and behavior during criminal trial
Definition: This category covers issues about how lawyers behave during a criminal trial, including for the prosecution and defense. This covers issues about their conduct or problems with it, and what they can include in their arguments.
Parent Terms: Criminal trial process [CR-08-02-00-00], Ethical rules for lawyer's behavior [CO-09-05-00-00]

Title: Evidence at a criminal trial
Definition: This category covers what kind of evidence can be brought into a criminal trial, how it can be challenged, and what it can be used for.
Parent Terms: Going to criminal court and being on trial [CR-08-00-00-00], Evidence for a court case [CO-05-00-00-00]

Title: Forensic evidence about a crime
Definition: This category covers what kinds of forensic evidence can be brought into a criminal trial, including ballistics, blood tests, DNA tests, and other tests from scientific methods that can show guilt or innocence.
Parent Terms: Evidence at a criminal trial [CR-08-03-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2042610], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2042619]

Title: Ballistics evidence
Definition: This category covers how ballistic evidence can be brought into a criminal trial to analyze how weapons have been used and what that means for a person's guilt or innocence.
Parent Terms: Forensic evidence about a crime [CR-08-03-01-00]

Title: Fingerprint and impression evidence
Definition: This category covers what kinds of fingerprint or other impression evidence can be brought into a criminal trial to prove a defendant's guilt or innocence.
Parent Terms: Forensic evidence about a crime [CR-08-03-01-00]

Title: Blood and body fluid evidence
Definition: This category covers serology evidence, about blood or other body fluids, used at a criminal trial to show guilt or innocence of a criminal defendant.
Parent Terms: Forensic evidence about a crime [CR-08-03-01-00]

Title: Hair and fiber evidence
Definition: This category covers how evidence about hair and fiber may be brought into a criminal trial to prove a person's guilt or innocence.
Parent Terms: Forensic evidence about a crime [CR-08-03-01-00]

Title: Expert testimony at a criminal trial
Definition: This category covers how experts may be brought into a criminal trial to discuss evidence or opinions about the defendant's guilt or innocence.
Parent Terms: Evidence at a criminal trial [CR-08-03-00-00]

Title: Genetic evidence at a criminal trial
Definition: This category covers what kind of genetic evidence can be brought into a criminal trial to show a defendant's guilt or innocence. This includes DNA evidence.
Parent Terms: Evidence at a criminal trial [CR-08-03-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2042620], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2042629], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2042622]

Title: DNA evidence at a criminal trial
Definition: This category covers how DNA evidence might be brought into a criminal trial to prove a defendant's guilt or innocence.
Parent Terms: Genetic evidence at a criminal trial [CR-08-03-04-00]

Title: Challenging genetic evidence as junk science
Definition: This category covers how evidence at a criminal trial can be challenged as junk science.
Parent Terms: Genetic evidence at a criminal trial [CR-08-03-04-00]

Title: Right to challenge witnesses
Definition: This category covers criminal defendants' rights under the US Constitution's Confrontation Clause to challenge the prosecution's witnesses and to dispute their testimony.
Parent Terms: Going to criminal court and being on trial [CR-08-00-00-00]

Title: Defenses against criminal charges
Definition: This category covers what defenses a person can raise when they are charged with a crime and on trial.
Parent Terms: Going to criminal court and being on trial [CR-08-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2040200], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2040600], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2040699]

Title: Criminal defense around lack of capacity or insanity
Definition: This category covers a possible criminal defense of saying the defendant lacked capacity or sanity, and so cannot be guilty.
Parent Terms: Defenses against criminal charges [CR-08-05-00-00]

Title: Self-defense as a criminal defense
Definition: This category covers how a criminal defendant may defend themselves at trial by claiming self-defense as the reason they violated the law.
Parent Terms: Defenses against criminal charges [CR-08-05-00-00]

Title: Grand Juries and being indicted for a crime
Definition: This category covers how a grand jury works to formally charge a person with committing a crime, as an indictment. This covers how grand juries work, what is allowed in a grand jury hearing, how to challenge their fairness, and how private or public they are.
Parent Terms: Going to criminal court and being on trial [CR-08-00-00-00], Being investigated for a crime [CR-16-00-00-00]

Title: Make motion for a new trial
Definition: This category covers how a person on trial for a crime can make a motion to ask for a new trial, based on some problem that has happened during the current one.
Parent Terms: Going to criminal court and being on trial [CR-08-00-00-00]

Title: Requesting a jury for a criminal trial
Definition: This category covers how and when a criminal defendant can request to have a jury trial rather than bench trial, and what this choice means. It also covers the defendant's right to have a jury trial.
Parent Terms: Going to criminal court and being on trial [CR-08-00-00-00]

Title: Sentencing and penalties after being found guilty
Definition: This category covers how a person may be sentenced to jail, fines, and other penalties after having been found guilty at a criminal trial. It covers how the sentence is decided on, and how the defendant may try to challenge it.
Parent Terms: Going to criminal court and being on trial [CR-08-00-00-00], After being found guilty of a crime [CR-02-00-00-00]

Title: Due Process rights in a criminal case
Definition: This category covers rights and options that a person has when facing criminal charges, in terms of what is required to allow them to have a fair trial with sufficient procedure that they can make their case and defend their rights.
Parent Terms: Crime and Prisons [CR-00-00-00-00], Due Process rights when dealing with the government [CO-07-10-00-00]

Title: Juvenile Justice
Definition: This category is about minors who are in criminal proceedings, or dealing with discipline in school, including getting advocates and support. It can cover issues of detention, special sentencing, standards of treatment, and the possibility of the death penalty. This might also be called juvenile delinquency.
Parent Terms: Family [FA-00-00-00-00], Crime and Prisons [CR-00-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2320900], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2320999], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [41], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [49]

Title: Challenging detention through Habeas Corpus
Definition: This category covers situations when a criminal suspect or defendant may raise a habeas corpus claim to challenge the validity of their detention. This could be before, during, or after a criminal trial. This covers how a person may file a writ of habeas corpus to challenge whether it's legal to detain a person, or whether a conviction is valid under the law.\n
Parent Terms: Appealing criminal court's decision [CR-08-01-00-00], Dealing with police and prosecutors [CR-12-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2040800], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2040899]

Title: Supporting a petition for habeas corpus
Definition: This category covers how one can support a suspect or defendant's petition for habeas corpus, to challenge if their detention is against the law.
Parent Terms: Challenging detention through Habeas Corpus [CR-11-00-00-00]

Title: Opposing a petition for habeas corpus
Definition: This category covers how one can oppose a suspect or defendant's petition for habeas corpus, to challenge if their detention is against the law.
Parent Terms: Challenging detention through Habeas Corpus [CR-11-00-00-00]

Title: Review of a habeas corpus petition
Definition: This category covers how a court will review a person's habeas corpus petition.
Parent Terms: Challenging detention through Habeas Corpus [CR-11-00-00-00]

Title: Dealing with police and prosecutors
Definition: This category covers issues and rights that a person may have when dealing with government agents like police and prosecutors -- particularly before a criminal trial. This includes what rights and protections a person has when interacting with the police, or being subject to searches or detention.
Parent Terms: Crime and Prisons [CR-00-00-00-00]

Title: Encounters with the police
Definition: This category covers what rights and options a person has when they interact with the police. This covers being stopped on foot, in a car, or other places. It also covers rights of someone who is a suspect or who is not.
Parent Terms: Dealing with police and prosecutors [CR-12-00-00-00], Being investigated for a crime [CR-16-00-00-00]

Title: Procedure for filing habeas corpus petition
Definition: This category covers how a person can file a petition for habeas corpus, challenging their detention or imprisonment.
Parent Terms: Challenging detention through Habeas Corpus [CR-11-00-00-00]

Title: Police or prosecutors' misconduct
Definition: This category covers situations in which a person believes the police or prosecutor has behaved incorrectly or unethically. This covers what options there are for challenging misconduct, what procedure may result, and what outcomes may happen.
Parent Terms: Dealing with police and prosecutors [CR-12-00-00-00], Ethical rules for lawyer's behavior [CO-09-05-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2042800], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2042899]

Title: Prosecutor failing to disclose evidence (Brady Violation)
Definition: This category covers situations in which a prosecutor or government agent fails to disclose evidence during a criminal proceeding, when that evidence could have materially favored the defendant. This is called a Brady violation, and it might be used to challenge the case and verdict by the defense.
Parent Terms: Dealing with police and prosecutors [CR-12-00-00-00]

Title: Misconduct cases against police or prosecutors
Definition: This category covers how a police officer or prosecutor may be investigated or sued for misconduct. This includes how a person may file a civil case against a police officer for misconduct.
Parent Terms: Police or prosecutors' misconduct [CR-12-06-00-00], Suing the government for civil rights violations [TO-04-07-00-00]

Title: Understanding Specific Types of Crimes
Definition: This category covers the types of crimes that a person might be accused of, including ones that are felonies or misdemeanors, substantive or not, or other types of crimes.
Parent Terms: Crime and Prisons [CR-00-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2041500], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2041503]

Title: Crimes against property
Definition: This category covers crimes that are against property (and not against a person). This could include burglary, vandalism, arson or theft in which a person's property is stolen or destroyed.
Parent Terms: Understanding Specific Types of Crimes [CR-13-00-00-00]

Title: Crimes against a person
Definition: This category covers the types of crime in which people are directly harmed, including murder, rape, or assault. This is as opposed to crimes against property in which the crime harms a person's relationship with their property.
Parent Terms: Understanding Specific Types of Crimes [CR-13-00-00-00]

Title: Reentry after prison
Definition: This category covers options and rules for people who have been prisoners, and are leaving prison to re-enter society. This concerns options for their work, housing, finances, education, and dealing with after-effects of the criminal justice system.
Parent Terms: Crime and Prisons [CR-00-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1832400], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1832499]

Title: Prisoners' rights, services, and conditions
Definition: This issue area is about situations that prisoners face, rights that they have, their security, rehabilitation, work and employment, health care, communications with the outside world, and other conditions.
Parent Terms: Crime and Prisons [CR-00-00-00-00]

Title: Being investigated for a crime
Definition: This category covers situations in which a person may be a suspect for a crime, before they have been charged or indicted with a crime.  This covers how police may try to gather evidence, get statements, find witnesses, and get identifications. This covers what protections and procedure a person can expect.
Parent Terms: Crime and Prisons [CR-00-00-00-00]

Title: Disaster Relief
Definition: This category covers issues related to natural disasters and public health emergencies, including people's rights, getting benefits and assistance, clearing title to property, and dealing with insurance.
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2051100], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2051199]

Title: Help for Farms after a Disaster
Definition: This category concerns issues and options that farmers have around a natural disaster or other emergency. This category covers assistance that might be available to them.
Parent Terms: Disaster Relief [DI-00-00-00-00], Running a farm business [BU-03-00-00-00]

Title: Public Benefits for individuals after a disaster
Definition: This category covers the financial and other benefits that a person might get after or during a disaster. It includes FEMA Benefits, housing help, local help, and other public assistance programs. It covers who is eligible for this help, how they access it, how to maintain it, or other issues that might arise.
Parent Terms: Disaster Relief [DI-00-00-00-00], Public Benefits [BE-00-00-00-00]

Title: Local Public Benefits to assist people after a disaster (not FEMA)
Definition: This category concerns how people who have been through a disaster can access local and state (not FEMA) public benefits programs for housing and other needs assistance. This includes grants or money to cover disaster-related expenses and needs.
Parent Terms: Public Benefits for individuals after a disaster [DI-02-00-00-00]

Title: FEMA 'Other Needs' assistance
Definition: This category covers how to access general funding assistance from FEMA's 'Other Needs' program, to get financial help to pay for medical and dental expenses, clothing, household items, school materials, public transport, car repair, moving and storage, cleaning property, or funeral expenses.
Parent Terms: Public Benefits for individuals after a disaster [DI-02-00-00-00]

Title: Appealing FEMA benefits decision
Definition: This category covers issues with appealing a decision made by FEMA, regarding a person's ability to get assistance after a disaster.
Parent Terms: Public Benefits for individuals after a disaster [DI-02-00-00-00]

Title: Unemployment assistance after a disaster
Definition: This category covers issues when someone loses employment because of a natural disaster. It covers how to apply for assistance, who is eligible, and how claims will be judged.
Parent Terms: Disaster Relief [DI-00-00-00-00], Unemployment Benefits, Compensation, and Insurance [BE-04-00-00-00]

Title: FEMA Buy-outs or Hazard Mitigation Grant Program
Definition: This category covers options for a person whose community may have gone through a natural disaster and then has the option for a FEMA Buy-out, or the Hazard Mitigation Grant Program (HMGP). It covers who is eligible and what the process is to go through this program.
Parent Terms: Public Benefits for individuals after a disaster [DI-02-00-00-00], Owning a Home [HO-09-00-00-00]

Title: Finding Missing Persons after a Disaster
Definition: This category is about options and assistance to find missing people after a natural disaster.
Parent Terms: Disaster Relief [DI-00-00-00-00]

Title: Insurance Claims after a disaster
Definition: This category concerns how individuals or groups can make home, property, medical, or other insurance claims after a disaster, to  get reimbursed. This includes how to file, determining your coverage, documenting issues, and managing disputes with insurance companies.
Parent Terms: Disaster Relief [DI-00-00-00-00], Insurance [MO-07-00-00-00]

Title: Rebuilding and Reconstruction after a disaster
Definition: This category concerns legal issues in rebuilding homes, business properties, and regional plans after a natural disaster. This includes dealing with building regulations and other utility and infrastructure issues. Issues  in this category include property buy-outs, beach access, insurance policies, and different governments' rules.
Parent Terms: Disaster Relief [DI-00-00-00-00], Environmental Justice [EN-00-00-00-00], Housing after a Disaster [HO-10-00-00-00]

Title: Replacing Lost Documents after a disaster
Definition: This category concerns issues with how to replace lost documents after a natural disaster has destroyed them. This may include identification documents, social security cards, birth certificates, marriage certificates, passports, title to property, or other important documents.
Parent Terms: Disaster Relief [DI-00-00-00-00], Getting information and records from the government [GO-02-00-00-00]

Title: Tax Relief after a disaster
Definition: This category covers what options a person or business might have after a disaster period, to have relief from paying certain taxes.
Parent Terms: Disaster Relief [DI-00-00-00-00], Taxes [MO-09-00-00-00]

Title: Deducting losses on damaged property after a natural disaser
Definition: This category covers issues on how a taxpayer can possibly deduct the damages and costs their property suffered during a natural disaster.
Parent Terms: Tax Relief after a disaster [DI-07-00-00-00]

Title: Public Health Emergency issues
Definition: This category concerns legal problems that might emerge during a public health emergency, like a pandemic or a quarantine (for example during the COVID-10 emergency). This includes unique problems that might arise when there are restrictions on leaving home, working, filing lawsuits, or using the court system; or when there are special protections for renters, workers, sick individuals, essential workers, vulnerable populations, or other people.
Parent Terms: Disaster Relief [DI-00-00-00-00], Health [HE-00-00-00-00]

Title: Family issues after a natural disaster
Definition: This category covers family law issues that may arise after a natural disaster, like problems around child visitation, making child support payments, destruction of marital home and property, and other issues.
Parent Terms: Disaster Relief [DI-00-00-00-00], Family [FA-00-00-00-00]

Title: Education
Definition:
This category covers issues around school, including accommodations for special needs, discrimination, student debt, discipline, and other issues in education.

Scenarios in this category include suspension/expulsion from school, truancy, safety, access to special education services, and denial of bilingual education.
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1190000], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1190099], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [19]

Title: Adult continuing education
Definition: This category covers issues that adults might face when seeking continuing education, including for those with disabilities, those seeking out new employment, or those having to fulfill education requirements for benefits programs.
Parent Terms: Education [ED-00-00-00-00]

Title: Vocational education
Definition: This category covers issues around vocational education, including requirements around receiving benefits or government support dependent on vocational educational and job training.
Parent Terms: Adult continuing education [ED-01-00-00-00], TANF work requirements and education or vocational training [BE-02-02-10-05]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1150000], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [15], Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-00015]

Title: Public Benefits offered through schools
Definition: This category covers the public benefits that children and families might receive, through the school system. It includes school lunch and breakfast programs, health benefits through Medicaid, and other programs that intend to offer key services to children and their families through the channel of a school. It also covers Head Start aid programs for low-income children.
Parent Terms: Education [ED-00-00-00-00]

Title: School breakfast and lunch programs
Definition: This category covers the national programs to provide free or reduced-price breakfast and lunch to children attending schools. It covers the eligibility requirements, what benefits it entitles students to, how to apply, and dealing with any issues that come up.
Parent Terms: Public Benefits offered through schools [ED-02-00-00-00], Food and Cash benefits [BE-02-00-00-00]

Title: Head Start services for families
Definition: This category covers students' and families' options around the Head Start Program from the US Department of Health and Human Services, that provides early childhood education, health, nutrition, and parenting services to low-income families and children. This covers who is eligible, how to apply, and how to receive services.
Parent Terms: Public Benefits offered through schools [ED-02-00-00-00]

Title: School clothing allowance program
Definition: This category covers if a family can apply for an allowance to pay for childrens's clothing fo school. It includes if this benefit is available, how to apply, how to use it, and who is eligible.
Parent Terms: Public Benefits offered through schools [ED-02-00-00-00]

Title: Paying for education
Definition: This category covers options, problems, and rights of people who are trying to pay for school, university, or other education programs. It includes issues around borrowing money, getting aid, covering fees, and other concerns.
Parent Terms: Money, Debt, and Consumer Issues [MO-00-00-00-00], Education [ED-00-00-00-00]

Title: Fees for educational programs
Definition: This category covers issues for students or their families regarding covering fees at their school
Parent Terms: Paying for education [ED-03-00-00-00]

Title: Vouchers to pay for private education
Definition: This category covers situations in which a family wants to get vouchers from the government to cover the costs of tuition at private schools. Not all states offer school vouchers. This covers how to get traditional vouchers, education saving accounts (ESAs) or tax credit scholarships.  It covers eligibility for vouchers, enrollment with a voucher, discipline, and special education needs.
Parent Terms: Paying for education [ED-03-00-00-00]

Title: Discipline, expulsion, or suspension from school
Definition: This category covers what options a parent or student has when facing discipline measures at a school, and how they may challenge these measures and protect their rights.
Parent Terms: Education [ED-00-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1120000], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1120199], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [12], Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-00012]

Title: Expulsion from school
Definition: This category covers a student and parent's options and rights when the school is trying to expel the student.
Parent Terms: Discipline, expulsion, or suspension from school [ED-04-00-00-00]

Title: Suspension from school
Definition: This category covers a student or parent's rights when the school is trying to suspend the student from school.
Parent Terms: Discipline, expulsion, or suspension from school [ED-04-00-00-00]

Title: Truancy and attendance
Definition: This category covers issues when a student has issues with attending school, skipping school, or being truant. This includes what consequences the student and their family, parents, and guardians may face if there is a problem with truancy. This includes how a school may notify the parents of truancy, visits to the home by an officer, meetings at school, and the possibility of going to the juvenile justice system.
Parent Terms: Discipline, expulsion, or suspension from school [ED-04-00-00-00], Juvenile Justice [CR-10-00-00-00]

Title: Discrimination and rights around education
Definition: This category covers situations in which people face discrimination when trying to access quality education. This could be based on disabilities, race, ethnicity, language, gender, or other factors. It also covers what rights people have to education.
Parent Terms: Education [ED-00-00-00-00], Civil and Human Rights [RI-00-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1130100], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [14], Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-00014]

Title: Desegregation of schools
Definition: This category covers issues with programs to desegregate school systems, or about options to promote desegregation to ensure equal access to quality education.
Parent Terms: Discrimination and rights around education [ED-05-00-00-00]

Title: Exclusion of students from activities
Definition: This category covers options for a student and parents if the student is being excluded from activities, like field trips, school programs, or other activities at the school.
Parent Terms: Discrimination and rights around education [ED-05-00-00-00]

Title: Discrimination based on sex/gender at a school (Title IX)
Definition: This category covers situations when a student feels they may be facing discrimination based on their sex in an educational program or activity that receives federal financial assistance, under the Title IX law. This could be that they're excluded from participation in a program, denied benefits, or subjected to discrimination.
Parent Terms: Discrimination and rights around education [ED-05-00-00-00], Women's Rights [RI-11-00-00-00]

Title: Privacy at school
Definition: This category covers a student's options and protections for the privacy of their personal and school-related information. It could cover concerns they have about school or university administrators inappropriately handling their data, or problems with the school's data privacy policies. It also includes concerns about school surveillance of students, and of students, parents, or other family members' ability to access to a student's school records.
Parent Terms: Education [ED-00-00-00-00], Privacy Rights and Protections [RI-12-00-00-00]

Title: Students with disabilities and special education
Definition: This category concerns the rights, benefits, and legal processes that are open to a student with a disability in the school system. This could also be called special education.
Parent Terms: Education [ED-00-00-00-00], Disability issues and rights [HE-01-10-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1130000], Wikidata Taxonomy [Q212105], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [13], Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-00013]

Title: Assistive technology for students with disabilities
Definition: This category covers what rights a student with disabilities may have to get technology that helps them learn at schools, and what laws (like the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA)) requires of schools.
Parent Terms: Students with disabilities and special education [ED-07-00-00-00]

Title: Protections for students with disabilities
Definition: This category covers rights and protections for students with disabilities. This includes protection under the Individuals with Disabilities Education Ac (ADA), Section 504 civil rights law, and the ADA.
Parent Terms: Students with disabilities and special education [ED-07-00-00-00], Discrimination and rights around education [ED-05-00-00-00]

Title: Rights of students with disabilities when facing discipline
Definition: This category covers the rights and options of students with disabilities or on Individualized Educaiton Plans, when they are facing discipline like suspension, removal from class, or other procedures.
Parent Terms: Protections for students with disabilities [ED-07-02-00-00], Discipline, expulsion, or suspension from school [ED-04-00-00-00]

Title: Individual Education Plans (IEPs)
Definition: This category covers issues around Individual Education Plans, or IEP's, to get quality education for a child's needs, particularly to deal with special needs or disability issues. This can cover how a parent can advocate for a student, make an IEP, make sure it is being followed, and have it changed as needed.
Parent Terms: Students with disabilities and special education [ED-07-00-00-00]

Title: School residency or enrollment
Definition: This category covers issues around enrolling in a particular school or school district, including residency requirements and enrollment procedures.
Parent Terms: Education [ED-00-00-00-00]

Title: School standards, testing, and requirements
Definition: This category covers legal obligations and requirements of schools and students, like the No Child Left Behind or the Every Student Succeeds act. This includes rules about standardized tests, proficiency on these tests, school's obligations to report on progress of certain students, and holding schools accountable for the quality of education.
Parent Terms: Education [ED-00-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1190500], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [ 1140400]

Title: School funding for quality education
Definition: This category covers what funding schools can get, like under Title I, especially for low-income students to improve their educational outcomes.
Parent Terms: School standards, testing, and requirements [ED-09-00-00-00], Students with disabilities and special education [ED-07-00-00-00]

Title: Language access to education
Definition: This category covers issues of getting public education that is bilingual or that is accessible to students with limited English proficiency.
Parent Terms: Language Access rights [RI-21-00-00-00], Discrimination and rights around education [ED-05-00-00-00]

Title: Quality of education for student with disability
Definition: This category covers issues with the quality of education that a student is receiving, and how that standard is defined or how the quality of the education a school is providing can be challenged.
Parent Terms: Students with disabilities and special education [ED-07-00-00-00]

Title: Students' Educational Records
Definition: This category covers how a student or parents can access their educational records, including in order to advocate for an individual education plan or challenge the quality of education being received.
Parent Terms: Education [ED-00-00-00-00], Students with disabilities and special education [ED-07-00-00-00]

Title: Education issues after a natural disaster
Definition: This category covers what rights families have after a natural disaster, to ensure that children can receiving schooling, including enrollment in schools where they are living temporarily
Parent Terms: Education [ED-00-00-00-00], Disaster Relief [DI-00-00-00-00]

Title: Environmental Justice
Definition: This category covers issues around pollution, hazardous waste, poisons, and other issues with the environment.
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2070000], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2070099]

Title: Air Pollution
Definition: This category covers issues around air pollution that people might have in their neighborhood or home, that are causing them problems and that they might need medical help or environmental clean-up for.
Parent Terms: Environmental Justice [EN-00-00-00-00], Problems with living conditions [HO-05-00-00-00]

Title: Environmental Protection
Definition: This category covers options a person might have to protect their environment, if they are concerned that it is being harmed or threatened. This could be in regard to harmful activities that are already occurring, or a wish to preserve the environment as it is.
Parent Terms: Environmental Justice [EN-00-00-00-00]

Title: Hazardous Waste
Definition: This category covers issues a person might have with waste in their community or their home that is causing them harm, or that threatens the environment. It covers options and rights for a person to address the problem, or to get help for harms they've experienced because of the waste.
Parent Terms: Environmental Justice [EN-00-00-00-00]

Title: Pesticides
Definition: This category covers issues that people might have with the use of pesticides, including medical harm they experience or other environmental clean-ups that they may need because of pesticide use.
Parent Terms: Environmental Justice [EN-00-00-00-00], Problems with living conditions [HO-05-00-00-00]

Title: Sustainable Agriculture
Definition: This category covers farmers' issues with organic or sustainable agriculture, including regulations of this industry, certification, leases, and contracts.
Parent Terms: Environmental Justice [EN-00-00-00-00], Running a farm business [BU-03-00-00-00]

Title: Water Pollution
Definition: This category covers issues that a person might experience because of pollution in their home water supply, or in their community's water. It covers options and rights that people have to address pollution problems and get help for harms they are experiencing.
Parent Terms: Environmental Justice [EN-00-00-00-00], Problems with living conditions [HO-05-00-00-00]

Title: Environmental issues after a natural disaster
Definition: This category covers problems like flooding, standing water, extra vegetation, and spoiled items that may occur after a natural disaster. It includes questions about what a homeowner can do with water and other environmental problems after a disaster.
Parent Terms: Environmental Justice [EN-00-00-00-00], Disaster Relief [DI-00-00-00-00]

Title: Estates, Wills, and Guardianships
Definition:
This category covers planning for end-of-life, possible incapacitation, and other special circumstances that would prevent a person from making decisions about their own well-being, finances, and property. This includes issues around wills, powers of attorney, advance directives, trusts, guardianships, conservatorships, and other estate issues that people and families deal with.

Scenarios in this category include making or changing a will/living will/advance directive, setting up a trust or power of attorney, and help with a probate or administering an estate.
Taxonomies: Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-00095], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1950000], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1950099], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [95]

Title: Making a Will and Estate Plan
Definition: This category covers plans that a person can make for what will happen with their property and responsibilities after they die. It includes topics of how property will be divided among spouses, family members, and other interested parties -- and how wills can be written in valid ways in order to spell out a specific plan.
Parent Terms: Estates, Wills, and Guardianships [ES-00-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1950900], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1950099]

Title: Drafting and signing a will
Definition: This category covers how a person can create a will that will be considered valid after they die, in order to specify what will happen to their property and responsibilities.
Parent Terms: Making a Will and Estate Plan [ES-01-00-00-00]

Title: Updating a Will through a Codicil
Definition: This category covers an option for a person to update a will they already wrote, by using a supplementary document called a 'codicil'. This can be to change who will receive property, who the executor will be, who will be guardian for children, or other decisions that were in the original will. The document would be used to change the will without revoking the original. This category covers what makes a codicil valid, how it can be drafted, how it can be signed and verified, and how it may be used after death.
Parent Terms: Making a Will and Estate Plan [ES-01-00-00-00]

Title: Distributing money through Payable-on-Death account
Definition: This category covers how a person might have other people directly receive money after they die, through a bank account called a Payable-on-Death (PDA) Account. It covers how to set such an account up, how long it will take people to receive money after you die, if and how the fund will be frozen, and how this account works with a probate court process.
Parent Terms: Making a Will and Estate Plan [ES-01-00-00-00]

Title: Estate Planning for a beneficiary with a disability
Definition: This category covers issues that a person might face when drafting their estate plans, if one of their children or other beneficiaries have disabilities. This includes how to transfer assets in ways that do not harm that beneficiary's ability to receive public benefits and other support. It also includes how to ensure that the beneficiary will have long-term support for health and care costs.
Parent Terms: Making a Will and Estate Plan [ES-01-00-00-00], Taking Care of Sick or Disabled Family [FA-16-00-00-00], Disability issues and rights [HE-01-10-00-00]

Title: Dealing with another person's estate after they die
Definition: This category covers the options and responsibilities of people who must deal with another's death, and how property is divided up, wills are carried through, or other decisions are made about the person's property and responsibilities. This includes possibly contesting a will or division of property, and what happens when a person dies without a will.
Parent Terms: Estates, Wills, and Guardianships [ES-00-00-00-00]

Title: Contesting a will
Definition: This category covers issues when a person would like to challenge a written will and testament, about how a now-deceased person's property is divided up. This includes who is eligible to contest a will through a legal process, what this process entails, what kinds of objections are valid, and what might happen after the contesting process ends.
Parent Terms: Dealing with another person's estate after they die [ES-02-00-00-00]

Title: Dying without a will (intestate)
Definition: This category covers the law and procedure of what happens to a person's estate if they die without a will. This is called dying "intestate". This covers the local state laws that determine who will get the person's property (including money, securities, real estate, and other assets), what family and partner relationships affect this division, and what happens if there is a probate court process to administer this division.
Parent Terms: Dealing with another person's estate after they die [ES-02-00-00-00]

Title: Probate process for an uncontested will
Definition: This category covers what happens when a person dies with a will, and then the will goes through the court probate process -- without anyone objecting to the will or raising any challenges to it.
Parent Terms: Going to Probate Court [ES-02-04-00-00]

Title: Going to Probate Court
Definition: This category concerns what Probate Court is, how they make decisions about whether a will is valid, how people are notified that an estate is being decided in the probate process, how possible beneficiaries can raise issues, how the court appoints people to administer the process, and how final decisions are made.
Parent Terms: Dealing with another person's estate after they die [ES-02-00-00-00], Going to court and dealing with procedure [CO-07-00-00-00]

Title: When an estate can avoid probate
Definition: This category covers the options people might have to have a now-deceased person's estate may be considered a "small estate" so that it does not have to go through a formal court probate process. This might be through a legal document like an affidavit, if the estate's value is underneath a certain amount and if real estate will not be transferred. These rules differ by state.
Parent Terms: Dealing with another person's estate after they die [ES-02-00-00-00]

Title: Being a 'beneficiary' to another's estate
Definition: This category covers what rights, options, and responsibilities a person has if they have 'beneficiary' status for another now-deceased person's estate. This includes the right to be informed about the will, other beneficiaries, raise issues, receive their inheritance, and be updated about the execution of the will/probate process.
Parent Terms: Dealing with another person's estate after they die [ES-02-00-00-00]

Title: Guardianship and Conservatorship
Definition: This category is about getting decision-making authority over an adult or child's funds, health care, school enrollment, estate, and other concerns. Some states use the term conservatorship for adults, other states use it for control of another person's financial decisions.
Parent Terms: Family [FA-00-00-00-00], Estates, Wills, and Guardianships [ES-00-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1330000], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1330099], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [33]

Title: Money and Property issues in a Guardianship or Conservatorship
Definition: This category is about accounting for funds spent (and possible financial exploitation) in a guardianship or conservatorship. It also covers issues when there is joint property ownership or other questions about the person's estate.
Parent Terms: Guardianship and Conservatorship [ES-03-00-00-00]

Title: Accountings for Funds Spent in a Guardianship or Conservatorship
Definition: This category is about the process and consequences of accounting how money is spent on a guardianship or conservatorship.
Parent Terms: Money and Property issues in a Guardianship or Conservatorship [ES-03-01-00-00]

Title: Financial exploitation in a Guardianship or Conservatorship
Definition: This category is about how to deal with concerns around financial exploitation in a guardianship or conservatorship, the process of evaluating whether there is exploitation, and consequences if there is exploitation.
Parent Terms: Money and Property issues in a Guardianship or Conservatorship [ES-03-01-00-00], Financial exploitation of a person [FA-18-00-00-00]

Title: Joint Property issues in a guardianship/conservatorship
Definition: This category covers issues when the person under the guardianship or conservatorship co-owns property with other people.
Parent Terms: Money and Property issues in a Guardianship or Conservatorship [ES-03-01-00-00]

Title: Guardianship or Conservatorship of an Adult
Definition: This category is about the processes of getting, contesting, changing, or ending a guardianship or conservatorship of an adult person over the age of 18. This might be when the adult is disabled, has a severe mental illness, or is not able to make decisions about their finances, legal matters, or physical well-being.
Parent Terms: Guardianship and Conservatorship [ES-03-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1330200], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1330204], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1330203], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1330202], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1330201]

Title: Getting a Conservatorship or Guardianship of an Adult
Definition: This category is about the process and consequences of becoming a guardian or conservator of an adult (someone over the age of 18), to care for a person who is unable to care for themselves or manage their finances. This might be because the person is disabled or incapacitated.
Parent Terms: Guardianship or Conservatorship of an Adult [ES-03-02-00-00]

Title: Getting an Emergency Guardianship of an Adult
Definition: This category is about applying for an emergency procedure to become the guardian of an adult. This may be because there has been an accident or injury that has made the adult mentally unable to care for themselves. The emergency guardianship would allow the guardian to care for the person's estate and person for a short period of time -- and then could possibly be extended.
Parent Terms: Getting a Conservatorship or Guardianship of an Adult [ES-03-02-01-00]

Title: Guardianship of a Mentally Ill Adult
Definition: This category is about the process of getting a guardianship (or conservatorship, in some states) of an adult who may have a severe mental illness. This includes the process to determine if the person has capacity to care for their own health, safety, and property. It includes different types of guardianships, and who can become this guardian or conservator.
Parent Terms: Getting a Conservatorship or Guardianship of an Adult [ES-03-02-01-00], Mental Health [HE-01-01-00-00]

Title: Guardian Ad Litem for vulnerable adults in housing cases
Definition: This category covers how a Guardian Ad Litem may be appointed for an adult facing a housing case (usually an eviction) who is unable to advocate for themselves because of an issue like mental illness or age. This category covers how and when this appointment might happen, what the Guardian Ad Litem does, and how the appointment may be terminated.
Parent Terms: Guardianship or Conservatorship of an Adult [ES-03-02-00-00], Eviction from a home [HO-02-00-00-00]

Title: Conservatorship of an adult's financial affairs
Definition: This category is about some states' options of getting a conservatorship of another adult's financial matters, when they are unable to make decisions for themselves. In some states, it may be called a Limited Conservatorship -- either of the 'person' when it's about the personal needs, or about the 'estate' when it's about financial needs.
Parent Terms: Getting a Conservatorship or Guardianship of an Adult [ES-03-02-01-00]

Title: Guardianship of a child (under 18)
Definition: This category is about the process and consequences of getting a guardianship or conservatorship of a child (under age 18), contesting one, changing one, and ending one. This includes situations where the child has an estate that is contested or uncontested, where the child has no estate, where there is a temporary or standby situation, and where there is a Guardian ad Litem (in court representation).
Parent Terms: Guardianship and Conservatorship [ES-03-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1440000], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1440099], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1440100], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1440200], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1440300], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1440600], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [44]

Title: Guardian Ad Litem for child in family law cases
Definition: This category covers the options and process around having a Guardian Ad Litem appointed to represent a child in court cases. This could be for an adoption, child custody, child support, divorce, emancipation, or visitation case. This category covers how and when the court may appoint a Guardian Ad Litem, what they do, and how they may be removed or the appointment ended.
Parent Terms: Guardianship of a child (under 18) [ES-03-03-00-00], Children's Issues during a divorce or separation [FA-06-06-00-00], Adoption [FA-01-00-00-00]

Title: Getting a Guardianship of a Child
Definition: This category concerns the process of becoming appointed by the court to be a guardian for a minor child (under age 18). The person being appointed should ensure the minor is properly cared for in terms of health, upbringing and education -- and that significant assets are protected.  This includes situations where there is an estate or no estate, when the appointment is contested or uncontested, and temporary or standby appointments.
Parent Terms: Guardianship of a child (under 18) [ES-03-03-00-00]
Taxonomies: Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-00044], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1440000], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1440099]

Title: Guardianship of a child who has been abused or neglected
Definition: This category covers how a legal guardianship of a minor child may be used if the parents are unable to provide for the child's safety and protection, and the guardian then becomes responsible for the child's care.
Parent Terms: Guardianship of a child (under 18) [ES-03-03-00-00], Domestic Violence and Abuse [FA-07-00-00-00], Terminating Parental Rights [FA-14-01-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1420100], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [42]

Title: Standby guardianship plan for a child
Definition: This category covers the option for parents to appoint another to take care of their child if they become incapacitated, they die, they face immigration actions, or otherwise are unable to care for their child suddenly. They do not give up their parental rights, and they may revoke their consent to this standby guardianship at any time. Typically this can be established with a signed document and witnesses, but without a court process.
Parent Terms: Guardianship of a child (under 18) [ES-03-03-00-00], Detention of immigrants [IM-02-00-00-00], Deportation or Removal of immigrants [IM-01-00-00-00]

Title: Short-term Temporary Guardianship of a child
Definition: This category covers legal options for a parent who wants another adult to be the guardian for their child for a short period of time (usually under a year or 6 months). This might be an arrangement that doesn't have to go through the court, but is through a private agreement.
Parent Terms: Guardianship of a child (under 18) [ES-03-03-00-00]

Title: Rights of Guardians and Conservators
Definition: This category is about the rights that people have while serving as guardians or conservators to others (including to children and to adults). This includes distinctions between the rights that a guardian might have, versus that of someone who adopts another.
Parent Terms: Guardianship and Conservatorship [ES-03-00-00-00]

Title: Removal of a Guardian or Conservator
Definition: This category is about the process and consequences of removing a person from the role of guardian or conservator for another person (child or adult).
Parent Terms: Guardianship and Conservatorship [ES-03-00-00-00]

Title: Trusts
Definition: This category is about how to set up, use, deal with disputes, and end a trust. It also covers different types of trusts, including those set up as part of a guardianship. Trusts are tools to save assets, set rules about how they are used, who can access the assets, and other issues. Trusts may be a part of a plan to provide for dependents with disabilities or special needs.
Parent Terms: Estates, Wills, and Guardianships [ES-00-00-00-00], Guardianship and Conservatorship [ES-03-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1950600], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1950699]

Title: Living Trusts
Definition: This category is about how to set up and use a living trust, to manage assets while someone still alive. It includes how assets may be distributed, and what kinds of types there are, including revocable and irrevocable living trusts. It also covers how a living trust is different from a will or a guardianship.

Title: Plans for if you are incapacitated or ill (Powers of Attorney and Advance Directives)
Definition: This category concerns options that a person has to have others make decisions about their medical, legal, financial, or other life matters. It includes options for medical care if a person has a terminal injury or illness, health-care proxies, do not resuscitate orders, organ donation choices, and powers of attorney.
Parent Terms: Estates, Wills, and Guardianships [ES-00-00-00-00], Health [HE-00-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1960000], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1960099]

Title: Advance Directives about possible medical treatments
Definition: This category concerns how to get an advance directive, maintain it, implement it, and deal with issues surrounding it. An advance directive is a document that spells out a person's wishes about medical treatment, so that others can carry these plans out if the person is unable to communicate them.
Parent Terms: Plans for if you are incapacitated or ill (Powers of Attorney and Advance Directives) [ES-05-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1960100], Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-00096], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [96]

Title: Living Wills for when a person is terminally ill
Definition: This category concerns how to get, maintain, implement, and deal with living wills, to determine how they will be treated if they are terminally ill. A living will is different than a last will and testament. It allows a person to approve or decline certain types of medical care, if one has a terminal injury or illness. It includes provisions about declining medical treatment, that might lead one to die as a result.
Parent Terms: Plans for if you are incapacitated or ill (Powers of Attorney and Advance Directives) [ES-05-00-00-00]

Title: Powers of Attorney
Definition: This category concerns how to get, maintain, implement, and deal with issues of Powers of Attorney. A power of attorney is typically a legal document that gives one person the power to act for another person, with authority to make legal decisions about property, finances, or medical care. It's usually used when a person is ill, disabled, or not present for a transaction. There are different types of power of attorney depending on the situation -- in which the designated person might have certain limits, durations, springing conditions, or otherwise.
Parent Terms: Plans for if you are incapacitated or ill (Powers of Attorney and Advance Directives) [ES-05-00-00-00]

Title: Options around Life-Sustaining Treatments
Definition: This category covers issues when a person needs life-sustaining medical treatment to stay alive, and there may be questions about whether these treatments should be withheld (not provided in the first place), or withdrawn (ended after they have begun).
Parent Terms: Plans for if you are incapacitated or ill (Powers of Attorney and Advance Directives) [ES-05-00-00-00]

Title: Funeral and Burial Issues
Definition: This category covers situations where a person must take care of a funeral and burial, including covering costs, making plans, and resolving disputes.
Parent Terms: Estates, Wills, and Guardianships [ES-00-00-00-00]

Title: Estate Planning for Military
Definition: This category includes issues around life insurance for military service members, and death benefits that are unique to service members.
Parent Terms: Veterans and Military [VE-00-00-00-00], Making a Will and Estate Plan [ES-01-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1770900], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1770999]

Title: Benefits for service members after death
Definition: This category covers what financial and other benefits that a service members' family can expect after the death of the service member, and how to make use of these benefits or deal with any problems.
Parent Terms: Estate Planning for Military [ES-07-00-00-00]

Title: Family
Definition:
This category covers issues that arise within a family, like divorce, adoption, name change, guardianship, domestic violence, child custody, and other issues.

Scenarios in this category include problems with serving as a foster parent, issues adopting a child, difficulties with being appointed as the guardian of a child, filing for divorce or separation, difficulty collecting alimony payments, experience with domestic violence or sexual assault, and problems involving a vulnerable adult being taken advantage of or abused.
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1390000], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1390099], Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-00039], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [39]

Title: Adoption
Definition: This category is about adopting a child or adult, challenging an adoption, and other family members' rights around an adoption.
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1300100], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1300199], Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-00030], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [30]

Title: Adopting a Child
Definition: This category is about the process and benefits of adopting a child, including dealing with a contested adoption or getting time off from work.
Parent Terms: Adoption [FA-01-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1300100], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1300199]

Title: Uncontested Adoption of a Child
Definition: This category is about the process and outcomes of adopting a child, when there is no one contesting the adoption.
Parent Terms: Adopting a Child [FA-01-01-00-00]

Title: Contested Adoption of a Child
Definition: This category is about the process and consequences of adopting a child, when someone is contesting the adoption.
Parent Terms: Adopting a Child [FA-01-01-00-00]

Title: Getting Time off Work for an Adoption
Definition: About taking a temporary leave from a current job, while going through an adoption process or after an adopted child has joined one's family.
Parent Terms: Adopting a Child [FA-01-01-00-00], Taking Time off Work at Current Job [WO-02-14-00-00]

Title: Adopting an Adult
Definition: This category is about the process and consequences of adopting a person who is legally an adult.
Parent Terms: Adoption [FA-01-00-00-00]

Title: Contesting an Adoption
Definition: This category is about challenging the adoption of a child or an adult, including the process to do so, eligibility to do so, and possible outcomes.
Parent Terms: Adoption [FA-01-00-00-00]

Title: Birth Parents' Rights around an Adoption
Definition: About the rights that the biological mother and father of a child have, during the adoption process and after it is complete.
Parent Terms: Adoption [FA-01-00-00-00]

Title: Grandparents' and other Family Members' Rights around an Adoption
Definition: About the rights of grandparents, aunts, uncles, cousins, siblings, and other family members (aside from the birth parents), regarding a child being adopted -- both during the adoption process and after it is finalized.
Parent Terms: Adoption [FA-01-00-00-00]

Title: Adoption of a Stepchild by a Stepparent
Definition: This category covers how a stepmother or stepfather may proceed with an adoption of a stepchild. It covers topics like abandonment by birth parents, consent from other parents, screening, consent from children, and the legal effects of an adoption.
Parent Terms: Adoption [FA-01-00-00-00]

Title: Birth Certificates and Identity Documents
Definition: About getting certificates, cards, licenses, and other official documentation to prove something about yourself or someone else.
Parent Terms: Family [FA-00-00-00-00], Getting information and records from the government [GO-02-00-00-00]

Title: Child Care Costs
Definition: About paying for the costs of children's daycare, caretakers, and educational expenses. It also relates to economic development and child care concerns.
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2050200], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1390300]

Title: Child Care support through TANF
Definition: This category concerns child care subsidies that low-income families might access through the Temporary Assistance for Need Families (TANF) program. States that administer TANF funds may use them to provide child care assistance (though not all do).
Parent Terms: Child Care Costs [FA-03-00-00-00], Amount of money received through TANF [BE-02-02-03-00]

Title: Child Custody, Parenting Plans, and Visitation
Definition:
This category is about making child custody orders and parenting plans, modifying it and enforcing it, getting visitation for different family members, and dealing with abductions by a family member.

Scenarios in this category include trouble reaching an agreement about custody or visitation arrangements, a custody or visitation agreement not being followed, and problems collecting or paying child support.
Parent Terms: Family [FA-00-00-00-00], Children's Issues during a divorce or separation [FA-06-06-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1310100], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1310199], Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-03100], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [31]

Title: Parental abduction or kidnapping of a child
Definition: This category concerns when a parent of a child might face charges for abducting and/or kidnapping the child, when violating a custody order, and snatching a child or concealing a child. This may involve the federal law of Parental Kidnapping Prevention Act (PKPA) that deals with jurisdictional problems of child custody cases, when a parent might take a child across state lines in violation of a custody order.
Parent Terms: Child Custody, Parenting Plans, and Visitation [FA-04-00-00-00], Custody issues around Domestic Violence [FA-07-03-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1370141], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1310101]

Title: Emergency Custody orders and hearings
Definition: This category concerns how to resolve 'emergency' issues around child custody, including around changing existing custody orders and getting a hearing with the court to make this temporary change.  It might regard imminent danger and harm the child faces, problems with the child's health and welfare, or other changed circumstances. A court hearing on the issue may result in an emergency order that will be temporary, and then reviewed at a full trial to determine if it should continue or be removed.
Parent Terms: Child Custody, Parenting Plans, and Visitation [FA-04-00-00-00]

Title: Modifying a Custody Order
Definition: This category concerns how to secure modifications of a child custody order and/or parenting plan.
Parent Terms: Child Custody, Parenting Plans, and Visitation [FA-04-00-00-00]

Title: Modifying a custody order for a parent in recovery for substance abuse
Definition: This category covers the options and processes for a parent who is in recovery for substance abuse, and wants to modify the custody order for visiting their children.
Parent Terms: Modifying a Custody Order [FA-04-03-00-00], Alcoholism and Substance Abuse [HE-01-04-00-00]

Title: Interstate Child Custody and Jurisdiction issues
Definition: This category concerns problems when parents of a child reside in separate states, and have issues with how custody will be decided. This includes questions about determining the child's home state, what state will have jurisdiction over the court matters, what the Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement Act says, and what happens when a parent wants to move a child out of state.
Parent Terms: Child Custody, Parenting Plans, and Visitation [FA-04-00-00-00], Court's Jurisdiction to hear a case [CO-07-03-04-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1310106], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1310109]

Title: Competing Jurisdictions for child custody cases
Definition: This category concerns issues when more there might be competing jurisdictions (states or countries) that might be the 'home state' for a child, and make decisions about a custody order for a child.
Parent Terms: Interstate Child Custody and Jurisdiction issues [FA-04-04-00-00]

Title: Emergency Jurisdiction for child custody
Definition: This category is about how a court (that is not usually in the 'home state' jurisdiction of the child) may have temporary emergency jurisdiction over the custody case, if the child is in that state and there has been an emergency. This might have been because the child has been abandoned, abused, threatened, or has another emergency.
Parent Terms: Interstate Child Custody and Jurisdiction issues [FA-04-04-00-00], Emergency Custody orders and hearings [FA-04-02-00-00]

Title: Enforcing a Child Custody order
Definition: This category concerns process and issues of enforcing a child custody order or parenting plan.
Parent Terms: Child Custody, Parenting Plans, and Visitation [FA-04-00-00-00]

Title: Temporary Child Custody
Definition: This category concerns how to get, deal with, extend, or end a temporary child custody order.
Parent Terms: Child Custody, Parenting Plans, and Visitation [FA-04-00-00-00]

Title: Child Visitation
Definition: This category concerns issues on getting visitation rights to see a child, over which one does not have custody. This includes the non-custodial parent's visitation rights, setting reasonable visitation schedules, and having third-party visitation like by grandparents or other extended family members.
Parent Terms: Child Custody, Parenting Plans, and Visitation [FA-04-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1310200], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1310299]

Title: Enforcing Child Visitation
Definition: This category concerns how a person can try to enforce their visitation order, if there are issues with the other parent adhering to the order's terms.
Parent Terms: Child Visitation [FA-04-07-00-00], Enforcing a court's judgment [CO-07-05-03-00]

Title: Modifying a Child Visitation Order
Definition: This category concerns the process and issues around making modifications to an existing child visitation order.
Parent Terms: Child Visitation [FA-04-07-00-00]

Title: Getting a Child Visitation Order
Definition: This category concerns the process and options of getting a visitation order (or sometimes known as a 'parenting time' order). This may be when parents are unable to agree with each other, and need the court to issue an official order to ensure the parent can have visitation and parenting time.
Parent Terms: Child Visitation [FA-04-07-00-00]

Title: Third-Party Visitation of child
Definition: This category concerns getting third parties, like grandparents or extended family members, visitation with a child.
Parent Terms: Child Visitation [FA-04-07-00-00]

Title: Supervised or Monitored visitation with a child
Definition: This category covers how a parent or other person might get visitation with a child, if it must be supervised or monitored. It might also include supervised exchanges of a child. This includes how to request this kind of supervision arrangement, how to comply with it, and how to deal with problems that might arise.
Parent Terms: Child Visitation [FA-04-07-00-00]

Title: Third-Party Child Custody
Definition: This category concerns custody issues when a third party, meaning a person who is not the biological parent of the child, is trying to establish, modify, or end custody of the child.
Parent Terms: Child Custody, Parenting Plans, and Visitation [FA-04-00-00-00]

Title: Parenting Plans
Definition: This category covers parenting plans, including what they are, how to establish one, how to change one, and how to enforce the plan. It could be an Individual Parenting Plan or Joint Parenting Plan.
Parent Terms: Child Custody, Parenting Plans, and Visitation [FA-04-00-00-00]

Title: Child Support
Definition: This category concerns issues around creating child support orders, modifying and enforcing them, paying for other children's' expenses, and claiming children's expenses on taxes.
Parent Terms: Family [FA-00-00-00-00], Money, Debt, and Consumer Issues [MO-00-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1380100], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1380199], Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-00038], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [38]

Title: Enforcement of Child Support
Definition: This category concerns issues around enforcing child support orders, including around tax intercepts, laws like URESA and 4-D, private enforcement, and other issues.
Parent Terms: Child Support [FA-05-00-00-00], Enforcing a court's judgment [CO-07-05-03-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1380300], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1380399]

Title: Going to Child Support (IV-D) Court
Definition: This category concerns issues when a person goes to a child support court (or IV-D or 4-D court) to deal with an issue around child support enforcement.
Parent Terms: Enforcement of Child Support [FA-05-01-00-00], Going to court and dealing with procedure [CO-07-00-00-00]

Title: Getting state support in enforcing child support
Definition: This category concerns issues in a particularly type of child support cases (known technically as IV-D cases), in which the parent with custody of the children receives assistance from the state's agency that helps to enforce child support. This support might be for locating the other parent, establishing paternity, or establishing and enforcing the child support order.
Parent Terms: Enforcement of Child Support [FA-05-01-00-00]

Title: Intercepting tax refunds for child support
Definition: This category concerns how a parent who doesn't have custody of their children, might have their federal income tax refund checks intercepted. They may also have lottery winnings or other money that the federal or state government owes them intercepted, in order to pay for child support payments they owe.
Parent Terms: Enforcement of Child Support [FA-05-01-00-00], Taxes [MO-09-00-00-00]

Title: Enforcing child support in different states
Definition: This category concerns issues of collecting child support payments in other states (than the original child support order was made). This includes the Uniform Reciprocal Enforcement of Support Act (URESA), a law that lets a parent enforce a child support order in different states.
Parent Terms: Enforcement of Child Support [FA-05-01-00-00]

Title: Petitions for Child Support
Definition: This category concerns how a person can ask for child support through a petition to the court, and how the other parent can respond to such a petition. This includes the court process to follow, the hearings, establishing an agreement, and responding to the other partners' requests.
Parent Terms: Child Support [FA-05-00-00-00]

Title: Private enforcement of child support
Definition: This category concerns private measures a parent might take to enforce a child support order, like through a private child support collection agency or private attorney.
Parent Terms: Enforcement of Child Support [FA-05-01-00-00]

Title: Modifying Child Support arrangement
Definition: This category concerns whether and how a parent can modify a child support order or arrangement. It also concerns how the other parent can respond to an attempt to modify the arrangement.
Parent Terms: Child Support [FA-05-00-00-00]

Title: Child Support Guidelines for calculation and enforcement
Definition: This category concerns the guidelines that have states set rules for how child support arrangements are calculated and enforced.  This includes the financial models that each state establishes, like based on income or needs. It also covers the judges' discretion in deciding how to use different models, and how a parent can challenge the guidelines.
Parent Terms: Child Support [FA-05-00-00-00]

Title: Other Custodial parent issues around child support
Definition: This category concerns issues that a custodial parent might have with child support, other than how to get child support, modify arrangements, or enforce an order. This might include questions around termination of child support, remarriage, finding help, or other issues.
Parent Terms: Child Support [FA-05-00-00-00]

Title: Other Non-custodial parent issues with child support
Definition: This category concerns other issues that a parent without custody over the child might have with child support, other than responding to petitions for it, modifying it, or dealing with enforcement of it. These issues might be around remarriage, moving home, bankruptcy, or the child getting older.
Parent Terms: Child Support [FA-05-00-00-00]

Title: Being Behind on child support
Definition: This category covers situations where a parent is behind on child support, and is trying to understand their options. It can include understanding what can be done, how being behind may affect visitation, and what consequences one might face.
Parent Terms: Child Support [FA-05-00-00-00]

Title: Divorce, Separation, and Annulment
Definition: This category concerns issues around filing for divorce, separation, or annulment, getting spousal support, splitting money and property, and following the court processes.
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1320200], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1320099], Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-00032], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [32]

Title: Spousal Support, Alimony, and Separate Maintenance
Definition: This category concerns issues that arise over financial support between spouses/partners that are separating or getting divorced. This is separate from child support or division of property during the divorce. This category includes how to get short-term or long-term financial support established, setting up lump sum payments, dealing with Qualified Domestic Relations Order (QDRO) to divide marital property, and other court-ordered payments during the separation or divorce.
Parent Terms: Divorce, Separation, and Annulment [FA-06-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1320300], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1320399], Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-00038]

Title: Long-term Spousal Support
Definition: This category covers questions around how a spouse can get long-term financial support, depending on local state rules about long-term or short-term marriages, the possibility of permanent alimony, or other issues. This is different than short-term support, because it is not a temporary arrangement during the divorce process but rather an official arrangement after the divorce is final.
Parent Terms: Spousal Support, Alimony, and Separate Maintenance [FA-06-01-00-00]

Title: Lump Sum Spousal Support
Definition: This category covers the possibility of when a spouse makes a single, all-encompassing lump sum payment to the other (rather than having recurring payments). This includes issues around calculating this amount, taxes on it, alimony buyouts, and other topics.
Parent Terms: Spousal Support, Alimony, and Separate Maintenance [FA-06-01-00-00]

Title: Spousal Support from pensions and retirement plans (with a QDRO)
Definition: This category concerns how divorcing spouses can divide assets held in pensions or retirement plans, using a formal Qualified Domestic Relations Order (QDRO). This includes both establishing the division during the divorce, or afterward when an ex-spouse is not receiving required support payments. The category covers when a judge can issue a QDRO to collect delinquent support, and which kinds of retirement funds can be subjected to QDRO.
Parent Terms: Spousal Support, Alimony, and Separate Maintenance [FA-06-01-00-00], Retirement and Pensions [WO-04-00-00-00]

Title: Short-Term or Temporary Spousal Support
Definition: This category covers short-term support that one spouse may have to pay to another during the divorce process. Once the divorce is over, the short-term or temporary support should end and a longer-term financial arrangement may begin.
