Parent Terms: Spousal Support, Alimony, and Separate Maintenance [FA-06-01-00-00]

Title: Legal Separation of spouses
Definition: This category deals with how married couples can officially separate from each other through a court process. It covers the rights and obligations the separated spouses have to each other, and how it differs from a permanent end to the marriage or from a more informal separation.
Parent Terms: Divorce, Separation, and Annulment [FA-06-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1320600], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1320699]

Title: Division of property among separated spouses
Definition: This category covers how spouses that are going through a formal, legal separation can divide property among each other, the different state rules on property division, and other issues.
Parent Terms: Legal Separation of spouses [FA-06-02-00-00], Dividing Property and Debt among spouses [FA-06-05-00-00]

Title: Property Settlement agreements for separated spouses
Definition: This category covers how separating spouses can formally divide their property using a property settlement agreement. It covers how this written contract can be made, contested, or ended.
Parent Terms: Legal Separation of spouses [FA-06-02-00-00], Property Settlement agreements among spouses [FA-06-05-01-00]

Title: Divorce process and types
Definition: This category concerns the options and process of getting divorced, or formally ending a marriage between two spouses. It covers contested and uncontested divorce paths, what happens afterward, how it affects finances and taxes, and other issues that arise.
Parent Terms: Divorce, Separation, and Annulment [FA-06-00-00-00], Going to court and dealing with procedure [CO-07-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1320500], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1320599], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1320560], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1320569]

Title: Contested divorce process
Definition: This category concerns the definition and process of a contested divorce, in which spouses cannot agree, either about whether to get divorced, or the terms of the divorce (like the division of assets and debts, alimony, child support, or custody). This includes how to contest a divorce, what the court procedure will be, and other issues that arise.
Parent Terms: Divorce process and types [FA-06-03-00-00]

Title: Uncontested Divorce process
Definition: This category covers the definition and process of getting an uncontested divorce. This is when both spouses agree on getting the divorce, and agree on the key areas of division of property, child support, spousal support, custody, and other topics. This includes how court hearings will work, what evidence you need, whether you need a lawyer, and other issues.
Parent Terms: Divorce process and types [FA-06-03-00-00]

Title: Subpoenas in a divorce process
Definition: This category covers how to use or respond to a subpoena in a divorce, which involves requesting documents or evidence to be presented in the court.
Parent Terms: Divorce process and types [FA-06-03-00-00]

Title: Taxes after divorce
Definition: This category concerns how spouses can file taxes, take exemptions and exclusions, and deal with other divorce-related tax issues.
Parent Terms: Divorce, Separation, and Annulment [FA-06-00-00-00], Taxes [MO-09-00-00-00]

Title: Child and spousal support's effect on taxes
Definition: This category covers a person's tax issues when they or their former spouse/partner is paying child support or spousal support (or, alimony). This includes questions of what is deductible, how to calculate income, and other questions.
Parent Terms: Taxes after divorce [FA-06-03-04-00], Child Support [FA-05-00-00-00], Spousal Support, Alimony, and Separate Maintenance [FA-06-01-00-00]

Title: Filing motions after the final divorce decree
Definition: This category concerns motions that a person might file after the divorce has been finalized to deal with issues they consider still in need of court involvement. It might mean the motions that an ex-spouse files to re-open questions that had been in the original divorce judgment.
Parent Terms: Problems after a final divorce, separation, or annulment judgment [FA-06-07-00-00]

Title: Consolidating cases during a divorce
Definition: This category covers how a spouse may consolidate separate court cases into a single one, during a divorce process. This might mean the consolidation of a divorce case with a child custody case, or with a domestic violence protection order, so that the court can resolve all issues at once.
Parent Terms: Divorce process and types [FA-06-03-00-00]

Title: Reopening a divorce for new evidence
Definition: This category covers how a spouse can reopen a divorce that had already been finalized if there has been new evidence that could change the outcome of the original hearing and judgment.
Parent Terms: Problems after a final divorce, separation, or annulment judgment [FA-06-07-00-00]

Title: Stopping (or staying) a divorce process
Definition: This category concerns how to stop or pause divorce proceedings in court. A stay is a ruling in the case that temporarily stops further actions in the legal process. It can be lifted and the case proceedings may start again later.
Parent Terms: Divorce process and types [FA-06-03-00-00]

Title: Venue of a divorce case
Definition: This category concerns what venue, or location, the divorce case should be filed in, or how the venue can be changed.
Parent Terms: Divorce process and types [FA-06-03-00-00]

Title: Filing for divorce
Definition: This category covers what a person can do when initiating a divorce process. This includes how to file a divorce case, how much it costs, what forms to fill out, and how to serve papers on the other side.
Parent Terms: Divorce process and types [FA-06-03-00-00], Being a Plaintiff in lawsuit (suing someone) [TO-04-02-00-00]

Title: Responding to a divorce the other spouse filed
Definition: This category covers how a spouse can respond to a divorce case that the other spouse has filed. This includes what to do when served with divorce papers, how to file an answer, and how to serve papers on the other spouse.
Parent Terms: Divorce process and types [FA-06-03-00-00], Being a Defendant in a lawsuit (being sued) [TO-04-03-00-00]

Title: Annulment of a marriage
Definition: This category covers how spouses can have the court formally say that their marriage (or domestic partnership) is not legally valid. The annulment will make it as if the marriage/partnership never happened because it was never legal. This category covers legal reasons for which spouses can get an annulment, like incest, bigamy, age at marriage, prior marriages, fraud, incapacity, or other issues. It also covers the process of getting an annulment, statute of limitations on filing for one, and other issues.
Parent Terms: Divorce, Separation, and Annulment [FA-06-00-00-00]

Title: Dividing Property and Debt among spouses
Definition: This category covers how property and debt are divided when two spouses separate or divorce. This includes topics like which property is subject to division, dealing with special rules like community property law, creating property settlements, contesting agreements, dealing with pensions, dividing debt obligations, and other issues that may arise when spouses end their marriage.
Parent Terms: Divorce, Separation, and Annulment [FA-06-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1320550], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1320559]

Title: Property Settlement agreements among spouses
Definition: This category covers how spouses that are divorcing or separating can formally agree to a division of their property, in a binding contract.
Parent Terms: Dividing Property and Debt among spouses [FA-06-05-00-00]

Title: Community Property laws for spouses
Definition: This category concerns how certain states' community property laws apply to spouses' money, real estate, and personal property. It covers the definition of what counts as community properties, how things will be divided if spouses separate or divorce, and what happens if one spouse dies.
Parent Terms: Dividing Property and Debt among spouses [FA-06-05-00-00], Marriages and civil unions [FA-10-00-00-00]

Title: Dividing Debt during a divorce
Definition: This category covers how spouses' debt may be divided during the divorce or separation process. This includes how the court will decide who is responsible for paying specific credit card, medical, mortgage, auto loan, and other bills.
Parent Terms: Dividing Property and Debt among spouses [FA-06-05-00-00], Debt and Lending Money [MO-12-00-00-00]

Title: Dividing real estate property in a divorce
Definition: This category concerns how spouses can divide real estate through deeds and abstracts while getting divorced. It covers how the ownership of the property might be transferred.
Parent Terms: Dividing Property and Debt among spouses [FA-06-05-00-00]

Title: Dividing pensions and retirement accounts in a divorce
Definition: This category concerns how spouses' pensions or other retirement accounts may be divided during a divorce process.
Parent Terms: Dividing Property and Debt among spouses [FA-06-05-00-00], Retirement and Pensions [WO-04-00-00-00]

Title: Marital vs. Non-Marital Property standards
Definition: This category covers how different states define what property is considered 'marital' or 'non-marital' when it comes to how this property will be divided during a divorce.
Parent Terms: Dividing Property and Debt among spouses [FA-06-05-00-00]

Title: Equitable Distribution laws for spouses
Definition: This category covers those states that have laws following an 'Equitable Distribution' standard in how property is divided up during a divorce. This is in comparison with community property law. This category covers how this standard affects how a court decides which property to divide, and how to divide it.
Parent Terms: Dividing Property and Debt among spouses [FA-06-05-00-00]

Title: Re-opening or changing divorce property judgments
Definition: This category concerns how an ex-spouse may request the court to reconsider a property judgment, change its permanency, or set it aside.
Parent Terms: Dividing Property and Debt among spouses [FA-06-05-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1320539], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1320528]

Title: Stopping a spouse from hiding or destroying assets
Definition: This category concerns how a spouse may stop another from hiding or destroying assets during the divorce process, to change how the property will be divided. This includes using a preliminary injunction in the court, to have the judge possibly stop this behavior and prevent fraud. It also covers what happens if a spouse violates this injunction from the court, including penalties and criminal charges that spouse might face.
Parent Terms: Dividing Property and Debt among spouses [FA-06-05-00-00]

Title: Children's Issues during a divorce or separation
Definition: This category concerns issues that children of divorcing or separating spouses may face during the legal process. This can include the determination of the best interest of the child, case management orders, parental rights and responsibilities, and other problems that may arise.
Parent Terms: Divorce, Separation, and Annulment [FA-06-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1310500], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1310599]

Title: Best Interest of Child standard
Definition: This category concerns the formal standard that courts will use, called the 'Best Interest of the Child'. It covers what this standard means, how it will be decided, what parents can prove regarding it, and what implications it has for child custody and other issues during the divorce process.
Parent Terms: Children's Issues during a divorce or separation [FA-06-06-00-00]

Title: Children-related divorce case management orders
Definition: This category covers orders that may be issued by a judge during possible case management conferences in a divorce process that relate to children's issues. This may include appointment of a guardian ad litem to represent children's issues, social investigations, resolve disputes, or keep the process moving.
Parent Terms: Children's Issues during a divorce or separation [FA-06-06-00-00]

Title: Mediation for children's issues and parenting plans
Definition: This category covers how mediation may be used during a divorce process to help parents resolve issues around parenting and create a parenting plan in the child's best interests. This includes details on state-specific rules about whether mediation is required, how mediation works, and what kind of settlement or agreement may be created during it.
Parent Terms: Children's Issues during a divorce or separation [FA-06-06-00-00], Child Custody, Parenting Plans, and Visitation [FA-04-00-00-00], Mediation and Alternative Dispute Resolution for family [FA-13-00-00-00]

Title: Parental Rights and Responsibilities during a divorce
Definition: This category concerns how parents' rights and responsibilities change during and after a divorce process. This includes how spouses and courts will determine what the new arrangement is for each parent's relationship to their child, possibly attending court-sponsored parenting classes, and other new obligations parents might have toward their child.
Parent Terms: Children's Issues during a divorce or separation [FA-06-06-00-00], Parental Rights (and Termination) [FA-14-00-00-00]

Title: Problems after a final divorce, separation, or annulment judgment
Definition: This category is about problems that a spouse or parent might have after a divorce case has ended with a judgment, especially if the other person is not following it. It might be issues around enforcing the order, modifying it, or holding the other person in contempt for not obeying the order.
Parent Terms: Divorce, Separation, and Annulment [FA-06-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1320510], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1320591]

Title: Contempt of court for violating a family law order
Definition: This category is about how one ex-spouse, partner, or parent may try to address problems with another person not following a family law court order, by asking the court to hold them in contempt. This covers what one needs to show to request a contempt of court ruling, what happens at the hearing, and the consequences of being found in contempt.
Parent Terms: Problems after a final divorce, separation, or annulment judgment [FA-06-07-00-00], Enforcing Child Visitation [FA-04-07-01-00], Enforcing a Child Custody order [FA-04-05-00-00], Enforcing a protection order [FA-07-09-00-00], Enforcement of Child Support [FA-05-01-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1320540], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1320549]

Title: Consequences of being found in contempt of family law judgment
Definition: This category concerns what happens if the court rules that a person is in contempt of a family law judgment, like that for divorce, custody, or otherwise. It covers the kinds of things that the other person might get, or what the person in contempt must do -- like get counseling, complete a parenting class, pay fees, or spend time with children.
Parent Terms: Contempt of court for violating a family law order [FA-06-07-01-00]

Title: Contempt for financial issues related to a family law judgment
Definition: This category concerns how one person may ask the court to hold another for being in contempt of a court order (like that for a divorce judgment), regarding financial issues. This could be if the person does not hand over required financial documents, failing to pay ordered money support, or otherwise.
Parent Terms: Contempt of court for violating a family law order [FA-06-07-01-00]

Title: Contempt for children's issues related to a family law judgment
Definition: This category concerns how a person might be held to be in contempt of court for violating a family law order (like that for child custody or divorce) related to children's issues. It could be about not following visitation schedules, custody orders, parenting plans, or other child-related orders. This category covers the process and consequences of being held in contempt.
Parent Terms: Contempt of court for violating a family law order [FA-06-07-01-00], Children's Issues during a divorce or separation [FA-06-06-00-00]

Title: Enforcing a divorce or separation judgment
Definition: This category concerns how to deal with issues around enforcing another spouse to follow a final divorce or separation judgment. This includes how one person can try to ask the court to enforce the order, in terms of financial or children's issues.
Parent Terms: Problems after a final divorce, separation, or annulment judgment [FA-06-07-00-00], Enforcing a court's judgment [CO-07-05-03-00]

Title: Modifying a divorce or separation judgment
Definition: This category concerns how a person may try to change a final judgment after the end of a divorce or separation process.
Parent Terms: Problems after a final divorce, separation, or annulment judgment [FA-06-07-00-00]

Title: Domestic Violence and Abuse
Definition: This category concerns options for people dealing with domestic violence and abuse, including getting protective orders, enforcing them, understanding abuse, reporting abuse, and getting resources and status if there is abuse.
Parent Terms: Family [FA-00-00-00-00], Crime and Prisons [CR-00-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-00037], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1370100], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1370199], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1420100], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [37]

Title: Getting a restraining or protection order
Definition:
This category concerns the options, process, and limitations of getting a restraining order (otherwise known as a protection order, order of protection, or other terms) to address domestic violence and abuse.
It could also be for non-domestic harassment, abuse, or stalking (by a person outside of one's family or household).
Parent Terms: Domestic Violence and Abuse [FA-07-00-00-00], Going to court and dealing with procedure [CO-07-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1370101], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1370106]

Title: Initial filing for a protection order
Definition: This category concerns how to initiate a court action to get a protection (or restraining) order. This may also be known as 'initial pleadings' or 'filing a petition' with the court, in order to open a case and begin the process of getting a protection order.
Parent Terms: Getting a restraining or protection order [FA-07-01-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1370110], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1370119]

Title: Modifying a protection order's complaint
Definition: This category concerns how a person can modify the original pleading (or complaint) that they had submitted to the court, in order to initiate the process of getting a protection (or restraining) order.
Parent Terms: Getting a restraining or protection order [FA-07-01-00-00]

Title: Modifying a temporary protection order
Definition: This category concerns the options, process, and consequences of modifying a temporary protection (or restraining) order that a person has gotten through the courts.
Parent Terms: Getting a restraining or protection order [FA-07-01-00-00]

Title: Extending a protection order
Definition: This category concerns how a person can extend a 'final' protection (or restraining) order, to last for a longer period of time, past the current expiration date.
Parent Terms: Getting a restraining or protection order [FA-07-01-00-00]

Title: Modifying or ending a final protection order
Definition: This category concerns how a person can change or terminate the finalized protection (or restraining) order. This may be done by the person who has the order against them, to ask the court to limit the order because it is too broad or burdensome.
Parent Terms: Getting a restraining or protection order [FA-07-01-00-00]

Title: Getting a protection order for non-domestic abuse or threats
Definition: This category covers how to get a protection order, sometimes called a Personal Safety Order, against someone who is abusing, stalking, threatening, or harassing you -- when that person is not a family or household member, or not someone you have had a romantic relationship with.
Parent Terms: Getting a restraining or protection order [FA-07-01-00-00], Harassment by another person [TO-05-00-00-00]

Title: Employment issues around domestic violence
Definition: This category concerns problems a person might face with employment, when they are dealing with domestic violence. This includes options to take leave to deal with family circumstances, providing security at work, and other issues that arise at a current job because of domestic violence problems.
Parent Terms: Domestic Violence and Abuse [FA-07-00-00-00], Problems at a Current Job [WO-02-00-00-00]

Title: Custody issues around Domestic Violence
Definition: This category concerns child custody issues that arise when there is a domestic violence or abuse situation in a family. It includes issues where a parent may be abusing a child, or when they have domestic violence-related court orders against them.
Parent Terms: Child Custody, Parenting Plans, and Visitation [FA-04-00-00-00], Domestic Violence and Abuse [FA-07-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1370140], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1370149]

Title: Financial Issues around Domestic Violence
Definition: This category concerns financial support that one family member may get from another, related to domestic violence -- including around child support, spousal support, damages, public benefits, or other financial issues.
Parent Terms: Domestic Violence and Abuse [FA-07-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1370120], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1370129]

Title: Child Support and Domestic Violence
Definition: This category concerns issues when one parent wants to get child support payments safely from another parent, when there has been domestic abuse towards the parent or child. This includes issues around waiving of the usual requirements or pursuing the child support in a more protective way.
Parent Terms: Financial Issues around Domestic Violence [FA-07-04-00-00], Child Support [FA-05-00-00-00]

Title: Damages and financial compensation for domestic violence
Definition: This category concerns options for survivors of domestic abuse to possibly sue the perpetrator in civil court to get financial compensation (damages) for physical injuries or other losses they experienced because of the abuse. This includes possible lawsuits for intentional torts of assault, battery, or intentional infliction of emotional distress.
Parent Terms: Financial Issues around Domestic Violence [FA-07-04-00-00], Claiming Money (Damages) in a lawsuit [CO-07-07-00-00]

Title: Spousal Support and Domestic Violence
Definition: This category concerns how domestic abuse affects the payment of spousal support, whether it is the person committing the abuse that is the person with obligations to pay, or is supposed to receive the payments. This includes possible 'rebuttable presumptions' that a person convicted of domestic violence should not receive a spousal support award. It also includes how domestic abuse may factor into a court's determination to grant interim or final spousal support to one spouse.
Parent Terms: Financial Issues around Domestic Violence [FA-07-04-00-00], Spousal Support, Alimony, and Separate Maintenance [FA-06-01-00-00]

Title: TANF Benefits exceptions for domestic violence victims
Definition: This category concerns exemptions that domestic violence victims may have when in the Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) public benefits program. This includes possible exemption from TANF's usual work and training requirements, like those as part of the IMPACT program. It might also mean that there is an additional extension of TANF benefits possible.
Parent Terms: Financial Issues around Domestic Violence [FA-07-04-00-00], Requirements to stay on TANF benefits [BE-02-02-10-00]

Title: Domestic Violence issues during a public health emergency
Definition: This category concerns issues that might arise in the unique situation of a public health emergency, where there are stay-at-home orders, quarantines, and other restrictions due to a disease. This includes issues and resources during the COVID-19 emergency.
Parent Terms: Domestic Violence and Abuse [FA-07-00-00-00], Public Health Emergency issues [DI-08-00-00-00]

Title: Drug and Alcohol Treatment related to Domestic Violence
Definition: This category concerns options and process for substance abuse treatment for those involved in a domestic violence situation. It might be for the victim of the abuse, or the person committing the abuse (or concerned that they might commit abuse). This is for issues with substances like alcohol and drugs.
Parent Terms: Domestic Violence and Abuse [FA-07-00-00-00]

Title: Defining what constitutes domestic violence and abuse
Definition: This category concerns the legal definitions of what kinds of actions rise to the level of 'domestic violence' or 'domestic abuse'.
Parent Terms: Domestic Violence and Abuse [FA-07-00-00-00]

Title: Firearms and other Weapons and domestic violence
Definition: This category concerns legal options and restrictions that might apply when an abusive partner has (or is trying to access) guns, firearms, and other weapons. This includes how protective orders/restraining orders affect who can purchase or possess firearms and ammunition, and laws that prohibit people who have been convicted of certain domestic violence crimes from buying or owning firearms. It also includes notifications that domestic violence offenders must receive from governments about federal firearm prohibitions under the Violence Against Woman Act (2005). Some states have additional restrictions on access to weapons by those who have been convicted of domestic violence, or who have protective orders against them.
Parent Terms: Domestic Violence and Abuse [FA-07-00-00-00], Firearms licenses [G0-01-01-00-00]

Title: Enforcing a protection order
Definition: This category concerns how a person, law enforcement, and others can enforce a restraining or protection order. This includes concerns about government actors (including law enforcement and courts) giving 'Full Faith and Credit' to protection order issued by other jurisdictions.
Parent Terms: Domestic Violence and Abuse [FA-07-00-00-00], Getting a restraining or protection order [FA-07-01-00-00]

Title: Housing Discrimination and Domestic Violence
Definition: This category concerns options and protections for victims of domestic violence who are facing housing discrimination. This could include being evicted from housing, or denied admission to housing, because of violence that has occurred.
Parent Terms: Domestic Violence and Abuse [FA-07-00-00-00], Discrimination around housing [HO-01-00-00-00]

Title: Responding to a restraining order
Definition: This category covers the options and procedures a person has, if someone has filed for a restraining order or protection order against them.
Parent Terms: Domestic Violence and Abuse [FA-07-00-00-00]

Title: Emancipation of a minor
Definition: This category concerns issues around a minor who requests to be emancipated from their parents, contesting it, rights afterward, and other situations of children (including adult children) breaking away from their parents.
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1430000], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [43]

Title: Foster Care
Definition: About getting foster care for children, and family members' rights in a foster care situation.

Title: Marriages and civil unions
Definition: This category is about the process of married or forming civil unions, getting a certificate to prove the union, and changing names for it.
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1390400], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1390499]

Title: Common Law Marriage
Definition: This category concerns the definition, options, and process of a common law marriage -- in which a couple lives together for a period of time, hold them out to others as 'being married', but have not formally gone through the process of getting a marriage license. Not all states recognize common law marriages, and they have different requirements for establishing this type of marriage.
Parent Terms: Marriages and civil unions [FA-10-00-00-00]

Title: Name or Gender Change
Definition: This category concerns options and process of changing one's name or gender assignment.
Parent Terms: Family [FA-00-00-00-00], Government Services [GO-00-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1340100], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1340199], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [LS002-00034], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [34]

Title: Name Change of an Adult
Definition: This category concerns how an adult can legally change their name.
Parent Terms: Name or Gender Change [FA-11-00-00-00], Marriages and civil unions [FA-10-00-00-00]

Title: Name Change of a Child
Definition: This category concerns how a child (a minor under the age of 18) can have their name changed.
Parent Terms: Name or Gender Change [FA-11-00-00-00]

Title: Gender Change of an Adult
Definition: This category concerns the process and options for an adult to change their gender legally.
Parent Terms: Name or Gender Change [FA-11-00-00-00]

Title: Gender Change of a Child
Definition: This category concerns how to change the gender of a child (or a minor, under the age of 18), including how to do so if you are a guardian or a dependency attorney for the child.
Parent Terms: Name or Gender Change [FA-11-00-00-00]

Title: Paternity
Definition: This category is about establishing paternity of a child, or responding to a paternity case filed against one.
Taxonomies: Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-00036], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1360100], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1360199], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [36]

Title: Acknowledging paternity
Definition: This category concerns how a person can acknowledge paternity of a child.
Parent Terms: Paternity [FA-12-00-00-00]

Title: Blood Tests to determine paternity
Definition: This category concerns how to use or respond to requests to take a blood tests to determine paternity of a child.
Parent Terms: Paternity [FA-12-00-00-00]

Title: Contested Paternity
Definition: This category concerns how to contest paternity or to respond when someone else is contesting paternity.
Parent Terms: Paternity [FA-12-00-00-00]

Title: Mediation and Alternative Dispute Resolution for family
Definition: This category covers options and processes for alternative dispute resolution to deal with family issues.
Parent Terms: Family [FA-00-00-00-00], Alternative Dispute Resolution, Mediation, and Settlements [CO-07-01-00-00]

Title: Parental Rights (and Termination)
Definition: This category is about terminating parental rights, reporting child abuse or neglect, prisoners' parental rights, and reunification services for parents and children.
Taxonomies: Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [35], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1310502], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1490400]

Title: Terminating Parental Rights
Definition: This category concerns how parental rights can be terminated. This includes the options and process of getting a court order that permanently ends the legal parent-child relationship. The termination might be based on abandonment, neglect, unfit parents, risk of injury to the child, sexual assault, or other issues.
Parent Terms: Parental Rights (and Termination) [FA-14-00-00-00], Emancipation of a minor [FA-08-00-00-00], Adopting a Child [FA-01-01-00-00], Domestic Violence and Abuse [FA-07-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1350100], Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-00035]

Title: Teen Parents' Rights and Obligations
Definition: This category concerns the rights that teenage (and potentially minor-age) parents have, in regards to their child. It includes questions about emancipation, relationships with the teen parents' family, custody, and support obligations when one or both of the parents is teenage. It covers state laws that determine if a parent is old enough to have to pay child support.
Parent Terms: Parental Rights (and Termination) [FA-14-00-00-00]

Title: Child Abuse and Neglect
Definition: This category covers issues related to suspected child abuse and neglect. It covers how investigations are carried out, what rights and procedures there are, how orders or plans might be issued, and how decisions are made.
Parent Terms: Parental Rights (and Termination) [FA-14-00-00-00], Domestic Violence and Abuse [FA-07-00-00-00]

Title: Sealing a record for child abuse or neglect
Definition: This category covers options and processes for a person who has a record of child abuse or neglect with an agency like Child Protective Services (CPS).
Parent Terms: Child Abuse and Neglect [FA-14-03-00-00], Criminal Records [CR-06-00-00-00]

Title: Elder Abuse
Definition: This category is about financial or physical abuse of elders, potentially by another family member. It could also cover evictions and rental house issues for the elderly, or scams directed at the elderly. This abuse could involve physical, sexual emotional, financial, or verbal behavior. It could also involve withholding access to food, money, or necessities, or exerting control over where a person goes, sees, and does.
Parent Terms: Family [FA-00-00-00-00], Domestic Violence and Abuse [FA-07-00-00-00], Getting a Conservatorship or Guardianship of an Adult [ES-03-02-01-00]

Title: Taking Care of Sick or Disabled Family
Definition: This category is about getting financial and work support, including leave, to take care of a sick or disabled family member, including around pregnancy. It also includes issues around estate planning, trusts, and other financial protections for another family member who may have special needs, health conditions, or other issues.
Parent Terms: Family [FA-00-00-00-00], Disability issues and rights [HE-01-10-00-00]

Title: Family members with money, criminal, and other issues
Definition: This category covers issues that a person might have related to a family member who is involved in criminal activity, money and debt problems, and other scenarios that might carry liability or dangers for the person. It covers issues about whether a person might be responsible for a family member's debt, problematic behavior, crimes, or other issues, and what obligations a person has if their family member is involved in irresponsible or criminal behavior.

Title: Financial exploitation of a person
Definition:
This category covers problems when a person is being financially exploited, with their money being intentionally misappropriated or misused. This could be the financial exploitation of an elderly person or a person with a mental impairment. 
The exploitation could be done by a family member, spouse or loved one, friend, or caretaker.
Parent Terms: Family [FA-00-00-00-00], Elder Abuse [FA-15-00-00-00]

Title: Firearms licenses
Definition: This category concerns license process, eligibility, and rules for someone who wants to purchase or posses a firearm (gun).
Parent Terms: Licenses for Driving, Business, Fishing, Guns, etc. [GO-01-00-00-00]

Title: Government Services
Definition: This category covers services that people request from the government, including licenses for firearms, businesses, and hunting, as well as requests for information, and other privileges from the government.
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2090000], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2090099]

Title: Licenses for Driving, Business, Fishing, Guns, etc.
Definition: This category concerns licenses that an individual or business might want to get from the government, to be able to legally drive, fish, use a gun, or do other activities that the government regulates.
Parent Terms: Government Services [GO-00-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-00093], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1930000], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1930099], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [93]

Title: Getting information and records from the government
Definition: This category concerns getting access to government records about oneself. This includes vital records, identification documents, passports, and birth certificates. It also includes name changes. It also includes accessing information about traffic tickets, bench warrants, and other records the government has about ones' alleged violations of law.
Parent Terms: Government Services [GO-00-00-00-00]

Title: Freedom of Information (FOIA) to request government info
Definition: This category is about how a person might request information from the government through a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request.
Parent Terms: Getting information and records from the government [GO-02-00-00-00]

Title: Voting and Elections
Definition: This category concerns a person's issues with participating in elections or in the law governing elections. This includes voting rights, voting systems, and election districting.
Parent Terms: Government Services [GO-00-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2060000], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2060099]

Title: Voting Systems, Ballots, and Rules
Definition: This category covers rules about how a person can submit a ballot to vote in an election, including rules about mail-in ballots, in-person voting, provisional ballots, and other procedural concerns about participating in an election.
Parent Terms: Voting and Elections [GO-03-00-00-00]

Title: Districting and Gerrymandering
Definition: This category covers how districts are created for elections, including concerns about gerrymandering or manipulation, and how to challenge districting plans.
Parent Terms: Voting and Elections [GO-03-00-00-00]

Title: Dealing with different branches of government
Definition: This category covers how a person can understand and deal with different levels and branches of the government.
Parent Terms: Government Services [GO-00-00-00-00]

Title: Dealing with federal agencies
Definition: This category covers how a person can understand and deal with the agencies of the federal government.
Parent Terms: Dealing with different branches of government [GO-05-00-00-00]

Title: Dealing with municipal government and ordinances
Definition: This category is about how a person can understand and deal with local, municipal government and ordinances.
Parent Terms: Dealing with different branches of government [GO-05-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2090200], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [97]

Title: Dealing with state and local agencies
Definition: This category is about how a person can understand and deal with state and local government agencies.
Parent Terms: Dealing with different branches of government [GO-05-00-00-00]

Title: Dealing with state legislatures and courts
Definition: This category is about how a person can understand and deal with state legislatures and courts.
Parent Terms: Dealing with different branches of government [GO-05-00-00-00]

Title: City regulations of renting a home
Definition: This category covers local city regulations of who and how a private home can be rented.
Parent Terms: Local regulations of rental housing [HO-06-06-00-00]

Title: Military Service-members' Protections against Foreclosure
Definition: This category concerns defenses and protections that a military service-member can use if they face a foreclosure on their home. This includes local state law, and the federal law, the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act (SCRA), which grants benefits and protections to service-members, depending on when they took out a mortgage loan. It can protect the homeowner from a default judgment, get them a delay, reduce interest rates, and other benefits.
Parent Terms: Defenses against a Foreclosure [HO-08-01-00-00], Legal protections for military [VE-06-00-00-00], Public Benefits for Veterans and Military [BE-06-00-00-00]

Title: Liens on a Home
Definition: This category concerns liens taken out on one's home. When borrowing money to pay for a home, one can use a lien to have the property serve as collateral. If one fails to meet payments or other requirements, the lien allows the lender to foreclose on the home and take the property. This might include mortgage liens.
Parent Terms: Owning a Home [HO-09-00-00-00], Liens on Property  [MO-12-01-07-00], Mortgages and other financing for a home [HO-09-05-00-00]

Title: Title to a home
Definition: This category concerns how to have a 'Title' to one's home, to show that one owns a home. This includes issues on how couples can arrange for multiple people to have 'title' to a home, how to change title to a home, or how to clear title one's home. This also includes issues around title when buying or selling a home, like needs to clear title to home, do title searches, get title insurance, and other issues.
Parent Terms: Owning a Home [HO-09-00-00-00], Buying a Home [HO-04-00-00-00]

Title: Health
Definition:
This category covers issues with accessing health services, paying for medical care, getting public benefits for health care, protecting one's rights in medical settings, and other issues related to health.

Scenarios in this category include billing, the inability to access or other problems getting health insurance, the denial of an interpreter in a medical setting, issues with debt collection or financial assistance, and payment for needed equipment, procedures, or other services.
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1590000], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1590099], Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-00066], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [59]

Title: Care for a specific condition or disability
Definition: This category covers what rights and options a person has, when they are dealing with a specific kind of disease, condition, or health care need. This could include AIDS/HIV, abortion, alcoholism or drug dependency, cancers, and other problems.

Title: Mental Health
Definition: This category covers issues with mental health treatment, insurance coverage, rights, commitment procedures, community programs, guardianship, and other problems and rules.
Parent Terms: Care for a specific condition or disability [HE-01-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1820000], Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-00082], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1820099], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [82]

Title: Commitment to a mental health facility
Definition: This category covers how a person may be committed to a mental health facility, either voluntarily or involuntarily. It covers what rights a person has, what other people's ability to commit them are, and what options or procedures must be followed.
Parent Terms: Mental Health [HE-01-01-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1820100], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1820199]

Title: Voluntary commitment to a mental health facility
Definition: This category covers situations when a person is committed to a mental health facility with their voluntary consent. It covers the procedures of commitment, and a person's rights.
Parent Terms: Commitment to a mental health facility [HE-01-01-01-00]

Title: Involuntary Commitment to a mental health facility
Definition: This category covers the procedures that must be followed to commit a person to a mental health facility against their will, as an involuntary commitment. This could also be called an emergency hold, 72-hour hold, a pick-up, an involuntary hold, an emergency commitment, a psychiatric hold, a temporary detention order, or an emergency petition.
Parent Terms: Commitment to a mental health facility [HE-01-01-01-00]

Title: Rights when being committed to a mental health facility
Definition: This category covers what rights a person has if they are being committed to a mental health facility, either voluntarily or involuntarily.
Parent Terms: Commitment to a mental health facility [HE-01-01-01-00], Mental Health Rights [RI-09-00-00-00]

Title: Community programs for mental health
Definition: This category covers options and rights to community programs that can assist with mental health needs.
Parent Terms: Mental Health [HE-01-01-00-00]

Title: Least Restrictive Alternative Standard for mental health care
Definition: This category covers what standards there are for mental health care, particularly a legal standard to use the least restrictive alternative in treating the person. This could also be part of a court's assessment that a person should go to an Assisted Outpatient Treatment facility is the least restrictive alternative for the person -- so that they should be ordered treatment at this facility.
Parent Terms: Mental Health [HE-01-01-00-00]

Title: Mental Health facilities and institutions
Definition: This category covers issues that a person might have with a mental health facility or institution. It could be about quality of care, infringement of rights, procedures to access care, or to raise complaints.
Parent Terms: Mental Health [HE-01-01-00-00]

Title: Mental Health Advanced Directive planning
Definition: This category covers how a person might set up a Mental Health Advanced Directive (MHAD) to plan for possible future needs or events. This includes what treatment or directions might be included, whether a service provider must follow it, and what a representative can do before or during a crisis.
Parent Terms: Mental Health [HE-01-01-00-00], Advance Directives about possible medical treatments [ES-05-01-00-00]

Title: HIV/AIDS care and rights
Definition: This category covers what people dealing with AIDS/HIV have in terms of protections and rights, and resources when dealing with health issues.
Parent Terms: Care for a specific condition or disability [HE-01-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1590200], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1590203]

Title: Health care for those with HIV/AIDS
Definition: This category covers what resources and rights a person with HIV/AIDS has.
Parent Terms: HIV/AIDS care and rights [HE-01-02-00-00]

Title: Abortion care and rights
Definition: This category covers what rights or limits a person has to access abortion care, and what resources there might be to receive medical care.
Parent Terms: Care for a specific condition or disability [HE-01-00-00-00]

Title: Alcoholism and Substance Abuse
Definition: This category covers options for treatment, services, and protections for those dealing with alcoholism, drug dependency, or other substance abuse.
Parent Terms: Care for a specific condition or disability [HE-01-00-00-00]

Title: Disability protections for substance use disorders
Definition: This category covers whether a person might be considered as having a disorder, like a substance use disorder (SUD) or opioid use disorder (OUD), and what disability protections they might qualify for. This includes possible protections from discrimination, and right to reasonable accommodation for their disability.
Parent Terms: Alcoholism and Substance Abuse [HE-01-04-00-00], Disability Rights and Discrimination [RI-03-00-00-00]

Title: Birth Control and Sterlization
Definition: This category covers options, rights, and protection a person has in regards to birth control or sterilization procedures.
Parent Terms: Care for a specific condition or disability [HE-01-00-00-00]

Title: Black Lung Disease (Pneumoconiosis) benefits
Definition: This category covers medical and financial benefits and protections for a person (like, a coal miner) who suffers from black lung disease, or pneumoconiosis. It could also cover the benefits to the survivors of the person who died from the disease. These benefits are provided for under the Black Lung Benefits Act.
Parent Terms: Care for a specific condition or disability [HE-01-00-00-00]

Title: Breast and Cervical Cancer
Definition: This category covers screening, treatment, and options for women facing possible breast or cervical cancer.
Parent Terms: Care for a specific condition or disability [HE-01-00-00-00]

Title: Counseling and social work needs
Definition: This category covers what options and rights a person might have to get services from a counselor or a social worker.
Parent Terms: Care for a specific condition or disability [HE-01-00-00-00]

Title: Immunization and Vaccines
Definition: This category covers options, rights, and obligations around getting immunizations and vaccines.
Parent Terms: Care for a specific condition or disability [HE-01-00-00-00], Public Health Emergency issues [DI-08-00-00-00]

Title: Disability issues and rights
Definition:
This category covers issues that people with a physical or mental disability may be dealing with, including around education, rights, work, estate planning, or other issues.

The scenarios in this category include the denial of state or federal benefits, denial of access to government programs, denial or limited access to public businesses, mishandled Social Security benefits, a court order requiring an unwanted guardian who provided poor treatment, and being placed in a mental health or longterm care facility
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1840000], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1840099], Wikidata Taxonomy [Q15978181]

Title: Health public benefits for a person with a disability
Definition: This category covers what options a person with a disability has to get public benefits to cover the cost of their medical care. This could include coverage through Medicaid, Medicare, or state programs.
Parent Terms: Disability public benefits [BE-01-00-00-00], Health public benefits and medical assistance programs [BE-03-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1840500], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1840599]

Title: Medicaid coverage for a person with a disability
Definition: This category covers what Medicaid benefits a person with a disability might be eligible for, and how they can access this coverage. This includes how to apply to get it, how it works with other insurance, what protections against discrimination works, and what special management plans might be.
Parent Terms: Health public benefits for a person with a disability [HE-01-10-01-00], Medicaid health coverage [BE-03-02-00-00]

Title: Medicare coverage for a person with a disability
Definition: This category covers what Medicare benefits a person with a disability might be eligible for, and how they can access this coverage. This includes how to apply to get it, how it works with other insurance, what protections against discrimination works, and what special management plans might be.
Parent Terms: Medicare health coverage [BE-03-03-00-00], Health public benefits for a person with a disability [HE-01-10-01-00]

Title: Mental Health Disabilities
Definition: This category covers situations when mental health issues are considered as disabilities, and what kinds of options, rights, and services people in this situation have to claim benefits and protect their well-being.
Parent Terms: Disability issues and rights [HE-01-10-00-00], Mental Health [HE-01-01-00-00]

Title: Disability services and resources
Definition: This category covers resources, services, and other options for assistance to people who are dealing with physical or mental disabilities.
Parent Terms: Disability issues and rights [HE-01-10-00-00], Care for a specific condition or disability [HE-01-00-00-00]

Title: Rights and discrimination around health care
Definition: This category covers what rights a person has to access health care, and to respond to discrimination when trying to seek out health services.
Parent Terms: Health [HE-00-00-00-00], Civil and Human Rights [RI-00-00-00-00]

Title: Language and cultural access to health care
Definition: This category covers what rights and options a person has to receive health care in a language that they can understand, and that is culturally appropriate to them.
Parent Terms: Rights and discrimination around health care [HE-02-00-00-00]

Title: Discrimination or Refusal to Treat a person
Definition: This category covers discrimination a person might face when seeking medical care, including possibly when the provider refuses to treat them. This covers when doctors are obliged to provide services, or what a person can do if the health care provider says they have an objection to provide services to a certain patient (like women and LGBTQ individuals).
Parent Terms: Rights and discrimination around health care [HE-02-00-00-00]

Title: Duty to provide health care to low-income individuals
Definition: This category covers what duties a health care provider has to people who cannot afford to pay for medical care.
Parent Terms: Rights and discrimination around health care [HE-02-00-00-00]

Title: Minority groups' access to health care
Definition: This category covers options and rights that members of minority groups have to get quality health care, and to deal with possible discrimination or low-quality care.
Parent Terms: Rights and discrimination around health care [HE-02-00-00-00], Racial Justice and discrimination [RI-18-00-00-00]

Title: Problems with medical or nursing home care
Definition: This category covers options, rights, and protections for a person who is unhappy with the quality of care they are receiving at a health facility or nursing home.

Title: Quality of care in a nursing home
Definition: This category covers rights and options for a person who is unhappy with the quality of care in a nursing home.
Parent Terms: Problems with medical or nursing home care [HE-03-00-00-00], Nursing Home Care and Assisted Living [HE-04-00-00-00]

Title: Complaining about medical services quality or cost
Definition: This category covers a person's options to complain about the quality or cost of medical services to an ombudsman, ombudsprogram, or consumer assistance group at a facility.
Parent Terms: Problems with medical or nursing home care [HE-03-00-00-00]

Title: Nursing Home Care and Assisted Living
Definition: This category covers the options and rights a person has when getting care in nursing home or assisted living facility. This can also be called long-term health care facilities.
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1560100], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1560199], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [56]

Title: Discharge or transfer from a nursing home
Definition: This category covers whether and how a person can be transferred out of a nursing home or discharged from it. This includes issues around the consent of the person, and obligations of the nursing home around discharge or transfer.
Parent Terms: Nursing Home Care and Assisted Living [HE-04-00-00-00]

Title: Assisted Living or Board and Care homes
Definition: This category covers options for board and care homes or assisted living arrangements, to help support individuals who need support with medical care and daily activities.
Parent Terms: Nursing Home Care and Assisted Living [HE-04-00-00-00]

Title: Licensing of nursing homes
Definition: This category covers how to become licensed and look up whether a nursing home is licensed.
Parent Terms: Nursing Home Care and Assisted Living [HE-04-00-00-00], Business and Occupational Licenses [BU-01-00-00-00]

Title: Medical Records and Privacy
Definition: This category covers what options and protections a person has in regard to their medical data, records that doctors and hospitals might have about them, and what they can do if they think private data has been shared about them inappropriately. It also covers their ability to access their own medical record and share it with other providers or people.
Parent Terms: Health [HE-00-00-00-00], Privacy Rights and Protections [RI-12-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1592400], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1593100]

Title: Health issues from living conditions
Definition: This category covers health and legal issues that a person might face because of poor living conditions. This could be problems with bad air quality, mold, pests, asthma, lead poisoning, poor water and sewage, environmental waste, or other issues.
Parent Terms: Health [HE-00-00-00-00], Environmental Justice [EN-00-00-00-00], Problems with living conditions [HO-05-00-00-00]

Title: Workers with health or disability issues
Definition: This category concerns the issues that an employee or worker might face at work, if they have health problems or a disability.
Parent Terms: Health [HE-00-00-00-00], Problems at a Current Job [WO-02-00-00-00], Disability issues and rights [HE-01-10-00-00]

Title: Disability Insurance coverage
Definition: This category covers how a person who is dealing with a disability can get insurance coverage for financial support, including through their employer. This could cover injuries, illnesses, pregnancies, and other situations when a person cannot earn a living and needs financial support. This could be about how to get insurance, how to make claims, how to dispute denials, and how long the coverage lasts.
Parent Terms: Workers with health or disability issues [HE-07-00-00-00], Insurance [MO-07-00-00-00], Taking Time off Work at Current Job [WO-02-14-00-00], Disability issues and rights [HE-01-10-00-00]

Title: Housing
Definition: This category covers issues with paying your rent or mortgage, landlord-tenant issues, housing subsidies and public housing, eviction, and other problems with your apartment, mobile home, or house.
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1690000], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1690099], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [66]

Title: Discrimination around housing
Definition: This category covers how a person may be protected from discrimination when searching for or living in housing. This could be for renting or buying a house. It covers what protections the law may give, for people in different demographic groups.
Parent Terms: Housing [HO-00-00-00-00], Civil and Human Rights [RI-00-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1660000], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1660099], Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-00066], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [66]

Title: Federal Protections against housing discrimination (Fair Housing Act)
Definition: This category covers the federal rights and protections people under the federal Fair Housing Act have when they are renting and buying a home, getting a mortgage, seeking housing assistance, or engaged in other housing-related actions. It includes protections based on a person's race, color, national origin, religion, sex, familial status, and disability. This category covers when these protections apply, how to make use of them, and what happens if you're accused of violating them.
Parent Terms: Discrimination around housing [HO-01-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1660100], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1660199]

Title: State protections against housing discrimination
Definition: This category covers a state's protections to a person looking to rent a home, buy a home, get housing assistance, or in other housing-related activities. These laws may vary state by state, and this category covers what a state's protections are and how to make use of them (or how to respond if you are accused of violating them).
Parent Terms: Discrimination around housing [HO-01-00-00-00]

Title: Local protections against housing discrimination
Definition: This category covers a local city, county, parish or municipality's protections to a person looking to rent a home, buy a home, get housing assistance, or in other housing-related activities. These laws may vary by local jurisdiction, and this category covers what the local jurisdiction's protections are and how to make use of them (or how to respond if you are accused of violating them).
Parent Terms: Discrimination around housing [HO-01-00-00-00]

Title: Housing discrimination based on race
Definition: This category concerns the legal options and rights a person may have if they have experienced discrimination around housing based on their race. This could be when they were trying to rent a home, get housing assistance, take out a mortgage, buy a home, or other housing-related activities. It includes the practice of redlining.
Parent Terms: Discrimination around housing [HO-01-00-00-00]

Title: Discriminatory housing lending (or Redlining)
Definition: This category covers issues around minorities being treated differently, regarding access to credit or mortgages to buy homes, or being targeted with predatory lending for homes. This could be in regards to discriminatory rent-to-own schemes, or unfair mortgage lending in minority communities. This category covers legal options, prohibitions, and types of relief for redlining.
Parent Terms: Discrimination around housing [HO-01-00-00-00]

Title: Housing discrimination based on disability
Definition: This category covers protections, rights, and options for people who are concerned they may have been discriminated against based on their disability.
Parent Terms: Disability rights around housing [RI-03-01-00-00], Discrimination around housing [HO-01-00-00-00]

Title: Housing discrimination based on national origin
Definition: This category concerns the legal options and rights a person may have if they have experienced discrimination around housing based on their national origin or apparent ethnicity. This could be when they were trying to rent a home, get housing assistance, take out a mortgage, buy a home, or other housing-related activities. It includes the practice of redlining.
Parent Terms: Discrimination around housing [HO-01-00-00-00]

Title: Housing Discrimination based on gender or sexuality
Definition: This category concerns the legal options and rights a person may have if they have experienced discrimination around housing based on their gender or sexuality. This could be when they were trying to rent a home, get housing assistance, take out a mortgage, buy a home, or other housing-related activities.
Parent Terms: Discrimination around housing [HO-01-00-00-00], Women's Rights [RI-11-00-00-00], LGBTQ Rights [RI-06-00-00-00]

Title: Housing discrimination based on familial status (having children, being pregnant, or adopting)
Definition: This category concerns the legal options and rights a person may have if they have experienced discrimination around housing based on their having children, intending to have children, being pregnant, or in the process of adoption. This could be when they were trying to rent a home, get housing assistance, take out a mortgage, buy a home, or other housing-related activities.
Parent Terms: Discrimination around housing [HO-01-00-00-00], Adoption [FA-01-00-00-00]

Title: Housing discrimination based on religion
Definition: This category concerns the legal options and rights a person may have if they have experienced discrimination around housing based on their apparent or actual religion. This could be when they were trying to rent a home, get housing assistance, take out a mortgage, buy a home, or other housing-related activities.
Parent Terms: Discrimination around housing [HO-01-00-00-00], Religious Freedoms and Discrimination [RI-17-00-00-00]

Title: Housing discrimination based on source of income/voucher subsidies
Definition: This category covers discrimination that a person might face when trying to rent a home, based on the source of their income to pay for this home -- like a Section 8 or Housing Choice Voucher. This includes what a person may do to protect themselves against this kind of discrimination, what rights they have, and how they can assert their rights if they feel they are facing discrimination. This can be known as 'No Section 8' policies.
Parent Terms: Discrimination around housing [HO-01-00-00-00], Federally Subsidized Housing (including Section 8/Housing Choice Vouchers) [HO-03-03-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1660300], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1612100]

Title: Eviction from a home
Definition: This category is about landlords removing a tenant from a home property through a lawsuit or force, ways to counter an eviction, or being removed from a shelter, subsidized housing, a group home. It includes evictions from private rentals, subsidized homes, public housing, and housing with rent control.
Parent Terms: Housing [HO-00-00-00-00], Renting or leasing a home [HO-06-00-00-00]

Title: Eviction from a homeless shelter or group home
Definition: This category concerns issues a person might face when being evicted from a homeless shelter or group home, what defenses they might raise to stop the eviction, and other concerns.
Parent Terms: Eviction from a home [HO-02-00-00-00], Homelessness and Housing Insecurity [HO-13-00-00-00]

Title: Eviction from subsidized or public housing
Definition: This category concerns issues around a tenant being evicted from a home, which is supported through public funds. This could be evictions from Section 8 or federally subsidized housing; public housing; non-federal housing programs; or Rural Economy Community Development (formerly Farmers Home ) subsidized housing.
Parent Terms: Eviction from a home [HO-02-00-00-00], Housing Assistance, Public Housing, and Subsidized Housing [HO-03-00-00-00]

Title: Eviction from a home subsidized by Rural Economic and Community Development
Definition: This category concerns issues for tenants when facing eviction from housing subsidized by Rural Economic and Community Development (formerly Farmers Home Administration or FMHA). It includes the defenses and protections tenants have.
Parent Terms: Eviction from subsidized or public housing [HO-02-02-00-00], Rural rental assistance (formerly FMHA) programs [HO-03-04-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1690910], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1690919]

Title: Eviction from federally subsidized (Section 8) housing
Definition: This category concerns issues when a tenant is facing eviction from a home that is federally-subsidized or Section 8 housing. This includes the defenses that a tenant can raise, like problems with the notice or procedure; reasonable accommodation; or warrant of habitability defenses. It also concerns policies like the One-Strike policy that can lead to the eviction.
Parent Terms: Eviction from subsidized or public housing [HO-02-02-00-00], Federally Subsidized Housing (including Section 8/Housing Choice Vouchers) [HO-03-03-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1610400], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1610402]

Title: Eviction from public housing (with government landlord)
Definition: This category concerns issues when a tenant of a public housing unit -- with a government housing authority as the landlord -- faces eviction. It includes the defenses that the tenant can raise.
Parent Terms: Eviction from subsidized or public housing [HO-02-02-00-00], Public Housing (with government as landlord) [HO-03-02-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1640300], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1640399]

Title: One-Strike Eviction policies in public and subsidized housing
Definition: This category covers one-strike eviction policies that people living in public federally subsidized (like, Section 8) housing might face. This covers the details of this policy, who it applies to, and what kinds of behavior might count under it. It also covers how a person might contest an eviction based on the policy.
Parent Terms: Eviction from subsidized or public housing [HO-02-02-00-00]

Title: Eviction from private rental housing (not public or subsidized)
Definition: This category concerns issues around eviction from a privately rented home, or other housing that is not federally subsidized, public housing, or supported through government programs. It concerns  the process that landlords can use to remove tenants from housing, how eviction cases proceed in courts, and defenses that tenants can raise.
Parent Terms: Eviction from a home [HO-02-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1630300], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1630399]

Title: Going to court for Eviction and Landlord-Tenant issues
Definition: This category covers how courts work when hearing an eviction (or unlawful detainer) lawsuit between a landlord and a tenant. This includes the rules, processes, options, and other procedural issues that people may need to understand to protect themselves during this kind of court proceeding.
Parent Terms: Going to court and dealing with procedure [CO-07-00-00-00], Eviction from a home [HO-02-00-00-00]

Title: Being a defendant in an eviction lawsuit
Definition: This category covers issues and options for being a defendant in an eviction or unlawful detainer lawsuit. These options, obligations, and processes change depending on local state and city jurisdictions.
Parent Terms: Going to court for Eviction and Landlord-Tenant issues [HO-02-03-02-00], Being a Defendant in a lawsuit (being sued) [TO-04-03-00-00]

Title: Being a plaintiff in an eviction lawsuit
Definition: This category is about the requirements, options, and procedures that a landlord must follow while a plaintiff in an eviction (or unlawful detainer) lawsuit.
Parent Terms: Going to court for Eviction and Landlord-Tenant issues [HO-02-03-02-00]

Title: Requesting a Jury Trial in an eviction lawsuit
Definition: This category covers if and how a person can request that their eviction lawsuit be heard by a jury (rather than just by a judge).
Parent Terms: Going to court for Eviction and Landlord-Tenant issues [HO-02-03-02-00]

Title: Appealing an eviction lawsuit's judgment
Definition: This category covers how a tenant or landlord can appeal the judge's final decisions or orders in an eviction lawsuit.
Parent Terms: Going to court for Eviction and Landlord-Tenant issues [HO-02-03-02-00]

Title: Nonpayment of Rent eviction case procedure
Definition: This category covers how a court process for an eviction based on nonpayment of rent works, including if a tenant can be sided, how they must be given notice, if they are able to pay back rent to make the lawsuit end, what defenses they might have, and what possible judgments and outcomes may be.
Parent Terms: Going to court for Eviction and Landlord-Tenant issues [HO-02-03-02-00], Rent charges, increases, and control [HO-06-02-00-00], Problems with paying rent [HO-06-07-00-00]

Title: Holdover eviction cases
Definition: This category covers a certain type of eviction lawsuit, a holdover case. These are more complicated than nonpayment of rent eviction cases. They could involve the landlord trying to remove a tenant who is not a direct tenant (like a roommate), or trying to remove a tenant for lease violations or other issues.
Parent Terms: Going to court for Eviction and Landlord-Tenant issues [HO-02-03-02-00]

Title: Canceling (or setting aside) an Eviction Order
Definition: This category covers options that a tenant might have after a court has ruled in an eviction case, ordering on the side of the landlord that they can remove the tenant from the home. This includes how to file a motion to set aside (or cancel) the eviction order, based on a legal reason why the order should never have been issued. This might be for problems with how the case procedure went, landlord fraud, mistake or surprise, new evidence, or that the tenant has already moved out.
Parent Terms: Going to court for Eviction and Landlord-Tenant issues [HO-02-03-02-00], Tenants' rights and options after an eviction [HO-02-05-00-00]

Title: Jurisdiction issues around an eviction case
Definition: This category covers which level and geographical area of court has jurisdiction to hear an eviction case between a landlord and tenant.
Parent Terms: Going to court for Eviction and Landlord-Tenant issues [HO-02-03-02-00], Court's Jurisdiction to hear a case [CO-07-03-04-00]

Title: Paying to dismiss an eviction case
Definition: This category covers a defendant's options in an eviction case, to potentially pay the plaintiff back-rent and other costs to have the case dismissed. This includes whether this right exists, how it works, and what happens if a landlord resists taking the payment.
Parent Terms: Eviction from private rental housing (not public or subsidized) [HO-02-03-00-00], Defenses to stop or delay an eviction [HO-02-04-00-00], Being a defendant in an eviction lawsuit [HO-02-03-02-01], Nonpayment of Rent eviction case procedure [HO-02-03-02-05]

Title: Discovery Requests and Responses in eviction lawsuit
Definition: This category covers how litigants or their attorneys can respond to discovery requests they receive in an eviction lawsuit, or how they can request or propound discovery from another side.
Parent Terms: Going to court for Eviction and Landlord-Tenant issues [HO-02-03-02-00], Discovery process to get evidence from other side [CO-07-09-00-00]

Title: Preparing for an Eviction Trial
Definition: This category covers how a litigant or their attorney can prepare for a trial in their eviction case. This can include understanding how court will proceed, what evidence or testimony is admissible, and how to raise defenses or counterclaims. It can also include preparation of binders, jury instructions, and other materials for the trial.
Parent Terms: Going to court for Eviction and Landlord-Tenant issues [HO-02-03-02-00]

Title: Settling an Eviction Lawsuit
Definition: This category covers how a litigant or their attorney can prepare for negotiations and a settlement of an eviction lawsuit, so that the case ends without going to trial. This can involve preparing for negotiation, setting settlement terms, reviewing a possible settlement, entering the settlement to the court, and moving forward.
Parent Terms: Going to court for Eviction and Landlord-Tenant issues [HO-02-03-02-00], Settlements, Mediation, and Diversion from Eviction [HO-02-09-00-00]

Title: Answering an Eviction Lawsuit
Definition: This category covers how an eviction lawsuit defendant can answer the lawsuit, often through a formal written Answer submitted to the court.
Parent Terms: Going to court for Eviction and Landlord-Tenant issues [HO-02-03-02-00], Filing and Serving pleadings, forms, and court paperwork [CO-07-12-00-00]

Title: Going to small claims court for eviction-related case
Definition: This category covers how a landlord or a tenant might go to small claims court for a problem related to an eviction or landlord-tenant issue.
Parent Terms: Going to court for Eviction and Landlord-Tenant issues [HO-02-03-02-00], Going to Small Claims court [MO-10-01-00-00]

Title: Defenses to stop or delay an eviction
Definition: This category concerns the legal defenses and other strategies that a tenant can use, to stop an eviction action or delay the removal from their home. This includes defenses that people in particular housing (subsidized, public, privately rented housing). It also includes the defenses and protections that particular groups (like veterans) might have.
Parent Terms: Eviction from a home [HO-02-00-00-00], Going to court for Eviction and Landlord-Tenant issues [HO-02-03-02-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1640320], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1610429], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1690911], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1690913]

Title: Notice and Procedural defenses against an eviction
Definition: This category is about defenses that a tenant might raise when they are facing eviction, around whether they were given adequate notice before the lawsuit was filed, if enough time passed between the notice and the lawsuit's filing, or if there were other procedural problems with how the lawsuit and hearing proceeded.
Parent Terms: Defenses to stop or delay an eviction [HO-02-04-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1610421], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1690912], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1640310], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1630304], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1630313]

Title: Reasonable Accommodation for a disability defenses against an eviction
Definition: This category covers how a tenant may defend themselves against an eviction if there is an issue of 'reasonable accommodation', for when the tenant has engaged in behavior related to their disability. If the landlord is able to alter their policies and rules to accommodate the tenant's disability, they must make this accommodation. This could include accommodation of wheelchairs, service or support animals, time needed to get assistance or treatment, or other issues. This category covers how to ask for reasonable accommodation and use it as a defense in a court action.
Parent Terms: Disability rights around housing [RI-03-01-00-00], Defenses to stop or delay an eviction [HO-02-04-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1610422], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1840103], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1630314], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1640330]

Title: Living conditions (habitability) defenses against an eviction
Definition: This category covers the defenses a tenant can raise in an eviction, about problems with their living conditions. This may also be referred to as Warranty of Habitability defenses.
Parent Terms: Defenses to stop or delay an eviction [HO-02-04-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1690914], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1630316], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1610423], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1640340]

Title: Military service-members' protections around eviction
Definition: This category concerns the protections and defenses that a military service-member has, when they or their dependents are facing eviction from a home. The Servicemember's Civil Relief Act (SCRA) protects dependents from being evicted while a service member is serving their country.
Parent Terms: Defenses to stop or delay an eviction [HO-02-04-00-00], Public Benefits for Veterans and Military [BE-06-00-00-00], Legal protections for military [VE-06-00-00-00]

Title: Title and ownership defenses against an eviction
Definition: This category covers issues a tenant may raise if sued for eviction, which challenges the landlord's claim to have title or ownership of the home. This might be called a Claim of Title defense.
Parent Terms: Defenses to stop or delay an eviction [HO-02-04-00-00]

Title: Retaliatory Eviction defenses against an eviction
Definition: This category covers how a tenant may defend themselves against an eviction action that they believe was filed in retaliation for exercising their rights as a tenant. This could be for having reported housing code violations, complaining about unsafe living conditions, exercising their First Amendment rights, or using their (possible) state rights to withhold or deduct rent to fix poor living conditions. This category covers how a defendant can stop an eviction by raising a defense that the eviction is illegal under anti-retaliation laws.
Parent Terms: Defenses to stop or delay an eviction [HO-02-04-00-00]

Title: Tenants' rights and options after an eviction
Definition: This category concerns what a tenant can do after they have been evicted from a home. This includes expunging an eviction judgment from one's record, masking an eviction, recovering money damages for an illegal eviction, appealing an eviction, or otherwise.
Parent Terms: Eviction from a home [HO-02-00-00-00], Tenant Rights, Organizations, and Participation [HO-06-03-00-00]

Title: Expungement or Masking of an Eviction Record
Definition: This category concerns how a person can have a record of an eviction lawsuit or order sealed, masked, or expunged. This may be useful when they want to apply for housing, benefits, employments, and other opportunities.
Parent Terms: Eviction from a home [HO-02-00-00-00], Tenants' rights and options after an eviction [HO-02-05-00-00]

Title: Challenging a landlord for a 'constructive eviction'
Definition: This category covers how a tenant can challenge a landlord for trying to evict them illegally, by making it so difficult to live in the home that they must leave. This might involve shutting off heat or water, changing the locks, harassing tenants, failing to make repairs, or other harmful actions. The category covers what a tenant must gather and prove to be able to make a 'constructive eviction' claim, what kinds of landlord behavior amounts to a constructive eviction, and what options and outcomes might result.
Parent Terms: Landlord locking-out or shutting off utilities [HO-02-08-00-00]

Title: Landlord locking-out or shutting off utilities
