Definition: This category covers renters' options and rights if their landlord changes their locks, blocks their entry to their home, or if they shut off their utilities while the renter is still living there. These actions may be an illegal eviction, that the renter can take the landlord to court for.
Parent Terms: Renting or leasing a home [HO-06-00-00-00], Utilities, Energy, and Heating at home [HO-07-00-00-00], Poor living conditions in a rented home [HO-05-01-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1630600], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1070800]

Title: Settlements, Mediation, and Diversion from Eviction
Definition: This category covers how an eviction may be averted, through a landlord and tenant settlement, mediation, diversion program, or prevention program.
Parent Terms: Eviction from a home [HO-02-00-00-00], Alternative Dispute Resolution, Mediation, and Settlements [CO-07-01-00-00], Going to court for Eviction and Landlord-Tenant issues [HO-02-03-02-00]

Title: Landlord Payments to Tenant for Eviction and Displacement
Definition: This category covers situations when a tenant may be entitled to money payments from their landlord when an eviction takes place. This money might be to cover relocation and inconvenience costs.
Parent Terms: Eviction from a home [HO-02-00-00-00]

Title: Housing Assistance, Public Housing, and Subsidized Housing
Definition: This category is about financial support to cover costs for renting a home and covering home costs. In includes vouchers, subsidized housing, public housing, Section 8, rural housing subsidies, and the standards and procedures of living in public and subsidized housing (or being removed from it).
Parent Terms: Housing [HO-00-00-00-00], Public Benefits [BE-00-00-00-00]

Title: Emergency Assistance for housing costs (rental assistance)
Definition:
This category covers options for people who need immediate help in paying for housing costs like rent or utilities. This includes what options are available, who is eligible for them, how to access them, and what limitations they have on them.
This includes emergency rental assistance programs (sometimes called ERA or ERAP).
Parent Terms: Housing Assistance, Public Housing, and Subsidized Housing [HO-03-00-00-00], Problems with paying rent [HO-06-07-00-00]

Title: Local housing assistance programs
Definition: This category covers local city, county, parish, or municipality programs that might help a person with housing costs on an emergency, temporary basis -- like for rent, utilities, and other costs.
Parent Terms: Emergency Assistance for housing costs (rental assistance) [HO-03-01-00-00]

Title: State housing assistance programs
Definition: This category covers state programs that might help a person with housing costs on an emergency, temporary basis -- like for rent, utilities, and other costs.
Parent Terms: Emergency Assistance for housing costs (rental assistance) [HO-03-01-00-00]

Title: Landlord refusing to accept emergency rent program payments
Definition: This category covers situations when a landlord resists participation or acceptance of rental assistance programs, that a tenant is trying to use to cover their rent payments temporarily. For example, this might cover instances when a tenant has gotten Emergency Rent approval, but the landlord refuses to accept the payments.
Parent Terms: Emergency Assistance for housing costs (rental assistance) [HO-03-01-00-00]

Title: Public Housing (with government as landlord)
Definition: This category covers options and rights for people in regards to public housing, in which the government directly provides a rental home to a person and acts as their landlord. This includes issues around who can get public housing, access to the rental, eviction from it, how rent amounts are calculated, and other issues. It also includes issues of building, demolishing, or rehabilitating public housing units.
Parent Terms: Housing Assistance, Public Housing, and Subsidized Housing [HO-03-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1640000], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1640099], Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-00064], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [64]

Title: Safety and security in public housing
Definition: This category is about issues around public housing tenants may have with physical safety and security in their homes. This includes their rights, ability to raise grievances, and obligations of housing authorities to deal with issues of safety.
Parent Terms: Public Housing (with government as landlord) [HO-03-02-00-00]

Title: Public Housing sites, rehabilitation, and demolition
Definition: This category covers issues people might have when public housing is built, demolished, relocated, or other issues as to where it is located. This could be issues around the rights of tenants when a housing unit is being demolished or relocated. It is also about the legal process and requirements of how sites are decided upon, and whether there is permission for demolition.
Parent Terms: Public Housing (with government as landlord) [HO-03-02-00-00], Affordable Housing development [HO-03-05-00-00]

Title: Site selection for public housing
Definition: This category covers how sites are decided on for public housing, and what rights people have to participate in this process.
Parent Terms: Public Housing sites, rehabilitation, and demolition [HO-03-02-05-00]

Title: Demolition of public housing
Definition: This category covers tenants' rights and options when their public housing unit is being torn down or otherwise demolished.
Parent Terms: Public Housing sites, rehabilitation, and demolition [HO-03-02-05-00]

Title: Relocation rights and assistance for public housing
Definition: This category covers rights, options, and assistance that tenants in public housing might have, if their home is being demolished, rehabilitated, converted, or acquired.
Parent Terms: Public Housing sites, rehabilitation, and demolition [HO-03-02-05-00]

Title: Employment opportunities (Section 3) for public and subsidized housing contracts
Definition: This category covers the Section 3 Rule about how public housing agencies must employ people who either live in public housing or are low-income, when they are contracting for improvements to public housing or other projects.
Parent Terms: Public Housing sites, rehabilitation, and demolition [HO-03-02-05-00]

Title: Hope VI program to revitalize public housing
Definition: This category covers issues and questions around the US government's Hope VI program to rehabilitate public housing projects through new grants, demolition, planning, and other efforts.
Parent Terms: Public Housing sites, rehabilitation, and demolition [HO-03-02-05-00]

Title: Getting public housing
Definition: This category covers the options, eligibility standards, and process of being admitted to live in public housing rentals.
Parent Terms: Public Housing (with government as landlord) [HO-03-02-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1640110], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1640199]

Title: Eligibility and Selection Criteria for public housing
Definition: This category covers who is eligible to apply for public housing, and how it will be determined if they will be admitted for housing or not. It includes the local housing authorities' definitions of specific admissions criteria.
Parent Terms: Getting public housing [HO-03-02-06-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1640110], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1640160]

Title: Preferences in who gets public housing
Definition: This category covers what preferences a housing authority might have in deciding who gets public housing, and how wait list positions for public housing are determined. This might be on residency past and plans, or other factors.
Parent Terms: Getting public housing [HO-03-02-06-00]

Title: Residency requirements for public housing
Definition: This category covers the requirements that a housing authority might have for possible renters, about how long they have lived in the geographic area or how long they are planning to stay.
Parent Terms: Getting public housing [HO-03-02-06-00]

Title: Having visitors in public housing
Definition: This category covers a public housing tenant's right to have guests or others in their home, when there might be limits on this, and how a tenant can protect their rights.
Parent Terms: Public Housing (with government as landlord) [HO-03-02-00-00]

Title: Federally Subsidized Housing (including Section 8/Housing Choice Vouchers)
Definition: This cateogry covers options and rights for tenants to receive subsidized housing, like in the form of Section 8 or Housing Choice Vouchers. The government is not directly their landlord (like public housing), but instead helps them pay their rent with a private landlord. This category covers eligibility for subsidies, access to the home, terminations, security charges, rent definitions, and other issues.
Parent Terms: Housing Assistance, Public Housing, and Subsidized Housing [HO-03-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1610100], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1610097], Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-00061], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1612201], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1610099], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1612200], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [61]

Title: Having visitors to federally subsidized rental home
Definition: This category covers tenants' rights, options, and limits to have visitors to their home that is subsidized by federal rental assistance, like a Section 8 or Housing Choice Voucher.
Parent Terms: Federally Subsidized Housing (including Section 8/Housing Choice Vouchers) [HO-03-03-00-00]

Title: Getting a Housing Choice (Section 8) voucher for federally subsidized rental
Definition: This category covers if and how a person can get federal subsidies to rent a home, like getting a Section 8 or Housing Choice Voucher.
Parent Terms: Federally Subsidized Housing (including Section 8/Housing Choice Vouchers) [HO-03-03-00-00]

Title: Recertifying/reporting changes to income and family for Section 8 voucher
Definition: This category covers how a tenant receiving a Section 8 or Housing Choice Voucher subsidy can recertify their income and family breakdown every year, and how they can report changes during the year if their family or income changes.
Parent Terms: Federally Subsidized Housing (including Section 8/Housing Choice Vouchers) [HO-03-03-00-00]

Title: Termination of a federal rental subsidy
Definition: This category covers the process and rights of a tenant who is facing termination of their rental subsidy, like their Section 8 or Housing Choice Voucher.
Parent Terms: Federally Subsidized Housing (including Section 8/Housing Choice Vouchers) [HO-03-03-00-00]

Title: Subsidized Housing Removal, Conversion, or Preservation
Definition: This category concerns options, rights, and legal strategies that are available when landlords consider removing rental homes from affordable or subsidized housing programs. This also covers notification and protections that must be given to tenants with federal subsidies and vouchers, if the landlord is planning to remove or demolish subsidized housing units.
Parent Terms: Federally Subsidized Housing (including Section 8/Housing Choice Vouchers) [HO-03-03-00-00], Affordable Housing development [HO-03-05-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1612000], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1612099], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1612202]

Title: Landlord Opting out of federal subsidies program
Definition: This category covers whether and how a landlord can decide to remove their home from inclusion in federally subsidized rent programs, like the Section 8/Housing Choice Voucher program. It covers the rights that tenants might have, notice that landlords must give, and possible housing authority or other action the landlords might face.
Parent Terms: Subsidized Housing Removal, Conversion, or Preservation [HO-03-03-06-00]

Title: Relocating with a federal rent subsidy voucher
Definition: This category covers a tenant's rights and processes to relocate to another home when they use a Section 8 or Housing Choice Voucher to help pay their rent. This includes how they might move if their home is being demolished or converted, if they need to move to a different state, or otherwise.
Parent Terms: Federally Subsidized Housing (including Section 8/Housing Choice Vouchers) [HO-03-03-00-00]

Title: Rural rental assistance (formerly FMHA) programs
Definition: This category covers federal rent subsidies from the Rural Economic and Community Development rent assistance programs (formerly FMHA housing programs). It covers how people can access this assistance for rental housing in rural communities, how rent is calculated, what security deposits are required, and what eviction procedures are.
Parent Terms: Housing Assistance, Public Housing, and Subsidized Housing [HO-03-00-00-00], Problems with paying rent [HO-06-07-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1690900], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1690999]

Title: Affordable Housing development
Definition: This category covers issues around the development of new affordable housing units.
Parent Terms: Housing Assistance, Public Housing, and Subsidized Housing [HO-03-00-00-00], Economic Development [BU-02-00-00-00]

Title: Low Income Housing Tax Credit to build affordable housing
Definition: This category covers questions and options for those interested in possibly building low-income housing, or rehabilitating existing units, to provide affordable rental housing for low- and moderate-income tenants. It also covers renters' and residents' rights regarding these development projects.
Parent Terms: Affordable Housing development [HO-03-05-00-00]

Title: Immigrants' eligibility for housing programs
Definition: This category covers if and how non-US citizens may be able to access public housing, subsidized housing vouchers, emergency assistance, and other programs that help them with the cost of their housing.
Parent Terms: Housing Assistance, Public Housing, and Subsidized Housing [HO-03-00-00-00], Public Benefits for immigrants [IM-03-00-00-00]

Title: Single Room Occupancy housing options
Definition: This category concerns options and rights for tenants in single room occupancy units, that lets low-income tenants have affordable housing.
Parent Terms: Housing Assistance, Public Housing, and Subsidized Housing [HO-03-00-00-00], Homelessness and Housing Insecurity [HO-13-00-00-00]

Title: Buying a Home
Definition: This category is about the process of buying a home, coop, condo, mobile home -- and dealing with problems with the purchase. This includes issues with getting title, closing on a house purchase, getting financing, and other issues.

Title: Federal subsidies to buy a home (Homeownership Voucher Program)
Definition: This category concerns a Section 8 or Housing Choice Voucher option to use housing assistance to cover homeownership costs (rather than rental costs). It covers eligibility factors, work and income requirements, time restrictions, and other process to follow to use the voucher program to become a homeowner.
Parent Terms: Buying a Home [HO-04-00-00-00], Housing Assistance, Public Housing, and Subsidized Housing [HO-03-00-00-00]

Title: Paying for a home through a Bond/Contract for Deed
Definition: This category covers options for someone who wants to pay for a home through borrowing money, and the borrower keeps the deed and the legal title to the house (and the borrower has physical possession of the house). It is usually known as a Bond for Deed or Contract for Deed arrangement. This includes dealing with consequences if the buyer defaults on the payments, what happens when the buyer makes improvements to the home,  lawsuits that might result from using this bond/contract.
Parent Terms: Buying a Home [HO-04-00-00-00], Mortgages and other financing for a home [HO-09-05-00-00], Contracts, Warranties, and Deceptive Trade Practices [MO-03-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1620650], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1620300]

Title: Installment Land Sale Contracts
Definition: This category is about the process of buying or selling land through a contract, in which the buyer does not get the deed until the installment payments are fully made.
Parent Terms: Paying for a home through a Bond/Contract for Deed [HO-04-02-00-00]

Title: Deeds for a home
Definition: This category covers issues with drafting, revising, transferring, or dealing with problems with a deed (the legal document about ownership) for a home. This typically done when a home property is being sold and transferred. This covers what kind of deeds are needed, how it is written, how it is recorded, and to deal with other problems.
Parent Terms: Buying a Home [HO-04-00-00-00]

Title: Closing on a home sale
Definition: This category covers issues with the closing of sale process of a home. This could include dealing with problems with the home sale, like liens or debts, unclear title, pests, defects in the home inspection, low appraisals, and other issues. This includes options for backing out of a home purchase, what documents are required, and what other issues and protections are possible.
Parent Terms: Buying a Home [HO-04-00-00-00]

Title: Cooperatives, Condominiums, and Homeowners Associations
Definition: This category covers issues that a person might have when they own a home that's part of a cooperative, condominium, or homeowners association. It includes dealing with governing boards, dealing with complaints and violations,  problems with other homeowners, control of decision-making, and other issues.
Parent Terms: Owning a Home [HO-09-00-00-00]

Title: Problems with living conditions
Definition: This category is about problems that people have where they live, including health issues, environmental issues, security, and other habitability issues with an individual home or neighborhood. It could be for rented homes, a home one owns, or the broader neighborhood.

Title: Poor living conditions in a rented home
Definition: This category concerns problems that a person may have as a tenant in a rental home. This includes issues with heat, air, water, plumbing, pests, major appliances, locks, doors, or other essential features. It may also be known as a "Warranty of Habitability" issue.
Parent Terms: Problems with living conditions [HO-05-00-00-00], Renting or leasing a home [HO-06-00-00-00]

Title: Poor living conditions in a federally subsidized (Section 8) home
Definition: This category concerns problems that a person may have as a tenant in a federally-subsidized (Section 8 voucher) rented home. This includes issues with heat, air, water, plumbing, pests, major appliances, locks, doors, or other essential features. It may also be known as a "Warranty of Habitability" or "Quality Standards" issue.
Parent Terms: Poor living conditions in a rented home [HO-05-01-00-00], Federally Subsidized Housing (including Section 8/Housing Choice Vouchers) [HO-03-03-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1612209], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1641200]

Title: Challenging a federally subsidized rental's living conditions
Definition: This category concerns options a tenant or government agencies may have to challenge a landlord's housing quality and affordability for federally subsidized rentals. This includes raising claims of Unfair Trade Practices, of fraudulently presenting rentals as fair, safe, and affordable, and subjecting tenants to uninhabitable and dangerous conditions. It also covers formal grievance procedures of raising problems to the local housing authority or other government actors.
Parent Terms: Poor living conditions in a federally subsidized (Section 8) home [HO-05-01-01-00], Poor living conditions in a rental subsidized with rural rental assistance [HO-05-01-02-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1612208], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1690940], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1610500], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1611000]

Title: Housing Quality Standards for federally subsidized rentals
Definition: This category covers the government-mandated standards that all rentals that qualify for housing choice vouchers, or Section 8 vouchers, must comply with. This includes issues of when the home is on the rental market, and its ongoing maintenance.
Parent Terms: Poor living conditions in a federally subsidized (Section 8) home [HO-05-01-01-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1612400], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1610900]

Title: Termination of 'Troubled Properties' as federally subsidized rentals
Definition: This category concerns what happens when a housing authority or other government agency determines that a rental unit that's associated with Section 8 or other housing subsidies is 'troubled', in that its living conditions do not meet quality standards. This can include the removal of the Section 8 contract, or repairs of the troubled properties -- and this category covers what rights and options tenants have in this process.
Parent Terms: Poor living conditions in a federally subsidized (Section 8) home [HO-05-01-01-00], Subsidized Housing Removal, Conversion, or Preservation [HO-03-03-06-00]

Title: Safety and security issues in subsidized housing
Definition: This category covers tenants' rights and options when they are concerned about their personal safety and security while living in a rental home with assistance from Section 8, housing choice vouchers, or other subsidized housing programs.
Parent Terms: Poor living conditions in a federally subsidized (Section 8) home [HO-05-01-01-00]

Title: Poor living conditions in a rental subsidized with rural rental assistance
Definition: This category concerns problems that a person may have as a tenant in a rental that is subsidized by a federal rural rental assistance program (formerly known as FMHA Housing program). This includes issues with heat, air, water, plumbing, pests, major appliances, locks, doors, or other essential features. It may also be known as a "Warranty of Habitability" issue.
Parent Terms: Poor living conditions in a rented home [HO-05-01-00-00], Rural rental assistance (formerly FMHA) programs [HO-03-04-00-00]

Title: Poor living conditions in public housing
Definition: This category covers issues that a person may have as a tenant in public housing, when the government/housing authority is their landlord. This includes issues with heat, air, water, plumbing, pests, major appliances, locks, doors, or other essential features. It may also be known as a "Warranty of Habitability" issue, or as a Quality Standards issue.
Parent Terms: Public Housing (with government as landlord) [HO-03-02-00-00], Poor living conditions in a rented home [HO-05-01-00-00]

Title: Housing code compliance
Definition: This category concerns how a tenant can raise code compliance violations if they think their landlord is providing a rental home that goes against the codes for housing quality standards. It also includes the protections that tenants may have about rent control or protection from retaliation if their landlord is in violation of the housing code.
Parent Terms: Poor living conditions in a rented home [HO-05-01-00-00]

Title: Disruptions to 'quiet enjoyment' of a rental
Definition: This category concerns issues a tenant might have, that prevent them from their basic rights of 'quiet enjoyment' of their home. This includes issues with ongoing noises or behaviors from neighbors, maintenance work that takes significantly longer than expected, pests making noises, or landlords calling or entering the property too frequently or without notice.
Parent Terms: Poor living conditions in a rented home [HO-05-01-00-00]

Title: Landlord harassment or problem behavior
Definition: This category is about situations where a landlord is behaving in a way that is threatening, harassing, or otherwise troubling for tenants.
Parent Terms: Poor living conditions in a rented home [HO-05-01-00-00]

Title: Lead Paint and Poisoning
Definition: This category covers options and rights for people who have encountered lead paint in their homes or in other buildings, and may have issues with poisoning from it.
Parent Terms: Problems with living conditions [HO-05-00-00-00], Health issues from living conditions [HE-06-00-00-00]

Title: Renting or leasing a home
Definition:
This category is about the process of renting or leasing a home, and problems that may come up while renting a home, mobile home lot, or while living in a group home or homeless shelter. 

It includes landlord-tenant issues for private rentals, subsidized homes, public homes, or other situations where the person living in the property doesn't own it.

Some scenarios in this category include a dispute with a landlord about rules or property, difficulty getting a security deposit back, the denial of reasonable accommodations for a medical condition, trouble getting a written lease or rental contract, failure to receive basic services or repairs, a threat of eviction, denial or trouble with a housing voucher or subsidy, harassment for rent, denial of relocation assistance from an unsafe rental unit, and denial of a rental unit because of prior juvenile or criminal system involvement.
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1630100], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1630099], Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-00063], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [63]

Title: Security Deposit for a rented home
Definition: This category concerns issues around security deposits, including how much a landlord can ask for, what they can deduct from it, how a tenant can get it back, and how to raise issues around this.
Parent Terms: Renting or leasing a home [HO-06-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1690930], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1630900]

Title: Security deposits and charges for federally subsidized (Section 8) rentals
Definition: This category concerns security deposit/charge issues that may arise for tenants in federally subsidized housing. This includes questions about how much landlords can charge for a deposit, how to get assistance to pay it, how it can be returned, and what can be deducted from it.
Parent Terms: Security Deposit for a rented home [HO-06-01-00-00], Federally Subsidized Housing (including Section 8/Housing Choice Vouchers) [HO-03-03-00-00]

Title: Income-based rent rates for public housing
Definition: This category covers how a person's rent for public housing is calculated, including what their annual income is, what parts of their income is disregarded, and other formulas that are used.
Parent Terms: Rent issues in public housing [HO-06-02-01-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1640520], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1640530], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1640540], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1690500]

Title: Security deposits and charges for public housing
Definition: This category concerns security deposit/charge issues that may arise for tenants in public housing. This includes questions about how much housing authorities can charge for a deposit, how to get assistance to pay it, how it can be returned, and what can be deducted from it.
Parent Terms: Security Deposit for a rented home [HO-06-01-00-00]

Title: Challenging a landlord's security deposit deductions
Definition: This category concerns how a tenant may challenge the deductions that a landlord takes from their security deposits, like for repairs or damages to the home after the tenant moves out. This includes possibly raising claims under the Unfair Trade Practices law, that the landlord misrepresented the repairs needed, in order to claim financial damages.
Parent Terms: Security Deposit for a rented home [HO-06-01-00-00]

Title: Rent charges, increases, and control
Definition: This category covers issues that a tenant may have with rent levels for their home, including how much rent they have to pay, how much it can be increased by, and protections they may have based on local laws or housing programs. It covers private rentals, subsidized rentals, and public housing.
Parent Terms: Renting or leasing a home [HO-06-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1630800], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1630899]

Title: Rent issues in public housing
Definition: This category covers issues that individual tenants or housing project groups may have with rent in public housing. This includes how the rent levels are defined, how the tenant's financial situation affects the rents, and how rent may be increased.
Parent Terms: Rent charges, increases, and control [HO-06-02-00-00], Public Housing (with government as landlord) [HO-03-02-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1640500], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1640599]

Title: Rent Ceilings or Flat Rent for public housing
Definition: This category concerns upper limits on what rents can be charged in public housing. It also may be known as the Flat Rent -- the most amount of rent you may be charged in public housing. This covers how this ceiling is calculated and when a tenant may use the flat rent rather than income-based rent amounts.
Parent Terms: Rent issues in public housing [HO-06-02-01-00]

Title: Utility allowances and charges for public or subsidized housing
Definition: This category covers how tenants of public housing or subsidized housing may be able to deduct a monthly utility allowance, if the utilities are not already included in their rent. This covers how much this allowance might be, according to a local housing authority and how it affects the rental amount that the person may have to pay.
Parent Terms: Rent issues in public housing [HO-06-02-01-00], Utilities, Energy, and Heating at home [HO-07-00-00-00], Rent issues in federally subsidized rentals [HO-06-02-02-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1640550], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1640900], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1611700], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1610702]

Title: Rent increases in public housing
Definition: This category covers if and how rent can be increased in public housing. This could also be called project-wide rental increases.
Parent Terms: Rent issues in public housing [HO-06-02-01-00]

Title: Rent issues in federally subsidized rentals
Definition: This category covers issues that tenants in federally subsidized (Section 8) rentals might have with rent levels, including how they are calculated, what ceiling rents are, what allowances they may have for utilities, how rents might be increased, and other issues.
Parent Terms: Rent charges, increases, and control [HO-06-02-00-00], Federally Subsidized Housing (including Section 8/Housing Choice Vouchers) [HO-03-03-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1610700], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1610799], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1611100]

Title: Income-based rent rates for federally subsidized housing
Definition: This category covers issues in how to calculate the rent/assistance levels that a tenant getting federally subsidized housing has, including how their income is defined, how rent is defined, what income is disregarded, and what utility allowances they are given.
Parent Terms: Rent issues in federally subsidized rentals [HO-06-02-02-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1610704], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1610701], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1610705], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1610702]

Title: Rent ceilings or Flat Rent rates for federally subsidized rentals
Definition: This category concerns upper limits on what rents can be charged for federally subsidized homes. It also may be known as the Flat Rent -- the most amount of rent you may be charged. This covers how this ceiling is calculated and when a tenant may use the flat rent rather than income-based rent amounts.
Parent Terms: Rent issues in federally subsidized rentals [HO-06-02-02-00]

Title: Rent issues in rural assistance subsidized homes
Definition: This category covers issues that tenants in homes subsidized by rural rental assistance programs (formerly FMHA programs) might have with rent levels, including how they are calculated, what ceiling rents are, what allowances they may have for utilities, how rents might be increased, and other issues.
Parent Terms: Rent charges, increases, and control [HO-06-02-00-00], Rural rental assistance (formerly FMHA) programs [HO-03-04-00-00]

Title: Late fees, penalties, other charges for a rental home
Definition: This category covers issues a tenant might have when a landlord charges them fees for paying their rent late, includes other penalties, or charges them more money than they expected for renting the home.
Parent Terms: Rent charges, increases, and control [HO-06-02-00-00]

Title: Pet fees, deposits, and rent
Definition: This category covers whether and how a landlord can charge a tenant an extra fee for having pets in the apartment. This includes things like pet fees, pet deposits, and pet rent. Rent control laws may explicitly prohibit these kinds of fees.
Parent Terms: Late fees, penalties, other charges for a rental home [HO-06-02-04-00]

Title: Landlord taking property for rent owed
Definition: This category covers what options and rights a tenant may have if their landlord takes or detains their property. This is typically when the landlord feels the tenant owes them rent or other money.
Parent Terms: Rent charges, increases, and control [HO-06-02-00-00], Renting or leasing a home [HO-06-00-00-00]

Title: Rent Control
Definition: This category covers issues around rent control, for tenants and landlords who live in an area with rent control policies. These policies, that are often put into law by city or county ordinances, limit the rent that landlords can charge to tenants, and how much and how often they can raise rent. This category covers questions about how people can complain about overcharges, deal with rent control laws, and deal with eviction and successions.
Parent Terms: Rent charges, increases, and control [HO-06-02-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1630800], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1630899]

Title: Overcharges of rent in a rent control area
Definition: This category covers how a tenant can complain of an overcharge, that is in violation of rent control policies in their local area. It also covers how landlords can respond, and how an overcharge complaint is processed and resolved.
Parent Terms: Rent Control  [HO-06-02-05-00]

Title: Determining if a home is covered by rent control
Definition: This category is about how to determine if a rental home is covered by rent control protections or not. This might be known as a 'coverage' issue. The coverage might depend on the location, age, and situation of the house.
Parent Terms: Rent Control  [HO-06-02-05-00]

Title: Rent control agencies' practices
Definition: This category covers how the organization that enforces rent control -- like a local rent board -- behaves, including how they they hear disputes and enforce the control laws.
Parent Terms: Rent Control  [HO-06-02-05-00]

Title: Eviction limits under Rent Control laws
Definition: This category covers the specific rules and protections that rent control laws (or ordinances) may give to tenants facing eviction. Rent control laws might limit the reasons that landlords can evict a tenant, and give extra defenses to a tenant who has been sued.
Parent Terms: Rent Control  [HO-06-02-05-00], Eviction from a home [HO-02-00-00-00]

Title: Rent control jurisdictions
Definition: This category covers whether a certain geographical area has rent control laws or not.
Parent Terms: Rent Control  [HO-06-02-05-00]

Title: Succession rights and process in Rent Control homes
Definition: This category covers how rent control or rent-stabilization laws determine how one tenant can take a home over from another. This includes succession rights eligibility, the landlord's ability to change the rent, when a family member can take over the home at the same rent level, how to claim these rights, and how to challenge a claimed succession.
Parent Terms: Rent Control  [HO-06-02-05-00]

Title: Tenant Rights, Organizations, and Participation
Definition: This category covers the basic rights that tenants have, their ability to organize or unionize, their ability to participate in the housing market or government agencies, and other related issues. This includes how a tenant in public or subsidized housing has rights to participate in decisions about the housing quality and modernization. It also covers rights around raising grievances and advocating for themselves.
Parent Terms: Renting or leasing a home [HO-06-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1631300], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1631100]

Title: Tenants' participation and organization in subsidized housing
Definition: This category covers how tenants who live in federally subsidized housing (like Section 8 voucher holders) can participate in the housing program, raise grievances, advocate for themselves, and organize into unions or other groups.
Parent Terms: Tenant Rights, Organizations, and Participation [HO-06-03-00-00], Federally Subsidized Housing (including Section 8/Housing Choice Vouchers) [HO-03-03-00-00]

Title: Tenants' participation and organization in public housing
Definition: This category covers the rights that tenants have when living in public housing, including their right to participate in decisions and modernization of the housing, their ability to raise grievances and to organize to advocate for themselves.
Parent Terms: Tenant Rights, Organizations, and Participation [HO-06-03-00-00], Public Housing (with government as landlord) [HO-03-02-00-00]

Title: Tenants' Rights around Evictions
Definition: This category covers what rights a tenant can expect to have if there is a threat of eviction. This might be a formal eviction, through a lawsuit in courts, or an informal eviction carried out without going to courts. This covers materials and events to help tenants know their rights.
Parent Terms: Tenant Rights, Organizations, and Participation [HO-06-03-00-00], Eviction from a home [HO-02-00-00-00]

Title: Landlord access to a rental
Definition: This category covers issues a tenant might have with how and when the landlord can access their rental home, and how they have 'quiet enjoyment' to their home. This covers private rentals, subsidized rentals, and public housing. It includes issues of landlords coming onto the property too frequently, unnecessarily, or without proper notice.
Parent Terms: Renting or leasing a home [HO-06-00-00-00]

Title: Landlord access to a federally subsidized rental
Definition: This category covers when and whether a landlord can come into a rented home that's subsidized by federally funding, like Section 8 vouchers. It covers issues when tenants have a problem that landlords come without notice or are entering their home.
Parent Terms: Landlord access to a rental [HO-06-04-00-00], Federally Subsidized Housing (including Section 8/Housing Choice Vouchers) [HO-03-03-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [ 1612303], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1612300], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1612399], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1612302]

Title: Landlord or Housing Authority access to a public housing rental
Definition: This category covers when and whether a landlord (or member of a public housing authority) can come into a public housing rental. It covers issues when tenants have a problem that landlords or housing authority representatives come without notice or are entering their home. This can be linked to the tenant's right to exclude people from their rental home.
Parent Terms: Landlord access to a rental [HO-06-04-00-00], Public Housing (with government as landlord) [HO-03-02-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1642010], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1642000], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1642099], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1642030]

Title: Leases & Rental Agreements for a rental home
Definition: This category covers the process of receiving, understanding, negotiating, and signing a lease between a landlord and tenant. This includes how a tenant can ensure the lease is fair, raise any objections, protect their rights, and deal with other issues with the lease. It can also be about how to understand, modify, or challenge a lease after signing it.
Parent Terms: Renting or leasing a home [HO-06-00-00-00]

Title: Leases for a federally subsidized home
Definition: This category covers the process of receiving, understanding, negotiating, and signing a lease between a landlord and tenant for federally subsidized (like Section 8 housing). This includes how a tenant can ensure the lease is fair, raise any objections, protect their rights, and deal with other issues with the lease. It can also be about how to understand, modify, or challenge a lease after signing it.
Parent Terms: Leases & Rental Agreements for a rental home [HO-06-05-00-00], Federally Subsidized Housing (including Section 8/Housing Choice Vouchers) [HO-03-03-00-00]

Title: Changing a rental agreement or lease
Definition: This category covers how a tenant and landlord may make changes to a lease or rental agreement. This could be through a mediation to stop an eviction, or it could be because of an emergency like COVID-19.
Parent Terms: Leases & Rental Agreements for a rental home [HO-06-05-00-00], Settlements, Mediation, and Diversion from Eviction [HO-02-09-00-00]

Title: Local regulations of rental housing
Definition: This category covers state, city, and other local rules that control how property-owners can rent out homes.
Parent Terms: Renting or leasing a home [HO-06-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1631400], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1631404]

Title: State regulations of rental housing
Definition: This category covers state rules on who can rent their private home out, and how they can do so.
Parent Terms: Local regulations of rental housing [HO-06-06-00-00]

Title: Rental protections for those with HIV/AIDS
Definition: This category covers protections, including from local state and city rules, regarding people living with HIV/AIDS. This could be about protection from discrimination, housing assistance programs, homelessness prevention, access to therapies and services, and other rules.
Parent Terms: Local regulations of rental housing [HO-06-06-00-00], Discrimination around housing [HO-01-00-00-00], Homelessness and Housing Insecurity [HO-13-00-00-00], HIV/AIDS discrimination [RI-03-03-00-00]

Title: Problems with paying rent
Definition: This category covers situations where the tenant is unable to pay their rent in full and on time.
Parent Terms: Renting or leasing a home [HO-06-00-00-00], Rent charges, increases, and control [HO-06-02-00-00]

Title: Ending a rental lease early
Definition: This category covers situations in which a landlord or tenant wants to end a rental agreement early, in order to have the tenant leave before the lease specifies.  This could be in situations where the tenant is unhappy with the housing, and wants to leave early. Or it could be when the landlord wants to have the tenant leave, even though the lease is for a longer term.
Parent Terms: Renting or leasing a home [HO-06-00-00-00]

Title: Landlord suing tenant for money
Definition: This category covers situations when a landlord brings a lawsuit against present or past tenants, to recover money from them.  This could include attempts to recover rent that was not paid, penalties, fees, or other financial damages that the landlord believes they have suffered. This could be filed alongside an eviction lawsuit, or separate from it.
Parent Terms: Renting or leasing a home [HO-06-00-00-00], Small Claims lawsuits [MO-10-00-00-00], Eviction from a home [HO-02-00-00-00]

Title: Abandoned Personal Property in Rental Home
Definition:
This category covers what happens to a person's property (like furniture, electronics, and other possessions) in their rental home, if they are evicted or have to leave the home.

It covers topics like how long a person has to retrieve their property, how to take care of it, and how to deal with law enforcement or the landlord if there is a conflict about the property.
Parent Terms: Renting or leasing a home [HO-06-00-00-00], Eviction from a home [HO-02-00-00-00]

Title: Renters' housing issues after a natural disaster
Definition: This category covers issues a renter might have with their housing after a natural disaster like a flood, hurricane, tornado, or other problem. This includes damage to their home, landlords' responsibility for repairs, eviction, and other issues.
Parent Terms: Renting or leasing a home [HO-06-00-00-00], Poor living conditions in a rented home [HO-05-01-00-00], Housing after a Disaster [HO-10-00-00-00]

Title: Having pets or assistance animals in a rental home
Definition: This category covers a renter's options about having a pet in their rental home. This includes rights to have a pet, like for a disability, common lease clauses about pets, what the landlord is able to do, what common problems occur, and more.
Parent Terms: Renting or leasing a home [HO-06-00-00-00]

Title: Utilities, Energy, and Heating at home
Definition: This category is about electric, energy, gas, and water utilities at home, including financial assistance, utilities being shut off, payment to them, or terminating them. It might also include issues if a utility company is in a crisis, and you must pay another party (like a receiver) instead of the company.
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1691100], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [07], Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-00007]

Title: Utility disconnection and reconnection
Definition: This category covers what might happen if a utility service disconnects for one's home, like for nonpayment of bills. It can cover what notification requirements exist, how to reconnect the services, and getting payment plans.
Parent Terms: Utilities, Energy, and Heating at home [HO-07-00-00-00]

Title: Foreclosure on a Home
Definition: This category is about problems with homes you own or live in, that are going into foreclosure, how to defend against it, and the court process around it.
Parent Terms: Housing [HO-00-00-00-00], Owning a Home [HO-09-00-00-00], Mortgages and other financing for a home [HO-09-05-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1670000], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1670099], Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-00067], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [67]

Title: Defenses against a Foreclosure
Definition: This category concerns options a homeowner may have to defend against a foreclosure action. These defenses can include that the bank didn't follow state procedures; that the loan holder can't prove that they own the loan (they lack standing); that the mortgage servicer make a serious mistake; that the homeowner is a service-member on active duty; or that the statute of limitations has passed.
Parent Terms: Foreclosure on a Home [HO-08-00-00-00]

Title: Stopping a foreclosure through a 'redemption' (paying off loan in full)
Definition: This category covers the option for a homeowner to 'redeem' their property within a certain time period in a foreclosure process, by paying off their debt or reimbursing the person who bought the property at the foreclosure sale. The options vary by state, about whether this redemption period is only before a foreclosure sale, or after the sale as well.
Parent Terms: Foreclosure on a Home [HO-08-00-00-00]

Title: Stopping a foreclosure by reinstating (catching up with) the loan
Definition: This category covers options for a homeowner who wants to stop a foreclosure, by 'reinstating' their loan through paying back money they owe (but not the full loan), and then keep up their monthly payments and other fees. States may have different deadlines for when reinstatement may occur, and different lenders may have different policies on reinstating the loan. This category covers how you can use reinstatement as a defense against foreclosure, and also contesting an incorrect reinstatement quote from the lender.
Parent Terms: Foreclosure on a Home [HO-08-00-00-00]

Title: Tenant options when landlord is in foreclosure or bankruptcy
Definition: This category covers what a tenant can do when their landlord's property is in foreclosure, or if their landlord is in the bankruptcy process. It covers what their rights are, what happens if they face eviction based on their landlord's situation, how their lease may change, or if there are new owners of the property.
Parent Terms: Foreclosure on a Home [HO-08-00-00-00], Renting or leasing a home [HO-06-00-00-00]

Title: Another person (receiver) taking over from a landlord
Definition: This category covers the options of tenants to get a 'Receiver' or a court-appointed party to take over from a landlord who is in foreclosure or having serious problems with a lender. For example, a tenant may be notified that they now should pay rent to the receiver, not to the landlord, because of a court appointment of this receiver.
Parent Terms: Tenant options when landlord is in foreclosure or bankruptcy [HO-08-06-00-00]

Title: Owning a Home
Definition:
This category concerns issues for homeowners, like with improvements, contractors, neighbors, mortgages, taxes, and titles. It also includes problems with owning a home, including foreclosures and liens.

It includes scenarios like being the target of misleading or dishonest mortgage lending practices, being told by a lender that extra financial products needed to be purchased to get a mortgage, falling several payments behind on a mortgage or having a home going into foreclosure, and having trouble selling or buying property.
Taxonomies: Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-00062], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1620100], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1620199], Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-00069], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [62]

Title: Clearing Title to one's home
Definition: This category concerns how to prove one own's one's home, by getting a clear title to the property. A title may not be clear if title was not formally transferred after the owner dies, or during a sale of the property. This may be important after a natural disaster, when homeowners must be able to prove they own their home in order to access relief funds that would let them rebuild their home.
Parent Terms: Title to a home [H0-09-02-00-00], Housing after a Disaster [HO-10-00-00-00]

Title: Zoning and Land Use of one’s property
Definition: This category covers issues a property owner might have with dealing with local government, to get approvals for what they might do with their property. It might include issues around dealing with government's zoning designations, redevelopment or additions, environmental issues, selling or acquiring properties, or other issues.
Parent Terms: Owning a Home [HO-09-00-00-00], Affordable Housing development [HO-03-05-00-00], Government Services [GO-00-00-00-00], Zoning issues related to housing [HO-12-00-00-00]

Title: Property Taxes
Definition: This category covers issues that a homeowner might have around paying their taxes for their property. This category covers how the taxes are calculated, how to pay them, and how to deal with disputes around them.
Parent Terms: Owning a Home [HO-09-00-00-00], Taxes [MO-09-00-00-00]

Title: Property Tax Appeals, Refunds and Abatements
Definition: This category covers options for property owners who believe they may have been charged with property taxes at an incorrect assessment, or with other problems. This includes options to appeal a property valuation or request a refund of the taxes they've paid for a property.
Parent Terms: Property Taxes [HO-09-04-00-00]

Title: Mortgages and other financing for a home
Definition: This category covers issues that a homeowner might have with taking out a mortgage, finding support and opportunities, dealing with scams, keeping up on their obligations, and understanding their options if problems arise.
Parent Terms: Owning a Home [HO-09-00-00-00], Money, Debt, and Consumer Issues [MO-00-00-00-00], Buying a Home [HO-04-00-00-00]

Title: Federally-Subsidized Mortgage Loans
Definition: This category covers issues homeowners might have with mortgage loans that are federally subsidized. This might include issues about who is eligible for these mortgages, restrictions on them, protections for mortgage-holders, relief programs, and other options. It might be from agencies like HUD, Federal Housing Authority, Federal Housing Finance Agency, Federal Home Loan Bank System, Freddie Mac, or Fannie Mae.
Parent Terms: Mortgages and other financing for a home [HO-09-05-00-00]

Title: HUD-Insured Mortgages
Definition: This category includes options for homeowners who have mortgages that are insured by the HUD agency, or the Federal Housing Authority. It includes how to deal with problems if there are collections or foreclosure issues.
Parent Terms: Federally-Subsidized Mortgage Loans [HO-09-05-01-00]

Title: Mortgages for Veterans
Definition: This category covers mortgage options for veterans and military service members, including opportunities to get a more favorable mortgage, protections, obligations, and dealing with problems that may arise.
Parent Terms: Mortgages and other financing for a home [HO-09-05-00-00], Public Benefits for Veterans and Military [BE-06-00-00-00]

Title: Mortgage Rescue Scams
Definition: This category is about possible scams a homeowner might face when they are facing collections or foreclosure, and they are offered services or help by groups claiming to be HUD or other government agencies -- or who are charging fees for what should be free services. They could also be posing as lawyers or other groups who promise they can help save a home from foreclosure.
Parent Terms: Mortgages and other financing for a home [HO-09-05-00-00]

Title: Reverse Mortgages (loans using home equity conversion)
Definition: This category covers issues that a homeowner might face if they take out a reverse mortgage, in which they receive money based on putting up their home as equity. This might be called Home Equity Conversion Mortgages. This category covers who is eligible for reverse mortgages, what repayment obligations are, what happens if someone defaults on them, what happens if a spouse/co-owner dies, and what scams might be.
Parent Terms: Mortgages and other financing for a home [HO-09-05-00-00], Loans [MO-08-00-00-00]

Title: Mortgage Predatory Lending
Definition: This category covers options and issues with possible predatory lending practices around mortgages. This includes what qualifies as predatory lending, using predatory lending as a defense to a foreclosure, options for a victim of predatory lending, or other issues.
Parent Terms: Mortgages and other financing for a home [HO-09-05-00-00]
Taxonomies: Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-06800], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [68]

Title: Dividing (Partition) a home with another owner
Definition: This category covers options for when there are multiple property owners, how to divide the land or home with the other people. This might be with a sibling, friend, partner, or spouse.  This covers options the person has to go to court for a 'partition' to officially divide their ownership rights and the property with an agreement they all live by.
Parent Terms: Owning a Home [HO-09-00-00-00], Dividing Property and Debt among spouses [FA-06-05-00-00]

Title: Housing after a Disaster
Definition: This category concerns issues a person might have with their housing after a natural disaster or other emergency. It can include issues around owning, clearing title, rebuilding, and insuring a home when you have experienced or at risk of a disaster. It also includes landlord-tenant and eviction issues.
Parent Terms: Housing [HO-00-00-00-00], Disaster Relief [DI-00-00-00-00]

Title: Eviction issues during a public health emergency
Definition: This category concerns issues that renters and landlords may face during a public health emergency, including dealing with special protections like eviction moratoriums, non-enforcement of eviction writs, and delayed rent. It also concerns what issues may happen in the immediate wake of the state of emergency, including options for financial assistance, mediation, special courts, or other programs to address possible displacement.
Parent Terms: Housing after a Disaster [HO-10-00-00-00], Eviction from a home [HO-02-00-00-00], Public Health Emergency issues [DI-08-00-00-00]

Title: FEMA Housing Assistance
Definition: This category covers how to apply for housing assistance from FEMA after a natural disaster. It covers who is eligible, what is needed to prove eligibility, and what kinds of assistance you can get to cover the cost of rent, home repairs, or access to government-provided housing.
Parent Terms: Housing after a Disaster [HO-10-00-00-00], Public Benefits for individuals after a disaster [DI-02-00-00-00], Housing Assistance, Public Housing, and Subsidized Housing [HO-03-00-00-00]

Title: Housing issues after contact with police
Definition: This category is about issues people experience with housing options and rights after they have been in the criminal justice system (like after an arrest, incarceration, or other police encounter).

Title: Zoning issues related to housing
Definition: About questions, regulations, and other concerns about zoning, and what kind of changes or buildings can be made based on zoning rules.

Title: Homelessness and Housing Insecurity
Definition: This category covers issues, rights, protections, and services for people who are experiencing housing instability or homelessness.

Title: Mobile Homes
Definition: This category covers issues with owning or renting a mobile home, or living in a mobile home park.
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1650000], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1650300], Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-00065], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [65]

Title: Owning a mobile home
Definition: This category covers legal issues that a mobile homeowner might have, when their mobile home is in a mobile home park, or on private land.
Parent Terms: Owning a Home [HO-09-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1650100], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1650200]

Title: Renting in a Mobile Home Park
Definition: This category covers rights and options that tenants of a mobile home might have, in a mobile home park. This also includes special rules around eviction or other problems.
Parent Terms: Mobile Homes [HO-14-00-00-00], Renting or leasing a home [HO-06-00-00-00]

Title: Eviction from a mobile home park
Definition: This category covers if and how a person can be evicted from their rented mobile home. This includes the formal requirements of notices and lawsuits, as well as informal evictions through turning off utilities and other illegal behavior.
Parent Terms: Renting in a Mobile Home Park [HO-14-02-00-00], Eviction from a home [HO-02-00-00-00]

Title: Immigration
Definition:
This category covers visas, asylum, green cards, citizenship, migrant work and benefits, and other issues faced by people who are not full citizens in the US.

Scenarios in this category include filling out or filing paperwork relating to U.S. immigration issues and attending any legal actions or proceedings related to U.S. immigration issues.
Taxonomies: Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-08100], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1810000], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1810099], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [81]

Title: Deportation or Removal of immigrants
Definition: This category covers situations in which an immigrant to the United States might be deported or removed, for a criminal situation, or another kind of violation. It also covers waivers and protections against removal, as well as the types of process and immigrant can use to stop the deportation.
Parent Terms: Immigration [IM-00-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1810500], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1810599]

Title: Criminal conviction leading to deportation
Definition: This category covers if and how a criminal conviction can lead to an immigrant's removal from the United States. It covers the process by which a conviction can lead to deportation, and how a person can appeal or stop the deportation.
Parent Terms: Deportation or Removal of immigrants [IM-01-00-00-00]

Title: Stopping deportation through Withholding of Removal
Definition: This category covers protections a person might have against being deported, particularly if their life or freedom would be threatened in the other country, on account of a protected ground, like race, religion, nationality, political opinion, or otherwise. This could be called 'withholding of removal' or 'non-refoulment'. This category covers how a person can try to use this process to stop their deportation or removal, and how the government will make a decision about it.
Parent Terms: Deportation or Removal of immigrants [IM-01-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1810504], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1810850]

Title: Waivers of Inadmissibility, Deportation, or Removal
Definition: This category covers options for an immigrant to get a waiver from deportation or removal proceedings, or from decisions that they are inadmissible to the US. This waiver may provide them exceptions from the usual rules of deportability or inadmissibility
Parent Terms: Deportation or Removal of immigrants [IM-01-00-00-00]

Title: Detention of immigrants
Definition: This category covers detention of immigrants in the United States, including how and when a person can be detained, how they might be released on bond, how they might be paroled, and the process and hearings that surround detention.
Parent Terms: Immigration [IM-00-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1810400], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1810499]

Title: Bond Hearing for a detained immigrant
Definition: This category covers the options for an immigrant who is being held in detention in the United States, to be released from detention through a bond hearing. This includes how to request a bond hearing, how the hearing will proceed, and what possible outcomes will result. It also covers the process of paying the bond and having this amount returned.
Parent Terms: Detention of immigrants [IM-02-00-00-00], Going to immigration interviews and hearings [IM-10-00-00-00]

Title: Parole for immigrants
Definition: This category covers options for parole, for immigrants who are detained in the U.S. This is about how an immigrant can request parole, in order to be able to leave detention for a temporary period while their case is pending in immigration court. It coves who is eligible, what documents and evidence are needed, and what the terms of the parole will be.
Parent Terms: Detention of immigrants [IM-02-00-00-00]

Title: Public Benefits for immigrants
Definition: This category concerns what public benefit programs an immigrant to the US might be able to access. This includes eligibility and procedural requirements for immigrants for programs like food stamps (SNAP benefits), Medicaid, Medicare, disability, old age, SSI, TANF, welfare, and other assistance programs from the government.
Parent Terms: Public Benefits [BE-00-00-00-00], Immigration [IM-00-00-00-00]

Title: Immigrants' access to health care
Definition: This category covers issues that immigrants to the US might have when trying to access health care, including programs that cover the costs of care like Medicaid, Medicare, or CHIP.
Parent Terms: Public Benefits for immigrants [IM-03-00-00-00], Health [HE-00-00-00-00]

Title: Immigrants' eligibility for Medicaid
Definition: This category covers whether an immigrant on a certain visa or status may be eligible for Medicaid benefits to cover health and medical costs.
Parent Terms: Eligibility and applications for Medicaid [BE-03-02-02-00], Immigrants' access to health care [IM-03-04-00-00]

Title: Options for immigration status, visas, permits, and travel papers
Definition: This category covers the various status options that an immigrant to the US might have, to enter or to remain in the US. This can include visas, green cards, permits, papers, and other types of legal status.
Parent Terms: Immigration [IM-00-00-00-00]

Title: Deferred Action immigration status
Definition: This category covers options for an immigrant to get a Deferred Action status, that gives people who are in the US illegally an indefinite delay of their deportation. Deferred Action does not give an immigrant legal status
Parent Terms: Options for immigration status, visas, permits, and travel papers [IM-04-00-00-00]

Title: Legalization of undocumented immigrant
Definition: This category covers options for an undocumented immigrant in the United States to get a legal status that lets them stay legally. This could be for an immigrant who has entered the country illegally, or one who has overstayed another visa. This includes options for Dreamers, or people who are on the Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) program. It also includes asylum, U Visas, and other options for people in special situations.
Parent Terms: Options for immigration status, visas, permits, and travel papers [IM-04-00-00-00], Undocumented immigrants [IM-11-00-00-00]

Title: Political asylum
Definition: This category covers options for an immigrant to apply for political asylum in the United States, including the procedure they must follow, what types of situations are covered, what kind of status are possible as an outcome, and consequences for one's family or a future ability to travel.
Parent Terms: Immigration [IM-00-00-00-00], Legalization of undocumented immigrant [IM-04-02-00-00], Refugees [IM-09-00-00-00]

Title: Immigrants' rights
Definition: This category concerns rights that immigrants to the country may have, including around work, standards of treatment, consular notification, and other protections. It also considers limits on the rights of non-citizens, as compared to citizens.
Parent Terms: Immigration [IM-00-00-00-00], Civil and Human Rights [RI-00-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2320700], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2320799]

Title: Discrimination against Immigrants
Definition: This category covers what rights and protections an immigrant might have if they face discrimination at work, at school, in the business, with the government, or otherwise.
Parent Terms: Immigrants' rights [IM-06-00-00-00]

Title: Sponsoring an immigrant
Definition: This category is about options for an individual, a company, or other groups to sponsor an immigrant to the United States, so that they are able to get legal status. This includes both the categories and the process of being a sponsor. It also includes obligations and rules that sponsors must follow.
Parent Terms: Immigration [IM-00-00-00-00]

Title: Sponsoring an immigrant for a work visa
Definition: This category covers options and procedure for a company or nonprofit that is considering sponsoring a work visa for immigrants to the United States. This covers what different work visas are, the process of being a sponsor, and what obligations and rules the sponsor must follow.
Parent Terms: Sponsoring an immigrant [IM-07-00-00-00], Work as an immigrant [IM-14-00-00-00], Small Business and IP [BU-00-00-00-00]

Title: Border searches
Definition: This category covers problems and rights for a person who is facing a search of their person or their property while crossing a border.
Parent Terms: Immigration [IM-00-00-00-00], Rights against government searches or arrests [RI-13-00-00-00]

Title: Refugees
Definition: This category covers options, services, and outcomes for refugees coming from other countries to the United States. This includes who qualifies to enter the country, what visas or options are open to them, what evidence they must prove to get status, and what ongoing services or pathways are open to refugees. This includes asylum options in the US.
Parent Terms: Immigration [IM-00-00-00-00]

Title: Going to immigration interviews and hearings
Definition: This category is about the process and rights for an immigrant who is going to an administrative hearing, interview, or other kind of official meeting regarding their immigration status and related concerns. It includes their rights to have counsel, how they will be able to participate, what kind of evidence or testimony they my present, and other options and protections they might have. It also includes their obligations and rules about going through this process.
Parent Terms: Immigration [IM-00-00-00-00], Administrative agency requests and hearings [CO-04-00-00-00]

Title: Undocumented immigrants
Definition: This category covers what options and rights a person may have when in the US as an immigrant without legal stauts.
Parent Terms: Immigration [IM-00-00-00-00]

Title: Immigrants working when undocumented or without authorization
Definition: This category covers rights and consequences of an immigrant in the US working, without legal status that allows them to work.
Parent Terms: Undocumented immigrants [IM-11-00-00-00], Work as an immigrant [IM-14-00-00-00]

Title: Immigration options for victims of domestic violence
Definition: This category concerns options that non-citizens in the US might have if they are facing domestic violence or abuse, including immigration pathways and other protections.
Parent Terms: Domestic Violence and Abuse [FA-07-00-00-00], Options for immigration status, visas, permits, and travel papers [IM-04-00-00-00]

Title: Green Card options for victims of domestic abuse
Definition: This category concerns how a spouse or a child of a US citizen might be eligible to apply for Legal Permanent Resident status (LPR, or green card), based on the Violence Against Women Act (VAWA). VAWA also provides that a spouse or child can apply for a 'battered spouse or child waiver' that lets the person with conditional LPR status (often when the marriage is less than 2 years old) -- continue with their LPR status without the other spouse's support. It also includes U-Visa options, with green card options for victims of crimes (including domestic violence).
Parent Terms: Immigration options for victims of domestic violence [IM-12-00-00-00]

Title: Immigration status through U-Visa for crime victims
Definition: This category concerns how a (non-citizen) victim of a crime in the US may be eligible to apply for a U-visa status, that allows a person to stay in the the country legally for up to 4 years (which can be extended), and also apply for lawful permanent residency (green card) after three years on the status. Victims of domestic violence may qualify for U-Visa status, if they have suffered substantial physical or mental abuse that constitutes a crime, and cooperate with the law enforcement regarding this crime.
Parent Terms: Immigration options for victims of domestic violence [IM-12-00-00-00], Being a victim or witness to a crime [CR-01-00-00-00], Legalization of undocumented immigrant [IM-04-02-00-00]

Title: Canceling Removal Proceedings for domestic abuse victims
Definition: This category concerns options for a spouse or child of a US citizen or a US Legal Permanent Resident (green-card holder) -- to end the removal proceedings against them. This involves protections under the Violence Against Women Act (VAWA), that allow the spouse or child who is currently in removal proceedings before an immigration judge, to stop these proceedings and to begin an application for legal permanent residency (green card).
Parent Terms: Immigration options for victims of domestic violence [IM-12-00-00-00], Deportation or Removal of immigrants [IM-01-00-00-00]

Title: Migrant and seasonal worker employment
Definition: This category concerns issues that migrant and seasonal workers (often working in agriculture) face around employment. It includes situations in which people are working on farms or other agricultural settings, getting permission to work in the US, addressing issues around being undocumented, dealing with sexual violence at work, or seeking protection and employment rights.
Parent Terms: Work as an immigrant [IM-14-00-00-00]

Title: Work as an immigrant
Definition: This category covers options, rights, and rules for immigrants in the U.S. who want to work. This includes how to get authorization to work, the visa statuses that allow work, and rules and penalties for violating rules around work.
Parent Terms: Immigration [IM-00-00-00-00], Work and Employment Law [WO-00-00-00-00]

Title: Military Service-members' protection against collection and repossession
Definition: This category concerns protections that a military service-member may have against debt collectors, and from their property from being repossessed  while they are in military service -- and possibly beyond the end-date of active duty. This includes for repossession of vehicles.
Parent Terms: Debt Collection, Repossession, Garnishment [MO-12-01-00-00], Legal protections for military [VE-06-00-00-00]

Title: Money, Debt, and Consumer Issues
Definition:
This category covers issues people face regarding money, insurance, consumer goods and contracts, taxes, and small claims about quality of service.

Scenarios in this category include getting credit because of identity theft, being the target of unfair lending practices or internet scams, problems with debt reduction or credit repair services, problems with terms for repayment of payday lenders, problems related to legal financial obligations, harassment by creditors, problems with pay for or repossession of a car, filing for bankruptcy, garnished wages, and
disconnected utilities due to nonpayment or a billing dispute
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1090000], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1090099], Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-00009], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [09]

Title: Paying for medical care
Definition: This category covers issues that a person might have to pay for their health and medical care, including through insurance programs, dealing with bills, dealing with medical debt, and other concerns.
Parent Terms: Money, Debt, and Consumer Issues [MO-00-00-00-00], Health [HE-00-00-00-00]

Title: Health Insurance
Definition: This category concerns issues a person might have with getting, using, or maintaining health insurance to pay for medical care. This is primarily about private health insurance (not those provided by government).
Parent Terms: Paying for medical care [MO-02-00-00-00], Insurance [MO-07-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1550000], Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-00055], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [55]

Title: Health care coverage through employer
Definition: This category covers workers' rights and protections to get health care coverage through their employer -- like whether employers must provide health insurance, whether dependents would be covered, how COBRA works, and what happens when one is terminated or leaves their job.
Parent Terms: Health Insurance [MO-02-01-00-00], Problems at a Current Job [WO-02-00-00-00]

Title: COBRA health insurance post-employement
Definition: This category covers issues a person might have with employment-based health care coverage after they have left a job or has been terminated -- or when they (or their family members) would otherwise have their health coverage end. This includes who is eligible to receive COBRA insurance coverage, how long it lasts, and what it covers. It also includes how to raise complaints if the employer doesn't offer COBRA coverage.
Parent Terms: Health care coverage through employer [MO-02-01-01-00], Problems regarding a Former Job [WO-03-00-00-00]

Title: COBRA coverage for dependents
Definition: This category covers options for dependents of an employee to get COBRA health insurance coverage, including when the employee dies; the adult child dependent turns 26 or can't stay on the plan; there is a divorce or legal separation; or the employee becomes eligible for Medicare.
Parent Terms: Health care coverage through employer [MO-02-01-01-00]

Title: Free and Low-Cost medical care
Definition: This category covers options and services that provide people with free care, or low-cost care.
Parent Terms: Paying for medical care [MO-02-00-00-00]

Title: Free or low-cost care through Hill-Burton facilities
Definition: This category covers the rules and options to get free or low-cost care through hospitals, nursing homes, or other facilities that are part of the Hill-Burton program. These facilities must notify the public that free or affordable services are available, and then provide services to people who qualify.
Parent Terms: Free and Low-Cost medical care [MO-02-03-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1591000], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1591099], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1591001], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1591002]

Title: Managed Care plans
Definition: This category covers options for a person on a managed care plan, in which a health insurance plan coordinates with providers. This might be through a private provider or a Medicaid program.
Parent Terms: Paying for medical care [MO-02-00-00-00]

Title: Debt collection for medical costs
Definition: This category covers situations in which a person faces debt collection for medical or dental bills, including calls, letters, warnings, and lawsuits.
Parent Terms: Paying for medical care [MO-02-00-00-00], Debt Collection, Repossession, Garnishment [MO-12-01-00-00]

Title: Contracts, Warranties, and Deceptive Trade Practices
Definition: This category concerns issues that consumers and businesses have, including around forming a contract, possible fraud or misrepresentation, payment plans and loans, poor performance, or other problems with the contracting.
Parent Terms: Money, Debt, and Consumer Issues [MO-00-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-00003], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1030100], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1030399], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [03]

Title: Corporate and Commercial Contracts
Definition: This category concerns contracts that are made between businesses or other entities (not personal/individual ones).
Parent Terms: Contracts, Warranties, and Deceptive Trade Practices [MO-03-00-00-00], Small Business and IP [BU-00-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2344444], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2051000]

Title: Arts & Entertainment Contracts
Definition: This category concerns contracts that are made in the arts and entertainment sector.
Parent Terms: Corporate and Commercial Contracts [MO-03-02-00-00]

Title: Consumer Contract issues
Definition: This category concerns problems a consumer might have with a contract they have signed with a business or other entity.
Parent Terms: Contracts, Warranties, and Deceptive Trade Practices [MO-03-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1030302], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1030300], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1030399]

Title: Building Contractors and Construction problems
Definition: This category covers issues that a consumer might have with shoddy construction work, incomplete construction, or other issues with a contractor's work or representations about what work they would do. This could include fraud by the contractor.
Parent Terms: Consumer Contract issues [MO-03-03-00-00], Housing after a Disaster [HO-10-00-00-00], Owning a Home [HO-09-00-00-00]

Title: Consumer Fraud and Misrepresentation
Definition: This category covers issues that a consumer may have after the purchase of a product or service, around possible lies or exaggerations about the purchase, and damages that are caused by it.
Parent Terms: Consumer Contract issues [MO-03-03-00-00]

Title: False advertising, deceptive pricing, and unfair trade
Definition: This category covers consumers' possible protections against unfair and deceptive trade practices, like around when a company may misrepresent what it is selling, what the price is, what guarantees there are, extra fees, or other unfair trade practices.
Parent Terms: Consumer Fraud and Misrepresentation [MO-03-03-02-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1080100], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [08], Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-00008]

Title: Installment Contracts
Definition: This category concerns when a person buys a product or service when the payment or the delivery happens in a series instead of all at once. This might be for cards, land, technology, farming equipment, or retail sales. Issues might be around the contract's details, failure to perform, or enforcing it.
