Parent Terms: Consumer Contract issues [MO-03-03-00-00]

Title: Installment Purchases and Rent-to-Own
Definition: This category covers issues consumers might have when buying things through installment payment plans, around repayment, getting out of debt, credit insurance, or other issues.
Parent Terms: Consumer Contract issues [MO-03-03-00-00]

Title: Warranty issues
Definition: This category concerns problems a consumer might have around a warranty for a product they have purchased. This may be a written warranty a company issues, spoken warranties from a salesperson, service contract warranties, or implied warranties created by state law. This category covers issues with understanding warranty offers, making claims around them, resolving disputes around warranties, or possible lawsuits around enforcing warranties.
Parent Terms: Contracts, Warranties, and Deceptive Trade Practices [MO-03-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1030200], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1030299]

Title: As-Is Warranty issues
Definition: This category concerns problems a consumer might face when buying a product -- like a car or other vehicle -- with an 'as-is' warranty. This includes the seller's obligation to notify the buyer of the 'as is' state, and the legal protections that buyers have after purchasing a thing 'as is', or the protective steps a consumer can take before purchasing the thing 'as is'. Some states have 'lemon laws' for cars purchased 'as is', that guarantee a certain warranty period or for certain problems.
Parent Terms: Warranty issues [MO-03-04-00-00]

Title: Credit practices and Credit reports
Definition: This category is about the problems a person might have with the information on their credit report, as well as opportunities to clean, mask, expunge, and otherwise remove damaging credit information.
Parent Terms: Money, Debt, and Consumer Issues [MO-00-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1040200], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1040299], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1090301]

Title: Building good credit
Definition: This category is about strategies and options a person can use to build credit that can help them access more lending opportunities and other resources.
Parent Terms: Credit practices and Credit reports [MO-04-00-00-00]

Title: Repairing credit
Definition: This category is about how a person can improve their credit and credit report if they have problems they need to address.
Parent Terms: Credit practices and Credit reports [MO-04-00-00-00]

Title: Finding and understanding a credit report
Definition: This category covers how a person can find, understand, and deal with their credit report.
Parent Terms: Credit practices and Credit reports [MO-04-00-00-00]

Title: Accessing credit and borrowing money
Definition: This category covers issues that consumers may have in borrowing money and accessing credit. This could be regarding 'credit invisibles' (consumers who do not have credit records or scores).
Parent Terms: Credit practices and Credit reports [MO-04-00-00-00], Debt and Lending Money [MO-12-00-00-00]

Title: Financial Literacy
Definition: This category concerns resources and options for improving a person's ability to understand their finances, and make choices in their best interest.
Parent Terms: Money, Debt, and Consumer Issues [MO-00-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1090300], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1090399]

Title: Using Bank Accounts
Definition: This category covers issues a person might have in getting and maintaining a bank account. This can be around understanding the options and rules of using banks, and how to maintain a bank account.
Parent Terms: Financial Literacy [MO-05-00-00-00]

Title: Using Checks
Definition: This category covers issues around a person using checks for their finances, including how to write them, how they work, and what might go wrong.
Parent Terms: Financial Literacy [MO-05-00-00-00]

Title: Using Debit Cards
Definition: This category covers how a person can use debit cards for their finances, including how to get a card, what fees and penalties there might be, and how the card transactions and payments work.
Parent Terms: Financial Literacy [MO-05-00-00-00]

Title: Using Credit Cards
Definition: This category covers consumers' issues with getting and using credit cards, or other forms of credit. This includes literacy around how credit works, what consequences there are, and how to maintain and use their credit card.
Parent Terms: Financial Literacy [MO-05-00-00-00]

Title: Identity Theft and Lost Credit Cards
Definition: This category covers the problems related to having one's identity stolen, or losing sensitive financial information, including the loss of credit cards or government documents.
Parent Terms: Money, Debt, and Consumer Issues [MO-00-00-00-00], Birth Certificates and Identity Documents [FA-02-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1090400], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1090499]

Title: Financial Identity Theft
Definition: This category covers problems when a person's information is used by another person to make purchases, get credit cards, rent a home, or get utilities. It also might be for stealing tax refunds, or using checks from the bank account.
Parent Terms: Identity Theft and Lost Credit Cards [MO-06-00-00-00]

Title: Criminal Identity Theft with police
Definition: This issue concerns what a person can do if their identity has been stolen by a person after they have committed a crime, and have presented themselves to the police with a false identity.
Parent Terms: Identity Theft and Lost Credit Cards [MO-06-00-00-00]

Title: Insurance
Definition: This category covers consumers' options and rights when getting insurance to protect themselves against accidents, illness, financial demands, and catastrophes. This includes insurance for health, cars, natural disasters, death, homes, and disability.
Parent Terms: Money, Debt, and Consumer Issues [MO-00-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1030800], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1030899]

Title: Homeowner's Insurance
Definition: This category covers issues that a homeowner might have with insuring their home, including getting covered by an insurance policy, making claims, dealing with scams or frauds, ending coverage, etc.
Parent Terms: Insurance [MO-07-00-00-00], Owning a Home [HO-09-00-00-00]

Title: Renters' Insurance
Definition: This category covers a tenant's options to get rental insurance for their home or property they're renting, how to make claims, how to deal with problems or fraud, and how to end coverage.
Parent Terms: Insurance [MO-07-00-00-00], Renting or leasing a home [HO-06-00-00-00]

Title: Insurance Scams and Fraud
Definition: This category covers options a person might have if they think they may be scammed around an insurance policy, or if they have been accused of insurance fraud. This could be by an insurance company that has deceived the consumer, or if the consumer may be misrepresenting their situation.
Parent Terms: Insurance [MO-07-00-00-00], Consumer Fraud and Misrepresentation [MO-03-03-02-00]

Title: Life Insurance
Definition: This category covers how a person might get, change, use, or end a life insurance policy. It also might cover how a survivor (like a spouse or child) may make claims of the insurance funds after the death.
Parent Terms: Insurance [MO-07-00-00-00], Dealing with another person's estate after they die [ES-02-00-00-00], Making a Will and Estate Plan [ES-01-00-00-00]

Title: Service Members' Group Life Insurance
Definition: This category covers options for veterans and military service members to get covered with group life insurance policies, and how their survivors may make use of them upon death.
Parent Terms: Life Insurance [MO-07-05-00-00], Estate Planning for Military [ES-07-00-00-00]

Title: Loans
Definition: This category covers issues when a person borrows money, including for school or education (financial aid or student loans), payday loans, and installment purchases. It also covers problems like predatory lending, fraud, or default.
Parent Terms: Money, Debt, and Consumer Issues [MO-00-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1060100], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1060199], Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-00006], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [06]

Title: Predatory Lending
Definition: This category covers situations when a person may be targeted with loan offers that are abusive, fraudulent, or discriminatory.
Taxonomies: Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-00005], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1060300], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [05]

Title: Student Loans and Financial Aid
Definition: This category covers issues a person may have when trying to borrow money to pay for school, like around getting financial aid, taking out student loans, paying them back, and dealing with any concerns. This may include how to resolve student loans, understanding aid's conditions, and dealing with possible predatory or fraudulent practices.
Parent Terms: Loans [MO-08-00-00-00], Paying for education [ED-03-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1160100], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1160199], Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-00016], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [16]

Title: Student Loan Discharge or Cancellation
Definition: This category covers when people's loans for education may be discharged (or canceled, so the person doesn't have to pay them back). This includes what situations may result in discharge, like for disability, bankruptcy, closed schools, identity theft, or school fraud.
Parent Terms: Student Loans and Financial Aid [MO-08-02-00-00]

Title: Student Loan Forgiveness
Definition: This category covers a person's options to possibly have their student loans forgiven, including options to do public service or work out a payment plan to lessen the amount of the loan they have to pay back.
Parent Terms: Student Loans and Financial Aid [MO-08-02-00-00]

Title: Student Loan Default and Delinquency
Definition: This category covers what happens if a person defaults, or doesn't pay back, their student loans. This includes the consequences of default, possible defenses and protections a person might use if they don't pay back on time or don't pay it in full.
Parent Terms: Student Loans and Financial Aid [MO-08-02-00-00]

Title: Student Loan Fraud
Definition: This category covers situations when a person feels they may have been scammed by a student loan provider, a school, or by family members around student loans. This includes issues around identity theft, predatory lending, or other fraud.
Parent Terms: Student Loans and Financial Aid [MO-08-02-00-00], Consumer Fraud and Misrepresentation [MO-03-03-02-00]

Title: Applying for Financial Aid (FAFSA)
Definition: This category covers how a person can apply for financial aid for college, like through the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA).
Parent Terms: Student Loans and Financial Aid [MO-08-02-00-00]

Title: Payday loans
Definition: This category covers options when a person is dealing with short-term, payday loans, which are typically smaller loans with very high fees or interest. This might include issues of falling behind on the loan, overdrafting bank accounts, illegal payday loan companies and practices, or other issues.

Title: Understanding the terms of a loan or credit card
Definition: This category covers situations when a person is trying to understand the terms of the loan or credit card a person is considering or has taken out, including what obligations a company has under the Truth in Lending Act, and what a person can do if the terms aren't clearly communicated.
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1060500], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1060599], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1060501]

Title: Canceling (or rescission of) a loan
Definition: This category covers consumers' possible right of rescission to cancel a loan or line of credit. This covers when people have this right, how to use it, and what it gives a person.

Title: Fees and Finance Charges for a loan
Definition: This category covers issues when a person has taken out consumer credit or borrowed money, and is dealing with fees or interest (finance charges) for this borrowing. It includes consumers' rights to know about these charges, how to respond if they seem overly high, or to complain if there has been possible fraud or miscommunication.

Title: High interest rates and Usury protections
Definition: This category covers issues around high-interest rates on loans and consumer credit, and when a person might be protected by laws that set limits on how much interest can be charged.

Title: Taxes
Definition: This category covers taxes, including income, sales, property, and other taxes. It covers the obligations and process of calculating and paying taxes, as well as penalties or how to respond to problems. It also covers Earned Income Tax Credits and other social benefit programs.
Parent Terms: Money, Debt, and Consumer Issues [MO-00-00-00-00], Government Services [GO-00-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1990100], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1990199], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [24], Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-00024]

Title: Income Taxes
Definition: This category covers how a person's income taxes are calculated and paid, to the federal and state government, based on money that they have made from wages, independent contractor work, royalties, interest, and other sources. It also covers what deductions and benefits might reduce the taxes owed.

Title: Getting your taxes done for free (VITA program)
Definition: This category covers how a person can get free help in doing their yearly income taxes, like through the Volunteer Income Tax Assistance, or VITA program.
Parent Terms: Income Taxes [MO-09-01-00-00]

Title: Spouse's Tax Debt and Innocent Spouse Relief
Definition: This category covers options for a person if their spouse owes taxes to the IRS, and they may have an option to protect themselves from this debt. It covers who is eligible to claim  Innocent Spouse relief from an IRS debt, how to claim this protection, and how it may proceed.
Parent Terms: Income Taxes [MO-09-01-00-00], Taxes after divorce [FA-06-03-04-00]

Title: Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC)
Definition: This category covers the Earned Income Tax Credit to give low- to moderate-income people with money through a tax credit. This covers who is eligible for an EITC refund, how it is calculated, how family members and income levels affect it, and how to make a claim for EITC.
Parent Terms: Taxes [MO-09-00-00-00], Food and Cash benefits [BE-02-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1291300], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [23], Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-00024]

Title: Small Claims lawsuits
Definition: This category covers how a person might sue or be sued for a small amount of money. These are called small claim actions, in which the lawsuit covers a small amount of money (usually around $5000 or $10,000 or less), and goes to a special court. It might be for money that one person thinks the other owes them, from a contract, security deposit, accident damages, deceptive business practice, bad check, or land trespass.
Parent Terms: Money, Debt, and Consumer Issues [MO-00-00-00-00], Suing someone, or being sued [TO-04-00-00-00]

Title: Going to Small Claims court
Definition: This category covers how a person can bring a court case through Small Claims Court, or respond to a small claims lawsuit filed against them.
Parent Terms: Small Claims lawsuits [MO-10-00-00-00], Going to court and dealing with procedure [CO-07-00-00-00]

Title: Discrimination against a customer
Definition: This category covers situations in which a customer of a business experiences discrimination, either by owners or employees of the business, or other customers. This covers what rights and protections a person has if they face discrimination, and how to use these rights. It also covers what obligations the owners or employees have to deal with the discrimination.
Parent Terms: Money, Debt, and Consumer Issues [MO-00-00-00-00]

Title: Debt and Lending Money
Definition: This category is about issues people might have with debts they owe (or other family members owe), dealing with debt collectors, going through a repossession or garnishment process, or filing for bankruptcy. It also covers issues with other people owing you debts, after lending money to them.
Parent Terms: Money, Debt, and Consumer Issues [MO-00-00-00-00]

Title: Debt Collection, Repossession, Garnishment
Definition: This category concerns issues around creditors and debt collectors trying to collect on outstanding loans or debts. This includes taking personal property, wages, liens against real property, freezes on a bank account, or other. This category concerns options, rights, strategies, and exemptions for debtors facing collection.
Parent Terms: Debt and Lending Money [MO-12-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-00002], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1020100], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1020199], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [02]

Title: Dealing with Abusive Debt Collection and Harassment
Definition: This category concerns options and rights of people who are facing harassment or abuse by a creditor or debt collector.
Parent Terms: Debt Collection, Repossession, Garnishment [MO-12-01-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1020200], Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-00400], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [04]

Title: Fair Debt Collection Practices Act protections
Definition: This category concerns protections that a person might have from abusive debt collection practices, under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act (FDCPA). This covers protections for credit card debt, auto loans, medical bills, student loans, mortgages, and household debts -- but not business debts. This limits the time and place that debt collectors can contact a person, or ways to stop contact.
Parent Terms: Dealing with Abusive Debt Collection and Harassment [MO-12-01-01-00]

Title: Being a Collection-Proof Debtor
Definition: This category concerns who qualifies to be 'collection-proof', and what they can do to protect themselves. Being collection proof means that a person is protected against personal, family, or household debt -- even if a creditor still can sue them.
Parent Terms: Debt Collection, Repossession, Garnishment [MO-12-01-00-00], Bankruptcy [MO-13-00-00-00]

Title: Debt Management Counseling
Definition: This category concerns counseling and guidance option for someone in debt, in order to deal with debt collection problems.
Parent Terms: Debt Collection, Repossession, Garnishment [MO-12-01-00-00], Bankruptcy [MO-13-00-00-00]

Title: Deficiency Judgment issues
Definition: This category concerns how to deal with a Deficiency Judgment, to pay off the remaining money that a court says a person owes after a foreclosure or repossession. The court judgment will order the person to pay back any remaining money to the creditor.
Parent Terms: Debt Collection, Repossession, Garnishment [MO-12-01-00-00]

Title: Frozen Bank Account issues
Definition: This category concerns options a person has if their bank account has been frozen because of a debt collection.
Parent Terms: Debt Collection, Repossession, Garnishment [MO-12-01-00-00]

Title: Garnishment issues
Definition: This category concerns problems around one's wages (paycheck) or property being garnished to pay for a debt. This includes exemptions a person might have to protect certain things from being garnished.
Parent Terms: Debt Collection, Repossession, Garnishment [MO-12-01-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1020400], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1020499]

Title: Exemptions from Garnishment
Definition: This category concerns how a person can protect their wages or property from a collector, including how to file for an exemption for wages.  Each state has different exemption laws that typically protect some of one's wages (for living costs), social security, disability, retirement, child support, or alimony payments.
Parent Terms: Garnishment issues [MO-12-01-06-00]

Title: Wage Garnishment or Assignment issues
Definition: This category concerns when a creditor has an order to assign or garnish an employee's wages to pay money that is owed. Sometimes this is called 'earnings assignment' or 'earnings withholding'. Employers typically receiving the order to garnish the wages directly.
Parent Terms: Garnishment issues [MO-12-01-06-00], Enforcing a court's judgment [CO-07-05-03-00]

Title: Non-Wage Garnishment issues
Definition: This category concerns issues when a creditor tries to take assets other than wages, through a levy or garnishment process. It includes how to claim an exemption to protect the asset.
Parent Terms: Garnishment issues [MO-12-01-06-00]

Title: Liens on Property
Definition: This category concerns how to deal with a lien taken out against a piece of one's property -- including how to remove it, pay it off, settle it, dispute it, or get it corrected. A lien is a legal claim against a property, that lets a creditor take the property if one doesn't repay a debt. Liens can taken out on homes and cars, or as mechanic's/construction liens or tax liens. They can be taken by debt collectors after a judgment, by filing a lien against the debtors' property.
Parent Terms: Debt Collection, Repossession, Garnishment [MO-12-01-00-00]

Title: Repossession of a car
Definition: This category concerns the repossession of an automobile, in which a lender or leasing company takes a vehicle back after the owner misses a payment.
Parent Terms: Debt Collection, Repossession, Garnishment [MO-12-01-00-00], Liens on Property  [MO-12-01-07-00], Issues with Owning a Car [TR-04-00-00-00]

Title: Being a Defendant in a Debt Collection Lawsuit
Definition: This category covers when a person is sued in court for an alleged debt that they owe. This may be in civil court or small claims court. This category covers issues like the forms, procedural requirements, court rules, options, and settlements that a person may deal with while going through a lawsuit.
Parent Terms: Debt Collection, Repossession, Garnishment [MO-12-01-00-00], Being a Defendant in a lawsuit (being sued) [TO-04-03-00-00]

Title: Personal Property Exemptions from debt collection
Definition: This category covers what personal property a person might protect from a debt collector, including those with a legal judgment from a court.
Parent Terms: Debt Collection, Repossession, Garnishment [MO-12-01-00-00], Exemptions from Garnishment [MO-12-01-06-01], Exemptions to protect property during bankruptcy [MO-13-06-00-00]

Title: Bankruptcy
Definition: This issue deals with a person's options regarding filing for bankruptcy, dealing with the procedure of it, and the possible outcomes of it. It concerns issues about who should file for bankruptcy, including around who might be collection-proof. It includes how to file for different kinds of bankruptcy -- Chapter 7, Chapter 11, Chapter 12, or Chapter 13. It also covers exceptions and exemptions, or stays in a bankruptcy.
Parent Terms: Money, Debt, and Consumer Issues [MO-00-00-00-00], Debt and Lending Money [MO-12-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-00100], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1010000], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1010099], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [01]

Title: Chapter 7 Bankruptcy for people with limited income
Definition: This category concerns the process and consequences of filing for Chapter 7 Bankruptcy, which is an option for individuals whose income is below certain requirements. Chapter 7 bankruptcy liquidates general debts (from credit cards and medical bills) without the need to pay them back. It is typically only available to people with low-income or little/no assets.
Parent Terms: Bankruptcy [MO-13-00-00-00]

Title: Chapter 13 Bankruptcy for people with regular income
Definition: This category concerns the process and issues of filing for a Chapter 13 'reorganization' bankruptcy for individuals, who have regular income and enough money left over each month to pay back some of their debts (as opposed to those eligible for Chapter 7 'liquidation' bankruptcy). Individuals and sole proprietor companies can apply for Chapter 13 bankruptcy if they meet eligibility requirements. It offers benefits but also requires a payment plan for the debts. It may be used by people who have non-dischargeable debts like for alimony or child support, or for people who have fallen behind on house or car payments and want to catch up on payments and keep the property. It can also be used for debt relief, to lower credit card payments, stop a lawsuit, or prevent wage garnishment.
Parent Terms: Bankruptcy [MO-13-00-00-00]

Title: Discharge of Debts in Bankruptcy
Definition: This category concerns the options and process of a bankruptcy discharge, when a court orders relieves a person from their obligation to pay a debt. This typically occurs at the end of a Chapter 7 or Chapter 13 bankruptcy hearing. Once a discharge happens, the creditor is prohibited from trying to collect the debt -- though they still may enforce liens attached to secured debts. Not all debts can be discharged in the different kinds of bankruptcy.
Parent Terms: Bankruptcy [MO-13-00-00-00]

Title: Exemptions to protect property during bankruptcy
Definition: This category concerns options a person might have to claim exemptions during a bankruptcy, which would protect certain property (like home, car, benefits, retirement, licenses, insurance, or tools of trade) from being sold by a trustee during the process. There are federal rules on bankruptcy exemptions, and some states have local exemption systems. This category concerns how to claim certain exemptions, deal with objections to them, and how this determines how much a person will have to pay to creditors.
Parent Terms: Bankruptcy [MO-13-00-00-00]

Title: Automatic Stays on creditors during bankruptcy
Definition: This category concerns the process of how to get and deal with an automatic stay against most creditors, collection agencies, and government entities when filing for bankruptcy. An automatic stay is a temporary federal injunction, that stops collection efforts against the person. The automatic stay does not extinguish debts, but pauses efforts to collect them. This category concerns limits to the automatic stay, how long it lasts, what happens if creditors violate the order, or how a creditor might remove it.
Parent Terms: Bankruptcy [MO-13-00-00-00]

Title: Exceptions to Debt Discharges during Bankruptcy
Definition: This category concerns the exceptions of which debts a person might not be able to discharge when filing for bankruptcy. The rules around exceptions will determine which debts a person must still have to pay back, even after going through a Chapter 7, 11, or 13 bankruptcy. This might be based on when the debts were incurred, what kinds of debts they are, or if the person used fraud or false pretenses when borrowing the money.
Parent Terms: Bankruptcy [MO-13-00-00-00]

Title: Chapter 11 Bankruptcy for businesses
Definition: This category concerns the option and process of filing for Chapter 11 bankruptcy, which is typically used by larger businesses to reorganize themselves. Chapter 11 bankruptcies allow a company to stay active while repaying creditors and restructuring debts.
Parent Terms: Bankruptcy [MO-13-00-00-00], Small Business and IP [BU-00-00-00-00]

Title: Chapter 12 Bankruptcy for farmers or fishermen
Definition: This category concerns the option and process of filing for Chapter 12 bankruptcy, which is typically used by family farmers or family fishermen to restructure their business. It requires the business to make payments to discharge debts.
Parent Terms: Bankruptcy [MO-13-00-00-00], Running a farm business [BU-03-00-00-00]

Title: Door-to-door Sales, Telemarketing, and Spam
Definition: This category covers issues a person may have with a salesperson coming door-to-door trying to sell something, or with telemarketers over phone or text message, or with spam on email. This might include what solicitations are legal, how to opt-out, how to report abuse or fraud, or how to protect oneself against problems.
Parent Terms: Money, Debt, and Consumer Issues [MO-00-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1030400], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1030499]

Title: Telemarketers
Definition: This category covers consumers' rights and options when dealing with telemarketers over phone or text messages.
Parent Terms: Door-to-door Sales, Telemarketing, and Spam [MO-14-00-00-00]

Title: Door-to-Door Sales
Definition: This category covers issues with salespeople who come to homes to sell things, including possible fraud, the ability to stop them from visiting, abuses, and other problems.
Parent Terms: Door-to-door Sales, Telemarketing, and Spam [MO-14-00-00-00]

Title: Spam on Email or Text
Definition: This category concerns a person's problem with receiving spam messages over email or text message, including fraud and scams, how to stop unwanted messages, and other issues.
Parent Terms: Door-to-door Sales, Telemarketing, and Spam [MO-14-00-00-00]

Title: Native American Issues and Tribal Law
Definition: This category covers issues and laws specific to Native Americans and indigenous populations. It includes special legal protections, programs, services, and options that members of Native American tribes may have, as well as the tribal court system, tribal enrollment, and native-based legal services. It also may cover particular problems that are unique to Native American communities.
Taxonomies: Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-09200], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1920000], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1920099], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [92]

Title: Government and lands of Native Americans
Definition: This category covers issues around the territory and jurisdiction of Native American tribes, including their sovereignty, jurisdiction, government set-up, and rights to hunt and fish.
Parent Terms: Native American Issues and Tribal Law [NA-00-00-00-00]

Title: Jurisdiction of Native American tribes
Definition: This category covers issues around what jurisdiction Native American tribal governments and courts might have over legal questions, cases, crimes, and other matters of government and law. This also covers who has jurisdiction on Indian reservations, and what laws apply to Native American tribe members.
Parent Terms: Government and lands of Native Americans [NA-01-00-00-00]

Title: Native American reservations
Definition: This category covers issues around Native American reservations, who can live there, what protections they have, and what happens with the and natural resources there.
Parent Terms: Government and lands of Native Americans [NA-01-00-00-00]

Title: Sovereignty of Native American tribes
Definition: This category covers issues around the rights of Native Americans and Alaska Natives to have tribal sovereignty, in order to govern themselves. This includes rights under the US Constitution to have their own government and powers akin to federal and state governments.
Parent Terms: Government and lands of Native Americans [NA-01-00-00-00]

Title: Treaties and Native Americans
Definition: This category covers what treaties set laws, obligations, and rules for Native American tribes and the US government under the "Indian treaties", including guaranteed protections for education, health care, housing, and other services, as well as the management of natural resources and land.
Parent Terms: Government and lands of Native Americans [NA-01-00-00-00]

Title: Tribal Government
Definition: This category covers what government structures exist for Native Americans and Native Alaskans, how they relate to US federal and state governments, how they establish laws, and how they administer benefits and other services.
Parent Terms: Government and lands of Native Americans [NA-01-00-00-00], Government Services [GO-00-00-00-00]

Title: Native-based legal services
Definition: This category covers legal help, legal aid, and other accessible legal services available to Native Americans and Alaska Natives.
Parent Terms: Native American Issues and Tribal Law [NA-00-00-00-00], Legal Help Resources to deal with legal issues [CO-02-00-00-00]

Title: Family and child support for Native Americans
Definition: This category concerns issues around family law for Native Americans, including around divorce, child custody, child support, and the Indian Child Welfare Act.
Parent Terms: Family [FA-00-00-00-00], Native American Issues and Tribal Law [NA-00-00-00-00]

Title: Divorce for Native American couples
Definition: This category concerns issues around divorce that arise when one or both of the spouses belongs to a Native American Tribe. This includes whether the tribe has jurisdiction over the case, to divide assets,
Parent Terms: Family and child support for Native Americans [NA-03-00-00-00], Divorce, Separation, and Annulment [FA-06-00-00-00]

Title: Native American children's custody by non-parents (Indian Child Welfare Act)
Definition: This category covers the rules and protections of how Native American children's custody may be changed, including under the Indian Child Welfare Act that sets state court rules about child custody. This could be around adoption, foster care placement, termination of parental rights, when a 3rd party (non-parent) files for custody, or other situations when a Native American child is placed outside their home.
Parent Terms: Family and child support for Native Americans [NA-03-00-00-00]

Title: Tribal enrollment
Definition: This category covers how a person may apply and enroll formally in a Native American tribe.
Parent Terms: Native American Issues and Tribal Law [NA-00-00-00-00]

Title: Native American crime victims
Definition: This category concerns particular protections, services, and rights that members of Native American tribes may have when they are victims of crimes. This includes access to Bureau of Indian Affairs victim assistance programs, that is meant to serve victims located in Indian country.
Parent Terms: Native American Issues and Tribal Law [NA-00-00-00-00], Being a victim or witness to a crime [CR-01-00-00-00]

Title: Education issues for Native Americans
Definition: This category covers issues that Native Americans may face when trying to access quality education, and what rights and options they have to address problems in their education.
Parent Terms: Education [ED-00-00-00-00], Native American Issues and Tribal Law [NA-00-00-00-00]

Title: Public Benefits for Native Americans
Definition: This category covers public benefits programs, options, and processes that are unique to members of Native American tribes. This can include benefits around health care, emergency assistance, and other areas.
Parent Terms: Public Benefits [BE-00-00-00-00], Native American Issues and Tribal Law [NA-00-00-00-00]

Title: Tribal TANF
Definition: This category covers options for American Indians and Alaska Natives to receive Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) through a specific benefits program called Tribal TANF. This provides cash aids and supportive services to needy children and families who apply.
Parent Terms: Public Benefits for Native Americans [NA-07-00-00-00], Temporary Assistance for Needy Families benefits (TANF) [BE-02-02-00-00]

Title: Rights and protections for Native Americans
Definition: This category covers situations in which a Native American might face discrimination, or need rights and protections based on their tribal identity.
Parent Terms: Civil and Human Rights [RI-00-00-00-00], Native American Issues and Tribal Law [NA-00-00-00-00]

Title: Native American hunting and fishing rights
Definition: This category covers what special rights that Native Americans have to hunt and fish on their own territory and other places.
Parent Terms: Rights and protections for Native Americans [NA-08-00-00-00], Government and lands of Native Americans [NA-01-00-00-00]

Title: Health Care for Native Americans
Definition: This category covers issues Native Americans might have in accessing and paying for health care.
Parent Terms: Health [HE-00-00-00-00], Native American Issues and Tribal Law [NA-00-00-00-00]

Title: Indian Health Service
Definition: This category covers issues around the Indian Health Service agency, that provides medical help and public health services to Native Americans and Alaska Native people.
Parent Terms: Health Care for Native Americans [NA-09-00-00-00], Public Benefits for Native Americans [NA-07-00-00-00]

Title: Criminal Tribal Courts
Definition: This category concerns how criminal proceedings work in tribal court systems.
Parent Terms: Native American Issues and Tribal Law [NA-00-00-00-00], Crime and Prisons [CR-00-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-00099], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [98]

Title: Civil and Human Rights
Definition: This category covers people's fundamental rights, that the government should protect and others should respect. It applies to situations of discrimination, abuse, due process, the first amendment, indigenous rights, and other key rights.
Taxonomies: Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-00085], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1850099], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1850000], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2320099], Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-00089], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2320000], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [85], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [89]

Title: Discrimination by Government (Equal Protection)
Definition: This category concerns situations in which a person feels that a government body (including at the federal government or state government level) has discriminated against them and caused them harm. This may also be known as an 'equal protection issue', based on the constitutional clause that says the government must treat people equally and fairly.
Parent Terms: Rights when dealing with the government [RI-20-00-00-00]

Title: Right to a free lawyer
Definition: This category covers a person's possible right to counsel (or a lawyer) that they might have for a specific type of legal matter -- like for a criminal charge, an eviction, or other issue.
Parent Terms: Civil and Human Rights [RI-00-00-00-00], Having a free lawyer appointed [CO-09-01-00-00], Having a lawyer in a criminal case [CR-04-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1850800], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2041300]

Title: Disability Rights and Discrimination
Definition: This category concerns situations in which someone feels they have been discriminated against based on their disability, or when they may have a right based on their disability. This includes situations around disability rights in education; protecting your employment rights while you have a disability; rights to service dogs and companion animals; voting access; rights to accommodation under the ADA; and otherwise.
Parent Terms: Civil and Human Rights [RI-00-00-00-00], Discrimination and rights around education [ED-05-00-00-00], Discrimination against a customer [MO-11-00-00-00], Disability issues and rights [HE-01-10-00-00]
Taxonomies: Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-00084], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1840000], Wikidata Taxonomy [Q61890180], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1840300], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [84]

Title: Disability rights around housing
Definition: This category covers what rights a person with a disability may have when it comes to their home, including reasonable accommodation requests they can make from their landlord, defenses they can raise in an eviction, access standards, and dealing with discrimination.
Parent Terms: Disability Rights and Discrimination [RI-03-00-00-00], Renting or leasing a home [HO-06-00-00-00]

Title: Housing rights for people with substance use disorder disability
Definition: This category covers what housing protections and rights a person may have when dealing with a substance use disorder disability. This includes protections if they feel they are being discriminated against or evicted by their landlord because of their disability.
Parent Terms: Disability rights around housing [RI-03-01-00-00], Reasonable Accommodation for a disability defenses against an eviction [HO-02-04-02-00], Housing discrimination based on disability [HO-01-06-00-00]

Title: Assistance animals in rental housing
Definition: This category covers if and how a tenant can have an animal to assist them in their rental home. It covers who qualifies to have an assistance animal, what restrictions there are around what kind of animal, and how to interact with landlords around this right.
Parent Terms: Disability rights around housing [RI-03-01-00-00], Having pets or assistance animals in a rental home [HO-06-13-00-00]

Title: Disability rights under the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA)
Definition: This category concerns what rights the ADA (Americans with Disabilities Act) gives to people, who is covered by it, and what obligations it imposes on businesses and people.
Parent Terms: Disability Rights and Discrimination [RI-03-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1840100], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1840199], Wikidata Taxonomy [Q56659801]

Title: Websites' accessibility requirements
Definition: This category covers what requirements there are for websites to be accessible to people with disabilities, including under the Americans with Disability Act (ADA). It also covers how people can raise complaints about lack of accessibility. It covers which websites must comply with accessibility standards, and what 'reasonable accessibility' means.
Parent Terms: Disability rights under the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) [RI-03-02-00-00]

Title: Reasonable Accommodation standard under ADA
Definition: This category covers issues with interpreting whether a group is compliant with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) or not, and whether they have offered reasonable accommodation to people with disabilities to use their buildings, websites, services, and other offerings.
Parent Terms: Disability rights under the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) [RI-03-02-00-00]

Title: Accessibility rights under ADA
Definition: This category covers what rights the Americans with Disabilities Act gives to people with disabilities, to have facilities, goods, services, and technologies be made accessible to them.
Parent Terms: Disability rights under the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) [RI-03-02-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1840101], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1840103]

Title: ADA Section 508 accessibility for federal government
Definition: This category covers situations when the American with Disabilities Act (ADA) requires that federal government agencies and services -- especially their technology and information tools -- be made accessible to people with disabilities. This includes which agencies this applies to, what it requires of them in development, procurement, and maintenance, and how people can complain about it.
Parent Terms: Disability rights under the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) [RI-03-02-00-00]

Title: Architectural barriers and accessibility under the ADA
Definition: This category covers what requirements physical spaces and buildings must comply with, in order to comply with the accessibility rules of the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). This includes which buildings must be in compliance, what constitutes an architectural barrier, and how people can make complaints.
Parent Terms: Disability rights under the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) [RI-03-02-00-00]

Title: Assistance animals in public
Definition: This category covers if and how a person might be able to bring an assistance animal with them in public places, including restaurants and theaters.
Parent Terms: Disability rights under the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) [RI-03-02-00-00]

Title: HIV/AIDS discrimination
Definition: This category covers what rights people with HIV/AIDS have, to be protected from discrimination or in getting assistance. It also covers privacy protections for people's health information. This could be in situations at work, health care facilities, schools, daycares, pools, gyms, and other places.
Parent Terms: Disability Rights and Discrimination [RI-03-00-00-00], LGBTQ Rights [RI-06-00-00-00], HIV/AIDS care and rights [HE-01-02-00-00]

Title: Disability discrimination in government programs
Definition: This category covers what protections a person with a disability might against discrimination in programs from federal government agencies, groups receiving government assistance, or contractors. This might be under the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 and its prohibition on disability-based discrimination in the federal government.
Parent Terms: Disability Rights and Discrimination [RI-03-00-00-00]

Title: Voting Rights
Definition: This category concerns what rights people have to vote in federal, state, and local elections -- and how to deal with any problems in voting.
Parent Terms: Civil and Human Rights [RI-00-00-00-00], Voting and Elections [GO-03-00-00-00]

Title: First Amendment Rights
Definition: This category covers what rights a person has under the First Amendment of the US Constitution, like to freedom of speech, freedom of religion, freedom of the press, right to assemble, and right to pettion. These rights may arise when a person think that the government is trying to interfere with their religious practices, their speaking or publishing infomration, their assembly or protests, or petitioning the government.
Parent Terms: Civil and Human Rights [RI-00-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1850400], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1850499]

Title: First Amendment protections of freedom of religion
Definition: This category covers situations where a person feels their freedom of religion is being limited by a government agent, or that the government is attempting to establish a national religion. The Constitution's First Amendment prohibits laws that attempt to establish a national religion, or that impede the free exercise of a religion.
Parent Terms: First Amendment Rights [RI-05-00-00-00], Religious Freedoms and Discrimination [RI-17-00-00-00]

Title: First Amendment protections of freedom of association
Definition: This category covers what rights a person has under the First Amendment to associate with others, including to organize around political and social ideas that might challenge the government.
Parent Terms: First Amendment Rights [RI-05-00-00-00]

Title: First Amendment protections of freedom of speech
Definition: This category covers what rights a person has under the First Amendment freedom of speech clause, including to express themselves and protest without the government interfering in this expression.
Parent Terms: First Amendment Rights [RI-05-00-00-00]

Title: LGBTQ Rights
Definition: This category covers what protections and rights that members of the LGBTQ (lesbian, gay, bisexual, and transgender) community may have, based on their sexual orientation and gender identity. This includes protections for same-sex marriage, discrimination, and hate crimes.
Parent Terms: Civil and Human Rights [RI-00-00-00-00]

Title: Human Rights
Definition: This category is about human rights protections, abuses, and claims.
Parent Terms: Civil and Human Rights [RI-00-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2320000], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2320099]

Title: Workers' Rights
Definition: This category covers rights that employees and other works have when it comes to their compensation, harassment, medical or family leave, insurance, safety protections, and other rights they may have. This includes rights for special categories of work or employees, like agricultural work, immigrant workers, undocumented workers, or sex workers.
Parent Terms: Civil and Human Rights [RI-00-00-00-00], Work and Employment Law [WO-00-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1852000], Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-00025], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [25]

Title: Agricultural workers' protections
Definition: This category covers what rights and special protections agricultural (farm) workers have -- especially under the special federal laws like the Migrant and Seasonal Agricultural Worker Protection Act (MSPA). These include obligations that employers have around labor standards and communication, as well as what workers and contractors must do in terms of registering with the US Department of Labor.
Parent Terms: Migrant and seasonal worker employment [IM-13-00-00-00], Workers' Rights [RI-08-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1260100], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [26]

Title: Poultry workers' protections
Definition: This category covers issues and rights for those who work in the poultry industry specifically.
