Title: Racial and ethnic discrimination in agricultural work
Definition: This category covers the discrimination potentially faced by people working in agriculture based on their race or ethnicity, including what protections and rights they have.
Parent Terms: Agricultural workers' protections [RI-08-01-00-00], Racial and Ethnic discrimination at work [WO-08-06-00-00]

Title: Mental Health Rights
Definition: This category covers the rights that a person experiencing mental health issues might have, particularly in situations where there are questions of decisions about medical treatment, or there are situations of discrimination, loss of liberty, or loss of autonomy.
Parent Terms: Civil and Human Rights [RI-00-00-00-00], Mental Health [HE-01-01-00-00], Guardianship or Conservatorship of an Adult [ES-03-02-00-00], Rights and discrimination around health care [HE-02-00-00-00]

Title: Rights to refuse mental health treatment
Definition: This category covers what rights a person has to refuse a possible treatment for mental health issues.
Parent Terms: Mental Health Rights [RI-09-00-00-00]

Title: Right to mental health treatment
Definition: This category covers what rights a person has to get treatment, and other health and medical care for their mental health issues.
Parent Terms: Mental Health Rights [RI-09-00-00-00]

Title: Prisoners' Rights
Definition: This category covers what rights a person might have while they are in a jail or prison.
Parent Terms: Civil and Human Rights [RI-00-00-00-00], Prisoners' rights, services, and conditions [CR-15-00-00-00]

Title: Women's Rights
Definition: This category covers rights and options that women have if they are facing discrimination, harassment, unequal treatment, limits on their health care or reproductive rights, access to benefits, or other issues based on their gender.
Parent Terms: Civil and Human Rights [RI-00-00-00-00]

Title: Privacy Rights and Protections
Definition: This category covers what rights and protections a person has about privacy, including to information about their health, schooling, work, finances, online activity, and other decisions and behavior. This includes constitutional rights to privacy, to be protected from interference by outsiders. It includes options a person might have under different state's laws to protect their personal information or make claims against those people they think have violated their privacy.
Parent Terms: Civil and Human Rights [RI-00-00-00-00]

Title: Rights against government searches or arrests
Definition: This category covers what rights a person might have when dealing with a government agent who is attempting to either search their property, home, or body -- or who is attempting to arrest or detain them. This may be called 'search and seizure' or 4th Amendment issues. This includes issues of what searches and seizures are reasonable, and  which are prohibited.
Parent Terms: Rights when dealing with the government [RI-20-00-00-00], Dealing with police and prosecutors [CR-12-00-00-00], Being investigated for a crime [CR-16-00-00-00]

Title: Right to Travel
Definition: This category covers the Constitutional right to travel, including to cross state borders, without the government interfering.
Parent Terms: Civil and Human Rights [RI-00-00-00-00], Public Health Emergency issues [DI-08-00-00-00]

Title: Sex workers' Rights
Definition: This category covers rights and protections that people in sex work may have, and how they can make use of them.
Parent Terms: Workers' Rights [RI-08-00-00-00]

Title: Human Trafficking rights and protections
Definition: This category covers the rights of people who have been through human trafficking. This includes protection from prosecution and options for visas or immigration statuses.
Parent Terms: Immigration [IM-00-00-00-00], Civil and Human Rights [RI-00-00-00-00], Being a victim or witness to a crime [CR-01-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1860000], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1860099], Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-00086], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [86]

Title: Religious Freedoms and Discrimination
Definition: This category covers protections and rights of people based on their belonging to an organized religious group, or based on their religious or moral beliefs. It covers issues around harassment, discrimination, interference with practicing of religion, reasonable accommodation, dressing and grooming, and other issues.
Parent Terms: Civil and Human Rights [RI-00-00-00-00]

Title: Racial Justice and discrimination
Definition: This category covers rights and options for people facing discrimination, harassment, unequal treatment, and other disproportionate harm based on their race.
Parent Terms: Civil and Human Rights [RI-00-00-00-00]

Title: Age Discrimination
Definition: This category covers situations where a person may have experienced discrimination based on their age. This could be at work, in a consumer context, or by other private or government actors.
Parent Terms: Civil and Human Rights [RI-00-00-00-00]

Title: Rights when dealing with the government
Definition: This category covers what rights a person has when dealing with government agents like police, prosecutors, courts, administrative agencies, prison officials, and others. This includes rights and protections for when someone is under investigation, having to go to court, applying for government benefits, protesting, or other activities that might put them in contact with the government.
Parent Terms: Civil and Human Rights [RI-00-00-00-00]

Title: Language Access rights
Definition: This category covers people's rights to get assistance with English in order to access government services and public programs, including rights to have an interpreter, to have important documents translated into another language, and to register complaints if they don't get equal treatment based on their language.
Parent Terms: Rights when dealing with the government [RI-20-00-00-00]

Title: Accidents and Torts
Definition: This category covers problems that one person has with another person (or animal), like when there is a car accident, a dog bite, bullying or possible harassment, or neighbors treating each other badly.
Taxonomies: Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-00094], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1940000], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1940099], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [94]

Title: Being Physically injured or harmed by another
Definition: This category covers options, rights, and services for a person who has been physically hurt or killed by another person (or entity's) actions. This category covers what they might be able to do to protect themselves, get financial or medical coverage, make themselves whole, and possibly punish the other person.  This might cover scenarios like being injured while getting medical care, interacting with a car, domestic violence, or otherwise.
Parent Terms: Accidents and Torts [TO-00-00-00-00]

Title: Suing a person or business for a personal injury
Definition: This category covers how a person might pursue a personal injury lawsuit against another person or a business if they have been injured. It covers who is able to sue, and what rights and processes they will have when pursuing this lawsuit.
Parent Terms: Being Physically injured or harmed by another [TO-01-00-00-00], Being a Plaintiff in lawsuit (suing someone) [TO-04-02-00-00]

Title: Personal data privacy breach and protections
Definition: This category covers process and options for a person who is concerned that their personal data has been accessed by another person inappropriately, that a company or controller of their data has had a breach that leaked their data, or wants to assert their privacy and data rights.
Parent Terms: Accidents and Torts [TO-00-00-00-00], Medical Records and Privacy [HE-05-00-00-00], Privacy Rights and Protections [RI-12-00-00-00]

Title: Getting Care and Compensation for an injury
Definition: This category covers options that a person has to get care for when they are injured physically, emotionally, or otherwise by another person or entity. This might be around getting medical care to deal with the injuries, insurance coverage to cover the costs, or other kinds of support to help be 'made whole' again.
Parent Terms: Accidents and Torts [TO-00-00-00-00]

Title: Suing someone, or being sued
Definition: This category is about the process and options for a person who either wants to sue another for a harm or injury they have experienced, or who has been sued by another person for an injury. It covers the process of how to initiate a lawsuit, how to respond to it, what rights and obligations both have, and how to deal with the final judgment.
Parent Terms: Accidents and Torts [TO-00-00-00-00], Going to court and dealing with procedure [CO-07-00-00-00]

Title: Car Accident lawsuits
Definition: This category concerns the process of suing someone, or being sued, for injuries around a car accident. It could be injuries to a person's body or to the property. This covers the steps to take in the lawsuit, what kinds of claims are possible, and what resolutions and consequences there might be.
Parent Terms: Suing someone, or being sued [TO-04-00-00-00], Traffic and Cars [TR-00-00-00-00]

Title: Being a Plaintiff in lawsuit (suing someone)
Definition: This category covers the options, process, and obligations of a person who is suing another person or entity, for a harm from an injury that has happened.
Parent Terms: Suing someone, or being sued [TO-04-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1940100], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2024400]

Title: Being a Defendant in a lawsuit (being sued)
Definition: This category covers the options, rights, and obligations of a person who is being sued in court for an injury (or tort) that another person alleges has happened. This includes how the court process will work, how a person can defend themselves, and what consequences they might face.
Parent Terms: Suing someone, or being sued [TO-04-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1940200], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2024400]

Title: Seeking an injunction to compel an action
Definition: This category covers how a person might sue another party for 'injunctive relief', in which they want that party to do certain acts or behave in a certain way. This is one remedy that could be claimed along with money damages.
Parent Terms: Outcomes a plaintiff can seek in a lawsuit [TO-04-06-00-00]

Title: Seeking a preliminary injunction before a trial ends
Definition: This category covers situations when a person may want to get an injunction, or a court order to have the other act in a certain way, before a trial has ended (or even before the case has gone to trial).
Parent Terms: Seeking an injunction to compel an action [TO-04-04-00-00]

Title: Suing to enforce a law (Private right of action)
Definition: This category covers situations when a person might want to enforce a law or legal requirement. They may try to use a private right of action to bring a lawsuit to enforce the law.
Parent Terms: Suing someone, or being sued [TO-04-00-00-00]

Title: Outcomes a plaintiff can seek in a lawsuit
Definition: This category covers what a person can try to get a court order for, in a civil lawsuit against another party. This may be called remedies. It could include money damages, injunctions, or other things for the court to order.
Parent Terms: Suing someone, or being sued [TO-04-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2022300], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2022399]

Title: Suing the government for civil rights violations
Definition: This category covers a person's options to sue the government for possible civil rights violations they have suffered by a government agency or official. This might be called a Section 1983 lawsuit. It might involve lawsuits against the police for the use of excessive force.
Parent Terms: Suing someone, or being sued [TO-04-00-00-00], Dealing with police and prosecutors [CR-12-00-00-00], Rights when dealing with the government [RI-20-00-00-00]

Title: Getting civil rights lawyer's fees paid
Definition: This category covers the possibility that a person could get their civil rights attorney's fees paid for, after they have brought a lawsuit around civil rights violations they have experienced. This could be called Section 1988.
Parent Terms: Suing the government for civil rights violations [TO-04-07-00-00], Lawyer's fees and payments [CO-09-02-00-00]

Title: Harassment by another person
Definition: This category covers the options and rights of a person who is facing harassment by another person (including threatening behavior, stalking, harassing behavior online or in texting, sexual harassment at work or otherwise, or other inappropriate behavior).  This category also covers options and protections if a person is being accused of harassing another person, and what process and consequences they might face, as well as how they might defend themselves. This includes harassment that might be considered under civil laws, or that might cross over to criminal laws. It also covers the difference between domestic violence and harassment (by non-family members, or more distant family members).
Parent Terms: Accidents and Torts [TO-00-00-00-00]

Title: Traffic and Cars
Definition: This category covers problems with traffic and parking tickets, fees, driver's licenses, and other issues experienced with the traffic system. It also concerns issues with car accidents and injuries, cars' quality, repairs, purchases, and other contracts.
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2240000], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2240099]

Title: Car injuries to people or property
Definition: This category is about what options or rights a person has if they have been injured by a car, or if they might have injured another person or property with their car. It could be based on the manufacturer's car vehicle defect or recall, or it could be around another person's driving. It covers what options this person might have, including filing a lawsuit to recover damages for the injury.
Parent Terms: Being Physically injured or harmed by another [TO-01-00-00-00], Traffic and Cars [TR-00-00-00-00]

Title: Dealing with traffic and parking tickets
Definition: This category covers issues a person might have when driving a car, including problems with driving, driving under the influence, or problems with one's license or insurance. This covers responding to tickets and going to court.
Parent Terms: Traffic and Cars [TR-00-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2240200], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [2240299]

Title: Speeding and Moving Violations
Definition: This category covers a person's options if they are facing a ticket for speeding, running a red light, or other problem with their driving.
Parent Terms: Dealing with traffic and parking tickets [TR-02-00-00-00]

Title: License and Registration Traffic Tickets
Definition: This category covers issues a person might have when they have gotten a ticket for issues with their driver's license or registration.
Parent Terms: Dealing with traffic and parking tickets [TR-02-00-00-00]

Title: No Insurance Traffic Tickets
Definition: This category covers issues a person might have if they have a ticket for driving without insurance, or driving without proof of insurance.
Parent Terms: Dealing with traffic and parking tickets [TR-02-00-00-00]

Title: Parking Tickets
Definition: This category covers issues a person might have for a parking ticket, around how their car was parked.
Parent Terms: Dealing with traffic and parking tickets [TR-02-00-00-00]

Title: Driving Under the Influence
Definition: This category covers options and rights for a person who is charged with driving under the influence (DUI), and what consequences they may face.
Parent Terms: Dealing with traffic and parking tickets [TR-02-00-00-00]

Title: Going to Traffic Court
Definition: This category covers how a person can go to traffic court to respond to a ticket, contest it, or see what options are available to resolve it.
Parent Terms: Dealing with traffic and parking tickets [TR-02-00-00-00], Going to court and dealing with procedure [CO-07-00-00-00]

Title: Driver's licenses or permits
Definition: This category concerns how an individual gets and maintains a driver's license or permit, to operate a car, motorcycle, truck, or other motor vehicle.
Parent Terms: Traffic and Cars [TR-00-00-00-00], Licenses for Driving, Business, Fishing, Guns, etc. [GO-01-00-00-00]

Title: Driver's License Suspension
Definition: This category covers how a person might have their driver's license suspended or taken away, how to contest this, and how to deal with the suspension. This could cover suspensions for traffic tickets, or for deteriorating health or ability to drive.
Parent Terms: Driver's licenses or permits [TR-03-00-00-00], Dealing with traffic and parking tickets [TR-02-00-00-00]

Title: Driver's License Suspension for court fines
Definition: This category covers what a person can do if their driver's license is suspended for failure to pay court fines. This includes possible payment plans and other options to reinstate a license.
Parent Terms: Driver's License Suspension [TR-03-01-00-00]

Title: Reinstating a Driver's License
Definition: This category covers how a person can have their driver's license reinstated after
Parent Terms: Driver's licenses or permits [TR-03-00-00-00], Dealing with traffic and parking tickets [TR-02-00-00-00]

Title: Issues with Owning a Car
Definition: This category concerns issues with owning a car, including how to pay for it, getting insurance for it, repairing it, warranties on it, and dealing with possible repossession.
Parent Terms: Traffic and Cars [TR-00-00-00-00], Money, Debt, and Consumer Issues [MO-00-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1090100], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1090199]

Title: Car Payment Issues
Definition: This category concerns problems a person might have with meeting payments for their car or car insurance -- and what options they might have.
Parent Terms: Issues with Owning a Car [TR-04-00-00-00]

Title: Issues with Purchasing and Financing a Car
Definition: This category concerns issues with purchasing a car, including getting financing, reviewing the contract, understanding the loan terms, and having your credit report assessed.
Parent Terms: Issues with Owning a Car [TR-04-00-00-00]

Title: Car Repair issues
Definition: This category concerns issues with having a car repaired, paying for it, refusing to pay, dealing with a mechanic's lien, and protection against unfair or deceptive trade practices for car repair estimates and use of rebuilt parts in the repairs.
Parent Terms: Issues with Owning a Car [TR-04-00-00-00]

Title: Warranties and contracts for a car
Definition: This category concerns problems around 'vehicle warranties' for a car that one has purchased, which a person might have purchased to protect against unexpected or costly repairs or that might come with a manufacturer's warranty. It covers auto service contracts, warranty coverage, disputes around these warranties, how to make a claim, and state/federal lemon laws that relate to vehicle warranties.
Parent Terms: Issues with Owning a Car [TR-04-00-00-00], Consumer Contract issues [MO-03-03-00-00], Warranty issues [MO-03-04-00-00]

Title: Contracts for Car Repairs
Definition: This category concerns problems a person might have when contracting for their car to be repaired.
Parent Terms: Warranties and contracts for a car [TR-04-04-00-00]

Title: Vehicle/Auto License or Registration
Definition: This category concerns the process and options of getting a license or other official registration for a vehicle, like a car, so that it can be legally permitted to be used.
Parent Terms: Issues with Owning a Car [TR-04-00-00-00], Licenses for Driving, Business, Fishing, Guns, etc. [GO-01-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1930100], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1930199]

Title: Car insurance
Definition: This category concerns issues with having insurance for a car one is using, including purchasing it, making claims, getting temporary insurance for a rental, and dealing with the insurance company.
Parent Terms: Traffic and Cars [TR-00-00-00-00], Insurance [MO-07-00-00-00], Issues with Owning a Car [TR-04-00-00-00]

Title: Veterans and Military
Definition:
This category covers issues, laws, and services specific to people who have served in the military.
It could include issues with discharge status, denial of Veterans Administration (VA) benefits, denial of access to service-related medical care, and problems getting an old job back after discharge.

Title: Active Duty Claims
Definition: This category covers how a military servicemember can make claims for compensation or other issues, while they are on active duty. This could be for household goods that have been damaged, lost, or stolen, or for medical issues. This includes how to file a claim, who's eligible for them, and how to appeal or follow through on them.
Parent Terms: Veterans and Military [VE-00-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1771100], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1771199]

Title: Active duty claim for household goods
Definition: This category covers how a military servicemember can make claims for compensation for household goods that have been damaged, lost, or stolen.
Parent Terms: Active Duty Claims [VE-01-00-00-00]

Title: Active duty medical claims
Definition: This category covers how a military servicemember can make claims for compensation for medical issues, while they are on active duty.
Parent Terms: Active Duty Claims [VE-01-00-00-00]

Title: Discharge from military
Definition: This category covers issues of veterans who need assistance with discharge, like getting a Discharge Upgrade or other problems after receiving a less than honorable discharge from military service.
Parent Terms: Veterans and Military [VE-00-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1770200], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1770299]

Title: Administrative Discharge (being fired) from military service
Definition: This category covers situations in which a military servicemember is fired or given an administrative discharge. It includes how a person can dispute or appeal this discharge, or try to change its code or characterization.
Parent Terms: Discharge from military [VE-02-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1770200], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1770299]

Title: Medical Discharge from military
Definition: This category covers what happens if a military service member is discharged from the military as a medical discharge, including with help around discharge upgrades or appeals, and when you may still be able to get to benefits.
Parent Terms: Discharge from military [VE-02-00-00-00]

Title: Applying for Military Discharge Upgrades
Definition: This category covers how a person can apply for an upgrade to their discharge from the military. It covers the options a person has, the forms to apply, and what standards will be used to evaluate the application.
Parent Terms: Discharge from military [VE-02-00-00-00]

Title: Draft into military
Definition: This category covers people's rights and options if they are facing a draft into military service.
Parent Terms: Veterans and Military [VE-00-00-00-00]

Title: Health benefits for military and veterans
Definition: This category covers medical assistance and health benefits available to members of the US military or veterans of it.
Parent Terms: Veterans and Military [VE-00-00-00-00], Health public benefits and medical assistance programs [BE-03-00-00-00], Public Benefits for Veterans and Military [BE-06-00-00-00]

Title: Mental Health for military and veterans
Definition: This category covers issues, services, and rights that military service-members or veterans might have, when they are dealing with mental health issues.
Parent Terms: Veterans and Military [VE-00-00-00-00], Mental Health [HE-01-01-00-00]

Title: Legal protections for military
Definition: This category covers the special protections that members of the military or veterans may have, including if they are facing eviction, foreclosure, debt collection, or other legal processes. This includes protections under the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act (SCRA).
Parent Terms: Veterans and Military [VE-00-00-00-00]

Title: Legal help for military
Definition: This category is about legal help for military and veteran service members, for issues they are experiencing.
Parent Terms: Veterans and Military [VE-00-00-00-00], Legal Help Resources to deal with legal issues [CO-02-00-00-00]

Title: Deployment preparation and issues
Definition: This category covers how a service member can prepare for being deployed, and issues that might arise when being deployed into service.
Parent Terms: Veterans and Military [VE-00-00-00-00]

Title: Work and Employment Law
Definition:
This category covers issues related to working at a job, including discrimination and harassment, worker's compensation, workers rights, unions, getting paid, pensions, being fired, and more.

Scenarios in this category include an employer who did not pay wages or other earned benefits, denial of worker’s compensation, unsafe working conditions, unfair termination, denial of accommodation for disability or a medical condition, denial of unemployment benefits, inadequate treatment of a workplace grievance, and sexual harassment by a supervisor or coworker.
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1290000], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [ 1290099], Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-00029], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [29]

Title: Applying and interviewing for a job
Definition: This category covers issues that might arise while a person is trying to get a job, including rights and discrimination, background checks, criminal records, drug testing, affirmative action, and inappropriate behavior.
Parent Terms: Work and Employment Law [WO-00-00-00-00]

Title: Being drug tested when applying for a job
Definition: This category covers a job applicant's rights and options if a potential employer is asking them to take a drug or alcohol test as part of the application process. This includes options to refuse a drug test, what rights you have if you fail the drug test, and what rules the employer must follow to correctly do drug testing without discrimination or inaccuracies.
Parent Terms: Applying and interviewing for a job [WO-01-00-00-00]

Title: Affirmative Action for employment
Definition: This category covers if and whether affirmative action policies will affect a person who is applying for a job. It covers the rules that might determine if an employer can or should promote job opportunities for specific groups of people, like people of color, women, people with disabilities, or military veterans.
Parent Terms: Applying and interviewing for a job [WO-01-00-00-00]

Title: Problems at a Current Job
Definition: This category is about problems that might arise while working at a job, including around proper payment and benefits, discrimination, inappropriate behavior, health issues and disabilities, immigration, training, and more.
Parent Terms: Work and Employment Law [WO-00-00-00-00]

Title: Being tested for drugs or alcohol at work
Definition: This category covers an employee's rights and options if an employer is asking them to take a drug or alcohol test as part of their job. This includes options to refuse a drug test, what rights you have if you fail the drug test, and what rules the employer must follow to correctly do drug testing without discrimination or inaccuracies. It also includes an employee's ability to challenge a drug test, and when employers are allowed to require a test based on 'reasonable suspicion'.
Parent Terms: Problems at a Current Job [WO-02-00-00-00]

Title: Wage payment, hours, and breaks at work
Definition: This category covers issues an employee may have with how much they are getting paid, if they are getting adequate overtime, if employers are requiring workers to clock out during breaks, if the employer is paying less than the minimum wage, or if there are other claims/problems around the amount paid for the hours worked. This might include topics like 'wage theft', when workers are not being paid what is owed to them.
Parent Terms: Problems at a Current Job [WO-02-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1220100], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1220199], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [22], Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-00022]

Title: Minimum wage at work
Definition: This category covers issues an employee might have if they think an employer is not paying them the required minimum wage in their state or local area. It also covers situations when an employer may pay less than the minimum wage because employees make tips -- with issues around whether this is legal and how to challenge this practice if the employee believes they are not getting paid enough.
Parent Terms: Wage payment, hours, and breaks at work [WO-02-04-00-00]

Title: Being paid a 'prevailing wage'
Definition: This category covers what rights certain kinds of employees have to make a set 'prevailing wage' for workers in their industry and position. This applies particularly when a worker is on a project funded by government money, like a construction project. This category covers if an employer has to pay certain workers a prevailing wage, how a worker can complain about it, and what compensation or other rights they have.
Parent Terms: Wage payment, hours, and breaks at work [WO-02-04-00-00]

Title: Getting paid for overtime work
Definition: This category covers issues that an employee has about getting paid enough for overtime work. This includes what kinds of workers qualify for overtime pay, how much they should get, and what to do if you have not been paid fairly.
Parent Terms: Wage payment, hours, and breaks at work [WO-02-04-00-00]

Title: Meal and Rest Breaks
Definition: This category covers what employees rights are for getting breaks to eat and rest, and whether they will be paid for the time they are on the break. This includes whether employees have to clock out at breaks, if your state requires employers to give rest or lunch breaks, and how much you should be paid for them.
Parent Terms: Wage payment, hours, and breaks at work [WO-02-04-00-00]

Title: Getting paid for trainings and work-related activities
Definition: This category covers issues a worker might have, about whether they should be getting paid for activities related to work, like required training, travel, seminars, waiting periods, on-call periods, sleep time, and other activities that might be involved with employment but not the work that the worker typically does on their job.
Parent Terms: Wage payment, hours, and breaks at work [WO-02-04-00-00]

Title: Getting reimbursed for work-related costs
Definition: This category covers questions about getting paid back by their employer for money they spent on work-related costs, like uniforms, supplies, or other materials.
Parent Terms: Wage payment, hours, and breaks at work [WO-02-04-00-00]

Title: Making a complaint under the Fair Labor Standards Act
Definition: This category covers employees' possible options to raise a complaint against their employer for a violation of how much they are paid, whether they are getting overtime, or other possible violation of the Fair Labor Standards Act. This includes what kind of employee is eligible for protections under this Act, which employers must abide by its rules, and how to raise a claim about a violation.
Parent Terms: Wage payment, hours, and breaks at work [WO-02-04-00-00]

Title: Minors' protections and restrictions at work
Definition: This category covers the legal limits on the employment of minors (people under the age of 18). This includes whether the minors can be employed at all, what jobs are considered too hazardous to have minors employed, what limits on hours or activities there might be, and what extra protections they might have at work.
Parent Terms: Problems at a Current Job [WO-02-00-00-00]

Title: Being an Employee vs. an Independent Contractor
Definition: This category covers questions a worker might have about their relationship with the organization they're working for, including if you have been misclassified as an independent contractor rather than an employee.
Parent Terms: Problems at a Current Job [WO-02-00-00-00]

Title: Being a subcontractor
Definition: This category covers the rights, obligations, and duties of subcontractor workers, who work for 'general contractors' at a job. This includes what obligations the employer and the general contractor have toward them, what tax and contract obligations subcontractors have, and what protections they have regarding wages, breaks, working conditions, termination, and other situations.
Parent Terms: Problems at a Current Job [WO-02-00-00-00]

Title: Taking Time off Work at Current Job
Definition: About taking time off from a current job because of illness, adoption, bereavement, religious reasons, military service, disability treatment, domestic violence, or other reasons
Parent Terms: Problems at a Current Job [WO-02-00-00-00]

Title: Taking leave for family and medical reasons
Definition: This category covers employees' options for taking family and medical Leave (especially under the Family and Medical Leave Act), including for giving birth, caring for a child, caring for another family member, dealing with an illness or other issues. This category covers questions about which employees are eligible for taking leave, if they will be paid, if they can be fired, how to get approved for leave, and what happens if you think your employer has violated their obligations.
Parent Terms: Taking Time off Work at Current Job [WO-02-14-00-00], Taking Care of Sick or Disabled Family [FA-16-00-00-00]

Title: Reasonable accommodation for a disability at work
Definition: This category covers how a person might request a reasonable accommodation for a disability at their job, what their rights are, what employers are required to do, and how to deal with issues with the request.
Parent Terms: Problems at a Current Job [WO-02-00-00-00], Disability discrimination at work [WO-08-04-00-00]

Title: Substance use disorder disability accommodation at work
Definition: This category covers what rights and options a person might have at their workplace, when they are dealing with a substance use disorder that qualifies as a disability. It includes what kinds of questions a prospective or current employer might ask, what accommodation they must give, and how to deal with possible discrimination because of their disorder.
Parent Terms: Being drug tested when applying for a job [WO-01-02-00-00], Being tested for drugs or alcohol at work [WO-02-03-00-00], Reasonable accommodation for a disability at work [WO-02-15-00-00], Alcoholism and Substance Abuse [HE-01-04-00-00]

Title: Problems regarding a Former Job
Definition: This category is about the period after leaving a job, including being fired or quitting, severance agreements, non-compete contracts, references, personnel files, getting back pay, and harassment.
Parent Terms: Work and Employment Law [WO-00-00-00-00]

Title: Being fired after whistleblowing
Definition: This category covers options and rights for a person who has been terminated from their job after being a whistleblower regarding illegal activity by their employer. This includes when whistleblowers have protections against termination, retaliation, or ability to make claims to be compensated for being fired.
Parent Terms: Being fired from a job [WO-03-02-00-00]

Title: Being fired from a job
Definition: This category covers issues a person might have after they have been terminated from their job. It includes the possibility to raise a 'wrongful termination' claim, when employers are allowed to let a worker go, what reasons are acceptable for it, and what a worker can do if they think they have been fired illegally or in a way that is against public policy (like for retaliation or discrimination).
Parent Terms: Problems regarding a Former Job [WO-03-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1291500], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1291599]

Title: Wrongful termination of employees who are not 'at will'
Definition: This category covers employees who are not the usual 'at will' employees (who can be fired at any time), who can raise a claim if they are fired. This might be based on public policy, anti-discrimination, implied contracts of good faith and fair dealing, or other protections that an employer has against termination.
Parent Terms: Being fired from a job [WO-03-02-00-00]

Title: Employment records from former job
Definition: This category covers how a person might request their personnel file from a former employer, how other possible employers might request your past employment records, and deal with other issues about what a previous employer says or releases about your work history.
Parent Terms: Problems regarding a Former Job [WO-03-00-00-00]

Title: Retirement and Pensions
Definition: This category is about getting payments and benefits after retiring from a job or at the end of a career. This includes around eligibility for benefits, proper management of benefit plans under ERISA, vesting of benefits, managers of benefits, and railroad retirement.
Parent Terms: Work and Employment Law [WO-00-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1250200], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1250299]

Title: Mismanagement of retirement and pension plans (under ERISA)
Definition: This category covers what employees can do if they believe that their employer has violated their obligations to properly manage retirement, pension, and profit-sharing plans under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act (ERISA). This includes obligations to provide benefits to current or former employees, to maintain their fiduciary duties toward the employees, and to protect their rights.
Parent Terms: Retirement and Pensions [WO-04-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1250300], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1250220]

Title: Eligibility for pension plan or retirement benefits
Definition: This category covers questions around whether a person is eligible to join a pension plan or get retirement benefits through their work.
Parent Terms: Retirement and Pensions [WO-04-00-00-00]

Title: Vesting of retirement plan
Definition: This category covers issues around when an employee's retirement plans vest, meaning that they have ownership over the account balance that the employer cannot take away. This includes rules around losing retirement benefits if a person leaves the job or works less than a certain number of hours. It also includes rules around when there must e 100% vesting.
Parent Terms: Retirement and Pensions [WO-04-00-00-00]

Title: Railroad workers' retirement system
Definition: This category covers issues around railroad retirement benefits. This is typically eligible to railroad workers and their families through the federal agency Railroad Retirement Board. This category covers eligibility, overpayments, benefit appeals, and other resources.
Parent Terms: Retirement and Pensions [WO-04-00-00-00]

Title: Unions
Definition: This category is about forming unions, joining them, rights as a union member, dealing with possible problems, and opting out of a union.
Parent Terms: Work and Employment Law [WO-00-00-00-00]

Title: Employer interfering with union activity (Unfair Labor Practices)
Definition: This category covers protections and issues for employees who are facing interference by their employer, when trying to organize, join, or assist a union. It also covers what kinds of employee activities are protected as concerted activities, like conversations, posting on social media, or collective bargaining. This is in part defined by the National Labor Relations Act, and other labor laws, that lay out protections for employees and unions.

Title: Unfair Labor Practices by Unions
Definition: This category covers restrictions on what unions can do at a workplace, under laws around unfair labor practices. This includes situations when unions may be restraining or coercing employees regarding their choice not to support a union, crossing a picket line, restraining an employer's choice of bargaining representative, causing employers to penalize employees who engage in anti-union activities, or charging excessive fees. This category covers how an employee might make a complaint to the NLRB about these practices, and what rights they have.

Title: Volunteering or interning at a job
Definition: About rights and duties of people who are interning or volunteering at a job.
Parent Terms: Work and Employment Law [WO-00-00-00-00]

Title: Being injured on the job
Definition: This category is about options that a person has after there has been health or physical injuries that happen while on the job. It includes how to report it, how to get workers compensation coverage for it, and what other protections and options the employee has. It also includes if an existing medical condition is made worse by workplace conditions. This category also covers if a person is able to sue their employer for their injury, or what they might do if the employer retaliates or discriminates against them after the injury.
Parent Terms: Work and Employment Law [WO-00-00-00-00], Problems at a Current Job [WO-02-00-00-00]

Title: Getting Worker's Compensation benefits
Definition: This category covers if and how an employee can get Worker's Compensation benefits. The laws vary state to state, but generally workers who are injured on the job or have a sickness or disability that is made worse by workplace conditions can access workers' compensation to help them cover their costs. This also covers whether Worker's Compensation programs stop an employee from being able to sue their employer for their injury.
Parent Terms: Being injured on the job [WO-07-00-00-00]

Title: Working conditions that are unsafe or unhealthy
Definition: This category covers an employee's options if they are working in a place that seems to have health or safety hazards. This could be for dangerous machines, toxic chemicals, or poor training. This category includes the ability to file complaints with the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), to get the workplace inspected and improved. It also covers what happens if an employee faces retaliation for making a complaint.
Parent Terms: Being injured on the job [WO-07-00-00-00]

Title: Discrimination around work and employment
Definition: This category is about possible discrimination around employment, based on disability, ethnicity, gender, marital status, race, religion, sexual harassment, sexual orientation, or age. It also includes what remedies an employee might be eligible to receive, if they have been discriminated against.
Parent Terms: Work and Employment Law [WO-00-00-00-00], Civil and Human Rights [RI-00-00-00-00], Workers' Rights [RI-08-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1210500], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1210599], Legal Server Index Taxonomy [LS002-00021], Legal Services Corporation Taxonomy [21]

Title: Remedies for discrimination at work
Definition: This category covers what an employee (or potential employee) might be eligible to receive if they have faced discrimination in their employment. This includes options to get back pay, compensatory damages, or punitive damages for the discrimination they have faced.
Parent Terms: Discrimination around work and employment [WO-08-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1210600], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1210699]

Title: Getting Back-Pay after discrimination at work
Definition: This category covers whether and how an employee can get back-pay after they have faced discrimination at work. This would be for the salary or other payments they would have received, had they not gone through the discrimination.
Parent Terms: Remedies for discrimination at work [WO-08-01-00-00]

Title: Getting Compensated after discrimination at work
Definition: This category covers an employee's options to get paid for compensatory damages for the discrimination they have experienced at work. Compensatory damages cover the costs the person has had to pay out-of-pocket because of the discrimination. This might include job search costs, medical expenses, emotional harms, inconvenience, mental anguish, or loss of enjoyment of life.
Parent Terms: Remedies for discrimination at work [WO-08-01-00-00], Claiming Money (Damages) in a lawsuit [CO-07-07-00-00]

Title: Punitive damages for work discrimination
Definition: This category covers if and how an employee can get punitive damages against an employer for discrimination. Punitive damages are generally possible if the employer's discrimination was especially malicious or reckless. This category covers how much money a person could get, what limits there are on this money, and when punitive damages might be possible.
Parent Terms: Remedies for discrimination at work [WO-08-01-00-00], Claiming Money (Damages) in a lawsuit [CO-07-07-00-00]

Title: Sexual harassment at work
Definition: This category covers situations when a person is facing sexual harassment at work or an interview for employment, including propositions, jokes, touching, and other physical or verbal conduct that is sexual in nature. This category includes the standards of what constitutes sexual harassment, how to make complaints, what workers' or applicants' rights are, and steps they can take to protect themselves.
Parent Terms: Discrimination around work and employment [WO-08-00-00-00], Harassment by another person [TO-05-00-00-00]

Title: Age discrimination at work
Definition: This category covers options and rights for a person who may be facing inappropriate treatment at work (or potential work) based on their age. This includes around their hiring, firing, pay, job assignments, promotions, or comments and insults. The category covers what the standards for discrimination are, and what a person can do to protect themselves.
Parent Terms: Discrimination around work and employment [WO-08-00-00-00], Age Discrimination [RI-19-00-00-00]

Title: Disability discrimination at work
Definition: This category covers options and rights for a person who may be facing inappropriate treatment at work (or potential work) based on their disability. This includes around their hiring, firing, pay, job assignments, promotions, or comments and insults. The category covers what the standards for discrimination are, and what a person can do to protect themselves.
Parent Terms: Discrimination around work and employment [WO-08-00-00-00], Disability Rights and Discrimination [RI-03-00-00-00]

Title: Gender discrimination at work
Definition: This category covers options and rights for a person who may be facing inappropriate treatment at work (or potential work) based on their gender. This includes around their hiring, firing, pay, job assignments, promotions, or comments and insults. The category covers what the standards for discrimination are, and what a person can do to protect themselves.
Parent Terms: Discrimination around work and employment [WO-08-00-00-00], Women's Rights [RI-11-00-00-00]

Title: Racial and Ethnic discrimination at work
Definition: This category covers options and rights for a person who may be facing inappropriate treatment at work (or potential work) based on their race, ethnicity, or country of origin. This includes around their hiring, firing, pay, job assignments, promotions, or comments and insults. The category covers what the standards for discrimination are, and what a person can do to protect themselves.
Parent Terms: Discrimination around work and employment [WO-08-00-00-00], Immigrants' rights [IM-06-00-00-00], Racial Justice and discrimination [RI-18-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1210502], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1210501]

Title: Religious discrimination at work
Definition: This category covers options and rights for a person who may be facing inappropriate treatment at work (or potential work) based on their religion. This includes around their hiring, firing, pay, job assignments, promotions, or comments and insults. The category covers what the standards for discrimination are, and what a person can do to protect themselves.
Parent Terms: Discrimination around work and employment [WO-08-00-00-00], Religious Freedoms and Discrimination [RI-17-00-00-00]

Title: Sexual orientation or Gender Identity discrimination at work
Definition: This category covers options and rights for a person who may be facing inappropriate treatment at work (or potential work) based on their sexual orientation (real or perceived) or their gender identity. This includes around their hiring, firing, pay, job assignments, promotions, or comments and insults. The category covers what the standards for discrimination are, and what a person can do to protect themselves.
Parent Terms: LGBTQ Rights [RI-06-00-00-00], Discrimination around work and employment [WO-08-00-00-00]

Title: Martial or Parental Status discrimination at work
Definition: This category covers options and rights for a person who may be facing inappropriate treatment at work (or potential work) based on their family status -- like around having children, being married, single, divorced, widowed, or head of household. This includes around their hiring, firing, pay, job assignments, promotions, or comments and insults. The category covers what the standards for discrimination are, and what a person can do to protect themselves.
Parent Terms: Discrimination around work and employment [WO-08-00-00-00], Women's Rights [RI-11-00-00-00]

Title: Proving discrimination at work
Definition: This category covers the legal standards and types of behavior that apply when a worker is bringing a complaint of discrimination against an employer.
Parent Terms: Discrimination around work and employment [WO-08-00-00-00]

Title: Discrimination based on a 'bona fide occupational qualification'
Definition: This category covers when an employer might have a legitimate reason to discriminate against workers or applicants, based on a 'bona fide occupational qualification' that is related to the work. (This does not usually allow them to discriminate based on race). Often employers use this standard to defend themselves, to say that they had to discriminate based on safety or other important concerns.
Parent Terms: Proving discrimination at work [WO-08-10-00-00]

Title: Neutral work policies that lead to discrimination (disparate impact)
Definition: This category covers situations when an employer has a policy that seems neutral on its face (like a certain test, requirement, or procedure) that leads to discrimination against workers of a certain race, gender, age, religion, or another protected demographic group. This category covers what someone needs to show to prove 'disparate impact' discrimination, and how employers can defend themselves.
Parent Terms: Proving discrimination at work [WO-08-10-00-00]

Title: Employment in prison
Definition: This category is about opportunities to work while in a prison. It also concerns rights, payments, and other concerns of people who are employed while in prison. This could be about work programs and work release programs.
Parent Terms: Work and Employment Law [WO-00-00-00-00], Prisoners' rights, services, and conditions [CR-15-00-00-00]

Title: Veterans and Military members' Civilian Work
Definition: This category is about rights and remedies when a person returns to civilian work after serving in the military, including dealing with problems with pay, promotions, and seniority that can be addressed through USSERA.
Parent Terms: Work and Employment Law [WO-00-00-00-00], Veterans and Military [VE-00-00-00-00]

Title: Uniform Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act for servicemembers
Definition: This category covers military servicemembers' and veterans' rights under the Uniform Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act (USERRA). This includes obligations for employers to put servicemembers back in their civilian jobs after military service. It also is about how they can seek employment without discrimination based on their military service.
Parent Terms: Veterans and Military members' Civilian Work [WO-10-00-00-00], Discrimination around work and employment [WO-08-00-00-00]
Taxonomies: NSMI v1 Taxonomy [ 1770800], NSMI v1 Taxonomy [1770899]

Title: Reemployment after military service
Definition: This category covers military servicemembers' and veterans' reentry into the civilian workforce, and their rights around reemployment.
Parent Terms: Veterans and Military members' Civilian Work [WO-10-00-00-00]

Title: Suing an employer for a tort
Definition: This category covers options for a person to sue an employer while working there or after leaving their job. It might be for tort claims for negligence around a safe workplace, fraud (when an employer deceives them), defamation (when an employer lies about them), false imprisonment (for not allowing them to leave), or for assault and battery (for allowing them to be injured on the job).
Parent Terms: Suing someone, or being sued [TO-04-00-00-00], Work and Employment Law [WO-00-00-00-00]
